meta.blurb_uz: Savdo agenti Gregor Samsa bir kuni ertalab ulkan hasharotga aylanib uyg'onadi. U oilasini boqib kelgan, endi esa ularga yukka aylanadi. Kafka bu g'ayrioddiy voqeani oddiy, deyarli kundalik ohangda hikoya qiladi — va shu bilan begonalashuv, burch va oila mehrining chegarasi haqida XX asrning eng kuchli asarlaridan birini yaratadi.
meta.why_uz: Qisqa (uch qism), lekin cheksiz talqin qilinadigan asar. Ingliz tilini o'rganuvchi uchun — boy, lekin tushunarli til: kundalik so'zlar, oilaviy dialoglar, his-tuyg'ular tasviri. Har bob 15–20 daqiqada o'qiladi.
meta.author_uz: Frans Kafka (1883–1924) — Pragada tug'ilgan, nemis tilida yozgan yozuvchi. Kunduzi sug'urta idorasida ishlab, kechalari yozgan. Hayotligida kam tanilgan, vafotidan keyin XX asrning eng ta'sirli yozuvchilaridan biriga aylangan. «Kafkaona» so'zi absurd, qo'rqinchli byurokratik vaziyatni anglatadi.
meta.edition_uz: To'liq matn. Asar 1915-yilda chiqqan, Kafka 1924-yilda vafot etgan — asar jamoat mulki. Inglizcha matn — WordDrop'ning nemischa asl nusxadan (Kurt Wolff nashri, 1917) qilgan yangi tarjimasi; o'zbekcha parallel tarjima ham WordDrop'niki. O'qish qulay bo'lishi uchun Kafkaning juda uzun xatboshilari ba'zan bir nechta qismga bo'lingan, matn qisqartirilmagan.

Ish va burch — Gregor ishning quli edi; uning qadri faqat pul topishi bilan o'lchangan.
Oila — mehr qachon tugaydi? Oila Gregorga «toqat qiladi», keyin undan qutulishni istaydi.

chapters.title: One Morning
chapters.recap_uz: Gregor Samsa bir kuni ertalab ulkan hasharotga aylanib uyg'onadi. U buni tushdek qabul qiladi va ko'proq ishga kechikayotgani haqida qayg'uradi. Oilasi eshikni taqillatadi, u esa karavotdan tusha olmay qiynaladi.

paras.en: One morning, as Gregor Samsa was waking up from troubled dreams, he found himself changed in his bed into a monstrous insect. He was lying on his back, which was as hard as armour, and when he lifted his head a little, he could see his brown, curved belly, divided into stiff arching segments. The blanket was barely staying on top of it and was ready to slide off completely. His many legs, pitifully thin compared with the rest of his body, waved helplessly before his eyes.
paras.uz: Bir kuni ertalab Gregor Samsa notinch tushlardan uyg'onar ekan, o'zini karavotida dahshatli hasharotga aylangan holda ko'rdi. U sovutday qattiq orqasi bilan chalqancha yotardi va boshini sal ko'targanida qavariq, jigarrang, yoysimon qattiq bo'g'imlarga bo'lingan qornini ko'rdi. Ko'rpa qorin ustida arang turar, butunlay sirg'alib tushishga tayyor edi. Tanasining qolgan qismiga nisbatan achinarli darajada ingichka ko'plab oyoqlari ko'zi oldida nochor qimirlardi.

paras.en: “What has happened to me?” he thought. It was not a dream. His room, a proper human room, only a little too small, lay quietly between the four familiar walls. Above the table, where a collection of cloth samples lay unpacked and spread out — Samsa was a travelling salesman — hung the picture that he had recently cut out of an illustrated magazine and put into a pretty gilded frame. It showed a lady in a fur hat and a fur stole, sitting upright and holding out towards the viewer a heavy fur muff into which her whole forearm had disappeared.
paras.uz: «Menga nima bo'ldi?» — deb o'yladi u. Bu tush emas edi. Uning xonasi — haqiqiy, faqat sal torroq odam xonasi — tanish to'rt devor orasida tinchgina turardi. Ustida gazlama namunalari ochib yoyib qo'yilgan stol tepasida (Samsa savdo agenti — sayyor sotuvchi edi) yaqinda u rasmli jurnaldan qirqib olib, chiroyli zarhal ramkaga solgan surat osilib turardi. Suratda mo'yna shlyapa kiygan, bo'yniga mo'yna boa o'ragan bir xonim tik o'tirib, butun bilagi ichiga kirib ketgan og'ir mo'yna muftani tomoshabin tomon ko'tarib turardi.

paras.en: Gregor's eyes then turned to the window, and the gloomy weather — he could hear raindrops hitting the metal windowsill — made him quite melancholy. “What if I went on sleeping a little longer and forgot all this nonsense?” he thought. But that was completely impossible, because he was used to sleeping on his right side, and in his present state he could not get into that position. However hard he threw himself onto his right side, he always rocked back onto his back. He must have tried a hundred times, closing his eyes so that he would not have to see his wriggling legs, and he only stopped when he began to feel a light, dull pain in his side that he had never felt before.
paras.uz: Keyin Gregorning nigohi derazaga tushdi va xira havo — deraza tunukasiga urilayotgan yomg'ir tomchilari eshitilardi — uni butunlay g'amgin qilib qo'ydi. «Yana bir oz uxlab, bu bema'niliklarning hammasini unutsam-chi?» — deb o'yladi u. Lekin buning iloji yo'q edi: u o'ng yonboshi bilan uxlashga o'rgangan, hozirgi holatida esa bu holatga o'ta olmasdi. O'zini o'ng tomonga qanchalik kuch bilan otmasin, har gal yana chalqancha holatga qaytib tebranardi. U buni yuz martacha urinib ko'rdi, tipirchilayotgan oyoqlarini ko'rmaslik uchun ko'zlarini yumdi va yonboshida ilgari hech qachon sezmagan yengil, simillagan og'riq paydo bo'lgandagina to'xtadi.

paras.en: “Oh God,” he thought, “what an exhausting job I have chosen! Travelling day in, day out. The stress of business is much greater on the road than in the actual office at home, and on top of that I have the torment of travelling: worrying about train connections, bad food at irregular times, and contact with people that always changes, never lasts and never becomes warm. The devil take it all!”
paras.uz: «Yo Xudo, — deb o'yladi u, — qanday mashaqqatli kasbni tanlabman-a! Kun-u tun safarda. Yo'ldagi ish tashvishlari uydagi idorada ishlashdan ancha ko'p, buning ustiga safarning azobi ham bor: poyezdlarga ulgurish tashvishi, vaqtida yemaydigan yomon ovqat, doim almashib turadigan, hech qachon davom etmaydigan va hech qachon samimiylashmaydigan odamlar bilan muloqot. Hammasini shayton olsin!»

paras.en: He felt a slight itch on the upper part of his belly. Slowly he pushed himself on his back closer to the bedpost so that he could lift his head better. He found the itchy place, which was covered with lots of little white spots that he could not make sense of. He wanted to touch the spot with one of his legs, but he drew it back at once, because when he touched it a cold shiver ran through him.
paras.uz: U qornining yuqori qismida yengil qichishishni sezdi. Boshini yaxshiroq ko'tarish uchun chalqancha holda asta karavot ustuniga yaqinroq surildi. Qichiyotgan joyni topdi: u yerda nima ekanini tushunolmagan juda ko'p mayda oq dog'lar bor edi. Bir oyog'i bilan o'sha joyni paypaslab ko'rmoqchi bo'ldi, lekin darhol tortib oldi, chunki tegishi bilan butun badanidan sovuq titroq o'tdi.

paras.en: He slid back into his earlier position. “This getting up early,” he thought, “makes a man completely stupid. A person needs his sleep. Other salesmen live like women in a harem. For example, when I go back to the hotel during the morning to write up the orders I've got, these gentlemen are only just sitting down to breakfast. I should try that with my boss; I'd be thrown out on the spot. Who knows, though, maybe that would be very good for me.
paras.uz: U yana avvalgi holatiga sirg'alib tushdi. «Bunday erta turish, — deb o'yladi u, — odamni butunlay ahmoq qilib qo'yadi. Inson uxlashi kerak. Boshqa agentlar haramdagi ayollardek yashaydi. Masalan, men tushgacha olgan buyurtmalarimni yozib qo'yish uchun mehmonxonaga qaytsam, bu janoblar endigina nonushtaga o'tirgan bo'ladi. Shuni xo'jayinim oldida bir qilib ko'rsam edi — o'sha zahoti haydab yuborardi. Kim biladi, balki bu men uchun juda yaxshi bo'lardi.

paras.en: If I didn't hold back because of my parents, I would have handed in my notice long ago. I would have gone up to the boss and told him exactly what I think, from the bottom of my heart. He would have fallen off his desk! It's a strange habit, too, sitting up on the desk and talking down to the employee from up there — and the employee has to come right up close because the boss is hard of hearing. Well, I haven't given up hope completely. Once I've got the money together to pay off my parents' debt to him — it should take another five or six years — I'll definitely do it. Then I'll make a clean break. For now, though, I have to get up, because my train leaves at five.”
paras.uz: Agar ota-onam sababli o'zimni tutmaganimda, allaqachon ishdan ketgan bo'lardim. Xo'jayin oldiga borib, unga dilimdagi barcha gaplarni aytgan bo'lardim. U stolidan yiqilib tushardi! Stol ustiga chiqib o'tirib, xodim bilan yuqoridan gaplashish ham g'alati odat — buning ustiga xo'jayin qulog'i og'ir bo'lgani uchun xodim unga juda yaqin borishi kerak. Mayli, umid hali butunlay so'nmagan. Ota-onamning unga bo'lgan qarzini to'lash uchun pul yig'ib olsam — buning uchun yana besh-olti yil kerak bo'lsa kerak — albatta shunday qilaman. Shunda hammasini bir yo'la uzaman. Hozircha esa turishim kerak, chunki poyezdim beshda jo'naydi.»

paras.en: And he looked over at the alarm clock ticking on the chest of drawers. “Heavenly Father!” he thought. It was half past six, and the hands were calmly moving on; it was even later than half past, it was nearly a quarter to seven. Had the alarm not gone off? He could see from the bed that it was correctly set for four o'clock; it must have rung. Yes, but was it possible to sleep peacefully through that noise, which shook the furniture? Well, he had not slept peacefully, but probably all the more deeply. But what was he supposed to do now? The next train left at seven; to catch it he would have to rush like a madman, the samples were not packed yet, and he himself did not feel especially fresh or lively.
paras.uz: U javon ustida chiqillab turgan budilnikka qaradi. «Ey Parvardigor!» — deb o'yladi u. Soat oltiyarim bo'lgan, millar xotirjam oldinga siljib borardi; hatto oltiyarimdan ham o'tib, yettiga chorak qolayotgan edi. Budilnik chalinmadimi? Karavotdan ham uning soat to'rtga to'g'ri qo'yilgani ko'rinib turardi; demak, albatta chalingan. Ha, lekin mebelni silkitadigan bu jiringlashni tinchgina uxlab o'tkazib yuborish mumkinmi? Aslida u tinch uxlamagan edi, lekin, ehtimol, shuning uchun ham qattiqroq uxlagan. Endi nima qilsin? Keyingi poyezd yettida jo'naydi; unga ulgurish uchun telbalarcha shoshilishi kerak, namunalar hali yig'ilmagan, o'zi esa unchalik tetik va chaqqon emasdi.

paras.en: And even if he caught the train, there was no avoiding a storm from the boss, because the firm's messenger had waited for the five o'clock train and had long since reported that he had missed it. The man was the boss's creature, with no backbone and no brains. What if he reported sick? But that would be extremely awkward and would look suspicious, because in his five years with the firm Gregor had not been ill even once. The boss would certainly come with the doctor from the health insurance fund, blame his parents for their lazy son and cut off every objection by pointing to the insurance doctor, for whom there are only completely healthy people who are afraid of work. And would he really be so wrong in this case? Apart from a sleepiness that was quite unnecessary after such a long sleep, Gregor actually felt very well and was even particularly hungry.
paras.uz: Poyezdga ulgurgan taqdirda ham xo'jayinning g'azabidan qochib bo'lmasdi, chunki firma xizmatchisi soat beshdagi poyezdni kutib turgan va uning kelmagani haqida allaqachon xabar bergan edi. U xo'jayinning qo'g'irchog'i — umurtqasiz va aqlsiz odam edi. Kasal ekanini aytsa-chi? Lekin bu juda noqulay va shubhali bo'lardi, chunki Gregor firmada ishlagan besh yil ichida bir marta ham kasal bo'lmagan. Xo'jayin, shubhasiz, sug'urta kassasi shifokori bilan kelar, ota-onasini dangasa o'g'li uchun ayblar va har qanday e'tirozni shu shifokorga ishora qilib bo'lib qo'yardi — uning nazarida dunyoda faqat sog'lom, lekin ishdan qochadigan odamlar bor. Aytgancha, bu holatda u unchalik nohaq bo'larmidi? Uzoq uyqudan keyin mutlaqo ortiqcha bo'lgan uyquchanlikni hisobga olmaganda, Gregor o'zini juda yaxshi his qilardi, hatto qorni qattiq ochgan edi.

paras.en: As he was thinking all this over in great haste, unable to make up his mind to leave the bed — the clock had just struck a quarter to seven — there was a careful knock at the door at the head of his bed. “Gregor,” someone called — it was his mother — “it's a quarter to seven. Didn't you want to catch the train?” That gentle voice! Gregor was shocked when he heard his own voice answering. It was clearly his old voice, but mixed into it, as if from below, was a painful squeaking that he could not suppress. It left the words clear only for a moment and then distorted their echo so much that you could not be sure you had heard them correctly.
paras.uz: U bularning barchasini shoshib o'ylar, karavotni tark etishga hech qaror qilolmasdi. Shu payt soat yettiga chorak qolganini urdi va karavotning bosh tomonidagi eshik ehtiyotkorlik bilan taqillatildi. «Gregor, — dedi kimdir (bu onasi edi), — yettiga chorak qoldi. Ketmoqchi emasmiding?» Qanday mayin ovoz! Gregor javob berayotgan o'z ovozini eshitib, qo'rqib ketdi. Bu, shubhasiz, uning avvalgi ovozi edi, lekin unga go'yo pastdan bostirib bo'lmaydigan, og'riqli chiyillash qo'shilgan edi. Bu chiyillash so'zlarni faqat birinchi lahzada aniq qoldirar, keyin esa aks-sadosini shunday buzardiki, to'g'ri eshitdimmi-yo'qmi, bilib bo'lmasdi.

paras.en: Gregor had wanted to answer in detail and explain everything, but in the circumstances he only said: “Yes, yes, thank you, Mother, I'm getting up now.” Because of the wooden door, the change in Gregor's voice probably could not be noticed outside, for his mother was satisfied with this answer and shuffled away. But the short conversation had made the rest of the family aware that, unexpectedly, Gregor was still at home, and already his father was knocking at one of the side doors, weakly, but with his fist. “Gregor, Gregor,” he called, “what's the matter?” And after a little while he warned again in a deeper voice: “Gregor! Gregor!”
paras.uz: Gregor batafsil javob berib, hammasini tushuntirmoqchi edi, ammo bu holatda faqat: «Ha, ha, rahmat, onajon, hozir turaman», — dedi. Yog'och eshik tufayli tashqarida Gregorning ovozidagi o'zgarish sezilmagan bo'lsa kerak, chunki onasi bu javobdan tinchlanib, oyog'ini sudrab nari ketdi. Lekin bu qisqa suhbatdan oilaning boshqa a'zolari Gregor kutilmaganda hali uyda ekanini bilib qolishdi va yon eshiklardan birini otasi taqillata boshladi — sekin, lekin musht bilan. «Gregor, Gregor, — dedi u, — nima bo'ldi?» Biroz o'tib yana pastroq ovozda ogohlantirdi: «Gregor! Gregor!»

paras.en: At the other side door, however, his sister was quietly lamenting: “Gregor? Aren't you well? Do you need anything?” Gregor answered in both directions: “I'm ready now,” and tried to take everything strange out of his voice by pronouncing the words very carefully and putting long pauses between them. His father went back to his breakfast, but his sister whispered: “Gregor, open the door, I beg you.” Gregor, however, had no intention of opening it, and he was glad of the habit, which he had picked up from travelling, of locking all the doors at night, even at home.
paras.uz: Ikkinchi yon eshik ortida esa singlisi ohista nolirdi: «Gregor? Mazang yo'qmi? Biror narsa kerakmi?» Gregor ikki tomonga ham: «Tayyorman», — deb javob berdi va so'zlarni juda puxta talaffuz qilib, ular orasida uzoq to'xtalishlar qilib, ovozidagi g'alati narsalarni yashirishga harakat qildi. Otasi nonushtasiga qaytdi, singlisi esa pichirladi: «Gregor, eshikni och, iltimos qilaman». Lekin Gregor eshikni ochishni xayoliga ham keltirmadi va safarlarda orttirgan odati — uyda ham kechasi barcha eshiklarni qulflab olishidan xursand bo'ldi.

paras.en: First of all he wanted to get up quietly and without being disturbed, get dressed and above all have breakfast, and only then think about what to do next, because he could tell that lying in bed he would never come to any sensible conclusion. He remembered that he had often felt some slight pain in bed, perhaps from lying awkwardly, which had then turned out to be pure imagination as soon as he got up, and he was curious to see how today's illusions would gradually fade away. He did not doubt in the least that the change in his voice was nothing more than the first sign of a heavy cold, an occupational illness of travelling salesmen.
paras.uz: Avvalo u tinch va hech kim xalaqit bermasdan turib, kiyinib, eng muhimi nonushta qilib, shundan keyingina nima qilish haqida o'ylamoqchi edi, chunki karavotda yotib o'ylasa, hech qanday oqilona xulosaga kelolmasligini sezib turardi. U karavotda ko'p marta noqulay yotgani uchun bo'lsa kerak, yengil og'riq sezganini, turishi bilanoq esa bu shunchaki xayol bo'lib chiqqanini esladi va bugungi tasavvurlari asta-sekin qanday tarqab ketishini qiziqib kutdi. Ovozidagi o'zgarish qattiq shamollashning — sayyor agentlarning kasb kasalligining — birinchi belgisidan boshqa narsa emasligiga u zarracha ham shubha qilmasdi.

paras.en: Throwing off the blanket was quite easy; he only needed to puff himself up a little and it fell off by itself. But after that it became difficult, especially because he was so unusually wide. He would have needed arms and hands to sit up; instead he only had all those little legs, which never stopped moving in every possible direction and which, on top of that, he could not control. If he wanted to bend one of them, the first thing it did was stretch out; and when he finally managed to make that leg do what he wanted, all the others meanwhile were working as if set free, in the highest, most painful excitement. “Just don't stay in bed doing nothing,” Gregor said to himself.
paras.uz: Ko'rpani uloqtirib tashlash juda oson edi: biroz shishsa bas, o'zi tushib ketdi. Ammo undan keyin qiyinlashdi, ayniqsa u g'ayrioddiy darajada keng bo'lgani uchun. O'tirish uchun unga qo'l va kaftlar kerak edi; ularning o'rniga esa uzluksiz har tomonga qimirlab turadigan va ustiga ustak o'zi boshqara olmaydigan ko'plab mitti oyoqlari bor edi. Ulardan birini bukmoqchi bo'lsa, oyoq avval cho'zilib ketardi; nihoyat shu oyoqqa xohlaganini qildira olganida esa, qolganlarining hammasi go'yo erkinlikka chiqqanday, nihoyatda og'riqli hayajon bilan tipirchilardi. «Faqat karavotda bekorga yotmaslik kerak», — dedi o'ziga Gregor.

paras.en: First he tried to get the lower part of his body out of the bed. But this lower part, which he had not yet seen and of which he could form no clear idea, turned out to be too hard to move; it went so slowly. When at last, almost wild with frustration, he gathered all his strength and pushed himself forward without care, he chose the wrong direction and banged hard against the bottom bedpost. The burning pain he felt taught him that, at the moment, the lower part of his body was perhaps the most sensitive part of all.
paras.uz: Avval u tanasining pastki qismini karavotdan chiqarmoqchi bo'ldi. Lekin hali ko'rmagan va qandayligini aniq tasavvur ham qilolmagan bu pastki qism juda qiyin harakatlanar ekan; hammasi juda sekin bo'lardi. Nihoyat, deyarli jahli chiqib, bor kuchini yig'ib, ehtiyot bo'lmay oldinga intilganida, yo'nalishni noto'g'ri tanladi va karavotning pastki ustuniga qattiq urildi. Sezgan kuydiruvchi og'rig'i unga hozir aynan tanasining pastki qismi, ehtimol, eng sezgir joyi ekanini o'rgatdi.

paras.en: So he tried to get the upper part of his body out of the bed first, and carefully turned his head towards the edge. This worked easily, and in the end, despite its width and weight, the mass of his body slowly followed the turn of his head. But when he finally held his head out of the bed in the open air, he became afraid to go on moving forward in this way, because if he let himself fall like that, it would take a real miracle for his head not to be injured. And at this moment, of all moments, he must not lose consciousness; he would rather stay in bed.
paras.uz: Shuning uchun u avval tanasining yuqori qismini karavotdan chiqarishga urindi va ehtiyotkorlik bilan boshini karavot chetiga burdi. Bu oson bo'ldi va kengligi hamda og'irligiga qaramay, tanasi oxiri boshining burilishiga sekin ergashdi. Lekin nihoyat boshini karavotdan tashqarida, ochiq havoda ushlab turganida, shu tarzda oldinga siljishdan qo'rqib ketdi, chunki o'zini shu holda tashlab yuborsa, boshi shikastlanmasligi uchun chinakam mo'jiza kerak bo'lardi. Ayniqsa hozir hushini yo'qotishga aslo haqqi yo'q edi; bundan ko'ra karavotda qolgani ma'qul.

paras.en: But when, after the same effort, he lay there sighing just as before, and again saw his little legs fighting each other even worse than before, and could find no way of bringing calm and order into this chaos, he told himself again that he could not possibly stay in bed, and that the most sensible thing was to risk everything if there was even the slightest hope of freeing himself from the bed. At the same time, however, he did not forget to remind himself now and then that calm, very calm thinking was much better than desperate decisions.
paras.uz: Lekin shuncha urinishdan keyin yana avvalgidek xo'rsinib yotganida, mitti oyoqlari yana avvalgidan ham battar bir-biri bilan olishayotganini ko'rib, bu tartibsizlikka tinchlik va tartib olib kirishning hech qanday yo'lini topolmaganida, u yana karavotda qolishi mutlaqo mumkin emasligini, agar karavotdan qutulishga zarracha umid bo'lsa, hamma narsani tavakkal qilish eng oqilona yo'l ekanini o'ziga aytdi. Shu bilan birga, u vaqti-vaqti bilan umidsiz qarorlardan ko'ra xotirjam, juda xotirjam fikrlash ancha yaxshi ekanini ham eslab turdi.

paras.en: At such moments he fixed his eyes as sharply as he could on the window, but unfortunately there was little confidence or cheerfulness to be gained from the sight of the morning fog, which hid even the other side of the narrow street. “Seven o'clock already,” he said to himself as the alarm clock struck again, “seven o'clock already and still such a fog.” And for a little while he lay quietly, breathing weakly, as if perhaps he expected the complete silence to bring back the real, normal state of things.
paras.uz: Shunday paytlarda u ko'zlarini iloji boricha derazaga tikardi, lekin afsuski, tor ko'chaning narigi tomonini ham to'sib qo'ygan tong tumanini ko'rishdan unchalik ishonch yoki tetiklik olib bo'lmasdi. «Soat yetti bo'pti, — dedi u o'ziga budilnik yana chalinganida, — soat yetti bo'pti, hamon shunday tuman». Va bir muddat u go'yo to'liq sukunat hamma narsani haqiqiy, odatiy holiga qaytarishini kutayotganday, kuchsiz nafas olib, jimgina yotdi.

paras.en: But then he told himself: “Before it strikes a quarter past seven, I absolutely must be completely out of bed. Besides, by then someone will come from the firm to ask about me, because the office opens before seven.” And he set about rocking his whole body out of the bed, evenly along its entire length. If he let himself fall out of bed in this way, his head, which he meant to lift sharply as he fell, would probably stay unhurt. His back seemed to be hard; nothing would happen to it when it fell onto the carpet. His greatest worry was the loud crash it was bound to make, which would probably cause, if not fear, then at least concern behind all the doors. But he had to take the risk.
paras.uz: Lekin keyin o'ziga dedi: «Soat yettidan chorak o'tguncha karavotdan butunlay tushgan bo'lishim shart. Bundan tashqari, shu paytgacha firmadan kimdir men haqimda so'rab keladi, chunki idora yettidan oldin ochiladi». Va u butun tanasini uzunasiga bir tekis tebratib, karavotdan chiqarishga kirishdi. Agar o'zini shu tarzda karavotdan tushirsa, yiqilayotganda keskin ko'tarmoqchi bo'lgan boshi, ehtimol, shikastlanmay qolardi. Orqasi qattiq ko'rinardi; gilamga tushganda unga hech narsa bo'lmasa kerak. Uni eng ko'p tashvishga solgani — albatta chiqadigan qattiq taraqa edi: bu barcha eshiklar ortida qo'rquv bo'lmasa ham, xavotir uyg'otishi aniq edi. Ammo tavakkal qilish kerak edi.

chapters.title: The Chief Clerk
chapters.recap_uz: Gregor karavotdan yiqilib tushadi. Firmadan bosh xizmatchi (prokurist) kelib, uni dangasalik va hatto pulni o'zlashtirishda shubha qiladi. Gregor uzoq gapirib o'zini oqlaydi, lekin uning ovozini hech kim tushunmaydi: «Bu hayvon ovozi edi».

paras.en: When Gregor was already sticking halfway out of the bed — the new method was more of a game than an effort; he only had to keep rocking in jerks — it occurred to him how simple everything would be if someone came to help him. Two strong people — he thought of his father and the maid — would have been quite enough. They would only have had to push their arms under his curved back, peel him out of the bed, bend down with their load and then just carefully wait while he swung himself over onto the floor, where his little legs would hopefully start to make sense. Well, apart from the fact that the doors were locked, should he really call for help? In spite of all his misery, he could not help smiling at the thought.
paras.uz: Gregor karavotdan yarmigacha chiqib qolganida — yangi usul mashaqqatdan ko'ra o'yinga o'xshardi, faqat siltanib tebranib tursa bo'ldi — agar unga kimdir yordamga kelsa, hammasi naqadar oson bo'lishi esiga tushdi. Ikki baquvvat odam — u otasi va oqsochni o'yladi — butunlay yetarli bo'lardi. Ular qo'llarini uning qavariq orqasi ostiga tiqib, uni karavotdan ko'chirib olishsa, yuk bilan engashib, so'ng uning polga ag'darilishini ehtiyotkorlik bilan kutishsa bas edi; polda esa mitti oyoqlari, umid qilamizki, biror ma'no kasb etardi. Xo'sh, eshiklarning qulflanganini aytmaganda ham, u rostdan yordam so'rab chaqirishi kerakmidi? Barcha azobiga qaramay, bu fikrdan jilmayib qo'ymaslikning iloji bo'lmadi.

paras.en: He had got so far that, if he rocked more strongly, he could hardly keep his balance any more, and very soon he would have to make a final decision, because in five minutes it would be a quarter past seven — when the doorbell of the flat rang. “That's someone from the firm,” he told himself and almost froze, while his little legs danced all the faster. For a moment everything stayed silent. “They're not opening,” Gregor told himself, caught up in some absurd hope. But then of course, as always, the maid went to the door with firm steps and opened it. Gregor only needed to hear the visitor's first word of greeting to know who it was — the chief clerk himself.
paras.uz: U shu darajaga yetdiki, qattiqroq tebransa, muvozanatini arang saqlab qolardi va tez orada uzil-kesil qaror qilishi kerak edi, chunki besh daqiqadan keyin soat yettidan chorak o'tadi. Shu payt kvartira eshigining qo'ng'irog'i chalindi. «Bu firmadan kimdir», — dedi u o'ziga va deyarli qotib qoldi, mitti oyoqlari esa yanada tezroq raqsga tushardi. Bir lahza hamma joy jim bo'ldi. «Ochishmayapti», — dedi o'ziga Gregor qandaydir bema'ni umidga berilib. Lekin keyin, albatta, har doimgidek oqsoch qat'iy qadamlar bilan eshik tomon borib, uni ochdi. Gregor mehmonning birinchi salom so'zini eshitishi bilanoq kimligini bildi — bosh xizmatchining o'zi.

paras.en: Why was Gregor of all people condemned to work for a firm where the smallest slip immediately aroused the greatest suspicion? Were all the employees, every single one, scoundrels? Was there not one loyal, devoted man among them who, if he had failed to use just a couple of morning hours for the firm, went half mad with guilt and was actually unable to leave his bed? Was it really not enough to send an apprentice to ask — if this asking was necessary at all? Did the chief clerk have to come himself, and did the whole innocent family have to be shown that the investigation of this suspicious matter could only be trusted to the chief clerk's intelligence?
paras.uz: Nega aynan Gregor eng kichik xato uchun ham darhol eng katta shubha uyg'onadigan firmada xizmat qilishga mahkum edi? Nahotki barcha xodimlar birdek muttahamlar bo'lsa? Nahotki ular orasida firmaga atigi bir-ikki tong soatini sarflay olmagani uchun vijdon azobidan aqldan ozayozgan va hatto karavotdan turolmaydigan birorta sodiq, fidoyi odam bo'lmasa? Nahotki so'rab kelish uchun — agar umuman so'rash kerak bo'lsa — biror shogird yuborish yetarli bo'lmasa? Bosh xizmatchining o'zi kelishi va butun aybsiz oilaga bu shubhali ishni tekshirishni faqat bosh xizmatchining aql-idrokiga ishonib topshirish mumkinligini ko'rsatishi shartmidi?

paras.en: And more because of the agitation these thoughts put him in than because of any proper decision, Gregor swung himself out of the bed with all his strength. There was a loud thump, but it was not really a crash. The fall was softened a little by the carpet, and his back was also more elastic than Gregor had thought, which explained the dull sound that was not so very noticeable. Only he had not held his head carefully enough and had hit it; he turned it and rubbed it on the carpet in annoyance and pain.
paras.uz: Va to'g'ri qarordan ko'ra ko'proq shu fikrlar uyg'otgan hayajon tufayli Gregor bor kuchi bilan karavotdan otilib tushdi. Qattiq gup etgan ovoz chiqdi, lekin bu haqiqiy taraqa emas edi. Yiqilishni gilam biroz yumshatdi, orqasi ham Gregor o'ylaganidan ko'ra egiluvchanroq ekan — shuning uchun unchalik e'tiborni tortmaydigan bo'g'iq tovush chiqdi. Faqat boshini yetarlicha ehtiyot qilmagan va uni urib olgan edi; u jahl va og'riq bilan boshini burib, gilamga ishqaladi.

paras.en: “Something has fallen in there,” said the chief clerk in the room on the left. Gregor tried to imagine whether something like what had happened to him today might not also happen to the chief clerk one day; after all, one really had to admit that it was possible. But as if in rough reply to this question, the chief clerk took a few firm steps in the next room and made his patent-leather boots creak. From the room on the right his sister whispered, to let Gregor know: “Gregor, the chief clerk is here.” “I know,” Gregor said to himself; but he did not dare to raise his voice loud enough for his sister to hear.
paras.uz: «U yerda nimadir yiqildi», — dedi chap tomondagi xonada bosh xizmatchi. Gregor bugun o'zi bilan sodir bo'lgan narsaga o'xshash voqea qachondir bosh xizmatchining boshiga ham tushmasmikin, deb tasavvur qilishga urindi; axir buning ehtimolini tan olish kerak edi. Lekin bu savolga qo'pol javob bergandek, bosh xizmatchi qo'shni xonada bir necha qat'iy qadam tashladi va laklangan etiklarini g'ijirlatdi. O'ng tomondagi xonadan singlisi Gregorni ogohlantirish uchun pichirladi: «Gregor, bosh xizmatchi keldi». «Bilaman», — dedi Gregor o'zicha; lekin singlisi eshitadigan darajada ovozini ko'tarishga jur'at etmadi.

paras.en: “Gregor,” his father now said from the room on the left, “the chief clerk has come and wants to know why you didn't leave on the early train. We don't know what to tell him. Besides, he wants to speak to you personally. So please open the door. I'm sure he'll be kind enough to excuse the untidiness of your room.” “Good morning, Mr Samsa,” the chief clerk called in a friendly way. “He's not well,” his mother told the chief clerk, while his father was still talking at the door, “he's not well, believe me, sir. How else would Gregor miss a train? The boy thinks of nothing but the business.
paras.uz: «Gregor, — dedi endi chap tomondagi xonadan otasi, — janob bosh xizmatchi kelib, nega ertalabki poyezdda jo'nab ketmaganingni so'rayapti. Unga nima deyishni bilmaymiz. Bundan tashqari, u sen bilan shaxsan gaplashmoqchi. Shuning uchun iltimos, eshikni och. U xonangdagi tartibsizlikni kechirishga muruvvat qiladi, albatta». «Xayrli tong, janob Samsa», — deb do'stona gap qo'shdi bosh xizmatchi. «Uning mazasi yo'q, — dedi onasi bosh xizmatchiga, otasi hali eshik oldida gapirayotgan paytda, — mazasi yo'q, ishoning, janob. Bo'lmasa Gregor poyezddan qolarmidi! Bolaning boshida ishdan boshqa hech narsa yo'q.

paras.en: It almost annoys me that he never goes out in the evenings. He's been in town for eight days now, but every evening he was at home. He sits with us at the table and quietly reads the newspaper or studies train timetables. Doing a bit of fretwork is entertainment for him. For example, in two or three evenings he carved a little frame; you'll be amazed how pretty it is; it's hanging in his room; you'll see it as soon as Gregor opens up. I'm glad you're here, by the way, sir; we would never have got Gregor to open the door on our own; he's so stubborn; and I'm sure he's not well, even though he denied it this morning.”
paras.uz: Kechqurunlari hech qayerga chiqmasligidan hatto jahlim chiqadi. Mana, sakkiz kundan beri shaharda, lekin har oqshom uyda o'tirdi. Biz bilan stolda o'tirib, jimgina gazeta o'qiydi yoki poyezd jadvallarini o'rganadi. Arracha bilan yog'och o'ymakorligi bilan shug'ullanish ham uning uchun ko'ngilxushlik. Masalan, ikki-uch oqshomda kichkina ramka o'yib yasadi; qanchalik chiroyli ekaniga hayron qolasiz; xonasida osig'liq turibdi; Gregor eshikni ochishi bilan ko'rasiz. Aytgancha, kelganingizdan xursandman, janob; o'zimiz Gregorni eshikni ochishga ko'ndira olmasdik; u juda o'jar; mazasi yo'qligi aniq, garchi ertalab buni inkor qilgan bo'lsa ham».

paras.en: “I'm coming,” said Gregor slowly and deliberately, and did not move, so as not to miss a word of the conversation. “I can't explain it any other way either, madam,” said the chief clerk. “I hope it's nothing serious. Though on the other hand I must say that we business people — whether you call it unfortunate or fortunate — very often simply have to overcome a slight illness for the sake of business.” “So can the chief clerk come in to you now?” asked his impatient father, knocking on the door again. “No,” said Gregor. In the room on the left there was an embarrassed silence; in the room on the right his sister began to sob.
paras.uz: «Hozir boraman», — dedi Gregor sekin va o'ylab, suhbatdan bitta so'zni ham o'tkazib yubormaslik uchun qimirlamay yotdi. «Men ham buni boshqacha izohlay olmayman, xonim, — dedi bosh xizmatchi, — umid qilamanki, jiddiy narsa emas. Garchi, boshqa tomondan, aytishim kerakki, biz ish odamlari — xohlang baxtsizlik deng, xohlang baxt — yengil betoblikni ish manfaati uchun ko'pincha shunchaki yengib o'tishimiz kerak». «Xo'sh, janob bosh xizmatchi endi oldingga kirsa bo'ladimi?» — deb so'radi sabrsiz otasi va yana eshikni taqillatdi. «Yo'q», — dedi Gregor. Chap tomondagi xonada noqulay sukunat cho'kdi, o'ng tomondagi xonada esa singlisi yig'lay boshladi.

paras.en: Why didn't his sister go to the others? She had probably only just got out of bed and had not even started to dress. And why was she crying? Because he was not getting up and not letting the chief clerk in, because he was in danger of losing his job, and because the boss would then go after his parents again with the old debts? Those were surely unnecessary worries for the moment. Gregor was still here and did not have the slightest intention of leaving his family. At the moment he was lying on the carpet, of course, and no one who knew his condition would seriously have asked him to let the chief clerk in.
paras.uz: Nega singlisi boshqalar oldiga bormayapti? U, ehtimol, endigina o'rnidan turgan va hali kiyina boshlamagan ham edi. Nega yig'layapti? U turmayotgani va bosh xizmatchini ichkariga kiritmayotgani uchunmi, ishini yo'qotish xavfi borligi uchunmi, shunda xo'jayin ota-onasini yana eski qarzlar bilan ta'qib qilishi uchunmi? Hozircha bular ortiqcha tashvishlar edi, albatta. Gregor hali shu yerda edi va oilasini tashlab ketishni zarracha ham o'ylamasdi. Hozir, to'g'ri, u gilamda yotardi va uning ahvolini bilgan hech kim undan bosh xizmatchini ichkariga kiritishni jiddiy talab qilmasdi.

paras.en: But Gregor could hardly be dismissed immediately because of this small piece of rudeness, for which a suitable excuse could easily be found later. And it seemed to Gregor that it would be much more sensible to leave him in peace now instead of disturbing him with crying and pleading. But it was precisely the uncertainty that was troubling the others and excused their behaviour.
paras.uz: Lekin keyinchalik osongina munosib bahona topiladigan bu kichik qo'pollik uchun Gregorni darhol ishdan haydab bo'lmasdi-ku. Gregorga hozir uni yig'i va yalinishlar bilan bezovta qilgandan ko'ra tinch qo'yish ancha oqilona bo'lardiday tuyuldi. Lekin aynan noaniqlik boshqalarni qiynar va ularning xatti-harakatini oqlardi.

paras.en: “Mr Samsa,” the chief clerk now called, raising his voice, “what is the matter? You barricade yourself in your room, you answer only yes and no, you cause your parents serious and unnecessary worry, and — I mention this only in passing — you neglect your business duties in a quite unheard-of way. I am speaking here in the name of your parents and of your employer, and I ask you very seriously for an immediate and clear explanation. I am astonished, astonished. I thought I knew you as a calm, sensible person, and now you suddenly seem to want to start showing off strange moods.
paras.uz: «Janob Samsa, — dedi endi bosh xizmatchi ovozini ko'tarib, — nima gap o'zi? Siz xonangizda barrikada qurib o'tiribsiz, faqat «ha» va «yo'q» deb javob beryapsiz, ota-onangizni jiddiy va keraksiz tashvishga solyapsiz va — buni shunchaki aytib o'tyapman — ish vazifalaringizni mutlaqo eshitilmagan darajada e'tiborsiz qoldiryapsiz. Men bu yerda ota-onangiz va xo'jayiningiz nomidan gapiryapman va sizdan juda jiddiy ravishda darhol aniq tushuntirish berishingizni so'rayman. Hayronman, hayronman. Men sizni xotirjam, aqlli odam deb bilardim, endi esa siz birdan g'alati injiqliklar bilan o'zingizni ko'rsatmoqchi bo'lyapsiz.

paras.en: This morning the boss did hint at a possible explanation for your absence — it concerned the cash payments recently entrusted to you — but I almost gave my word of honour that this explanation could not be true. Now, however, I see your incomprehensible stubbornness here, and I am losing all desire to stand up for you in the slightest. And your position is by no means the most secure. I originally intended to tell you all this privately, but since you are making me waste my time here for nothing, I don't see why your parents shouldn't hear it too. Your work recently has been very unsatisfactory. It is not, we admit, the season for doing particularly good business; but there is no such thing as a season for doing no business at all, Mr Samsa. There must not be.”
paras.uz: Bugun ertalab xo'jayin kelmaganingizga bir izoh borligiga ishora qildi — bu yaqinda sizga ishonib topshirilgan naqd pul yig'imiga tegishli edi — lekin men bu izoh to'g'ri bo'lishi mumkin emasligiga deyarli or-nomusim bilan kafolat berdim. Endi esa bu yerda sizning tushunib bo'lmas o'jarligingizni ko'rib, siz uchun zarracha ham qayg'urish istagini yo'qotyapman. Sizning lavozimingiz esa aslo mustahkam emas. Dastlab bularning hammasini sizga yolg'iz qolganda aytmoqchi edim, lekin siz meni bu yerda behuda vaqt yo'qotishga majbur qilayotganingiz uchun, nega ota-onangiz ham bilmasligi kerakligini tushunmayman. Oxirgi paytlardagi ishingiz juda qoniqarsiz bo'ldi. To'g'ri, hozir katta savdo qiladigan mavsum emas, buni tan olamiz; lekin savdo qilmaydigan mavsum degan narsa umuman yo'q, janob Samsa, bo'lishi ham mumkin emas».

paras.en: “But sir,” cried Gregor, beside himself, forgetting everything else in his excitement, “I'm opening the door right away, this very moment. A slight illness, a dizzy spell, has kept me from getting up. I'm still lying in bed now. But I'm already quite fresh again. I'm just getting out of bed. Just one little moment of patience! It's not going as well as I thought yet. But I'm already feeling well. How suddenly a thing like that can attack a person! Only last night I was perfectly fine, my parents know that — or rather, last night I already had a slight feeling. People must have been able to see it in me. Why didn't I report it to the office! But you always think you'll get over an illness without staying at home.
paras.uz: «Lekin, janob, — deb qichqirdi Gregor o'zini yo'qotib, hayajondan hamma narsani unutib, — men hozir, shu zahoti eshikni ochaman. Yengil betoblik, bosh aylanishi turishimga xalaqit berdi. Hozir ham karavotda yotibman. Lekin allaqachon yana butunlay tetikman. Mana, karavotdan tushyapman. Bir lahzagina sabr qiling! Hali men o'ylaganchalik yaxshi chiqmayapti. Lekin o'zimni yaxshi his qilyapman. Odamga shunday to'satdan yopishishi mumkin ekan-a! Kecha kechqurun ham juda yaxshi edim, ota-onam biladi, aniqrog'i, kecha kechqurunoq biroz sezib turgandim. Buni yuzimdan ko'rish mumkin edi. Nega idoraga aytmadim-a! Lekin odam doim kasallikni uyda qolmasdan yengib o'taman deb o'ylaydi.

paras.en: Sir! Spare my parents! There is no reason for all the reproaches you are making now; nobody ever said a word to me about them. Perhaps you haven't read the last orders I sent. Anyway, I'll still set off on my trip on the eight o'clock train; these few hours of rest have made me stronger. Don't let me keep you, sir; I'll be at the office myself in a moment, and please be so kind as to tell them that and give my respects to the boss!”
paras.uz: Janob! Ota-onamni ayang! Hozir menga qilayotgan barcha ta'nalaringizga hech qanday asos yo'q; menga bu haqda hech kim biror so'z aytmagan. Balki siz men yuborgan oxirgi buyurtmalarni o'qimagandirsiz. Qolaversa, soat sakkizdagi poyezdda safarga jo'nayman, bu bir necha soatlik dam meni kuchga to'ldirdi. Ushlanib qolmang, janob; hozir o'zim idoraga boraman, iltimos, shuni ayting va xo'jayinga mendan salom yetkazing!»

paras.en: And while Gregor blurted all this out in a hurry, hardly knowing what he was saying, he had moved easily towards the chest of drawers, probably thanks to the practice he had already gained in bed, and was now trying to raise himself up against it. He really wanted to open the door, really wanted to show himself and speak to the chief clerk. He was eager to find out what the others, who were now so anxious to see him, would say at the sight of him. If they were frightened, then Gregor would no longer be responsible and could be calm. But if they took it all calmly, then he too had no reason to get upset, and if he hurried he could really be at the station by eight.
paras.uz: Gregor bularning hammasini nima deyayotganini o'zi ham bilmay shoshib aytib tashlar ekan, karavotda orttirgan mashqi tufayli bo'lsa kerak, osongina javonga yaqinlashdi va endi unga tayanib qaddini rostlashga urinardi. U chindan ham eshikni ochmoqchi, chindan ham o'zini ko'rsatib, bosh xizmatchi bilan gaplashmoqchi edi. Hozir uni ko'rishni bunchalik istayotganlar uni ko'rganda nima deyishini bilishga intiqib turardi. Agar ular qo'rqib ketishsa, demak, Gregor endi javobgar emas va xotirjam bo'lishi mumkin. Agar hammasini xotirjam qabul qilishsa, unda unga ham hayajonlanishga sabab yo'q va shoshilsa, soat sakkizda chindan ham vokzalda bo'lishi mumkin.

paras.en: At first he slid off the smooth chest a few times, but at last he gave himself one final swing and stood upright; he no longer paid any attention to the pain in his lower body, however much it burned. Then he let himself fall against the back of a nearby chair and held on to its edges with his little legs. With that he had gained control of himself and fell silent, because now he could listen to the chief clerk.
paras.uz: Avvaliga u silliq javondan bir necha marta sirg'alib tushdi, lekin oxiri o'zini so'nggi marta siltab, tik turib oldi; tanasining pastki qismidagi og'riqqa, u qanchalik achishtirmasin, endi e'tibor ham bermadi. Keyin u o'zini yaqin turgan stulning suyanchig'iga tashladi va mitti oyoqlari bilan uning chetlaridan mahkam ushlab oldi. Shu bilan u o'zini boshqarishga erishdi va jim bo'ldi, chunki endi bosh xizmatchini tinglashi mumkin edi.

paras.en: “Did you understand a single word?” the chief clerk asked the parents. “He isn't making fools of us, is he?” “For heaven's sake,” cried his mother, already in tears, “perhaps he's seriously ill and we're tormenting him. Grete! Grete!” she then screamed. “Mother?” called his sister from the other side. They were communicating through Gregor's room. “You must go to the doctor at once. Gregor is ill. Quickly, get the doctor. Did you hear Gregor speaking just now?” “That was the voice of an animal,” said the chief clerk, strikingly quietly compared with the mother's screaming.
paras.uz: «Birorta so'zini tushundingizmi?» — deb so'radi bosh xizmatchi ota-onadan. — U bizni masxara qilmayaptimi?» «Xudo haqqi, — dedi onasi yig'lab yuborib, — balki u og'ir kasaldir, biz esa uni qiynayapmiz. Grete! Grete!» — deb qichqirdi keyin. «Onajon?» — dedi singlisi narigi tomondan. Ular Gregorning xonasi orqali gaplashishardi. «Darhol shifokorga borishing kerak. Gregor kasal. Tezroq shifokorni chaqir. Hozir Gregorning gapirganini eshitdingmi?» «Bu hayvonning ovozi edi», — dedi bosh xizmatchi, onaning qichqirig'iga nisbatan juda past ovozda.

paras.en: “Anna! Anna!” his father called through the hall into the kitchen, clapping his hands, “fetch a locksmith at once!” And already the two girls were running through the hall with rustling skirts — how had his sister got dressed so quickly? — and they pulled open the front door. There was no sound of the door slamming; they had probably left it open, as is usual in homes where a great misfortune has happened.
paras.uz: «Anna! Anna! — deb chaqirdi otasi dahliz orqali oshxonaga qarab va qarsak chaldi. — Darhol chilangar olib kel!» Va mana, ikki qiz yubkalarini shitirlatib dahlizdan yugurib o'tishdi — singlisi qanday qilib buncha tez kiyinib oldi? — va kvartira eshigini yulqib ochishdi. Eshik yopilgani eshitilmadi; ular, ehtimol, katta baxtsizlik yuz bergan uylarda odat bo'lganidek, uni ochiq qoldirishgan edi.

paras.en: Gregor, however, had become much calmer. So they no longer understood his words, even though they had seemed clear enough to him, clearer than before, perhaps because his ear had got used to them. But at least people now believed that something was not quite right with him and were ready to help him. The confidence and certainty with which the first orders had been given did him good. He felt himself included once more in the human circle, and he hoped for great and surprising achievements from both the doctor and the locksmith, without really distinguishing between them.
paras.uz: Gregor esa ancha tinchlanib qolgan edi. Demak, uning so'zlarini endi tushunishmayapti, garchi ular unga yetarlicha aniq, hatto avvalgidan aniqroq tuyulgan bo'lsa ham — ehtimol, qulog'i ko'nikib qolgani uchun. Lekin har holda endi hamma u bilan nimadir joyida emasligiga ishonar va unga yordam berishga tayyor edi. Birinchi buyruqlar berilgandagi ishonch va qat'iyat unga yoqdi. U o'zini yana odamlar davrasiga qo'shilganday his qildi va ikkalasidan — shifokordan ham, chilangardan ham, ularni aslida bir-biridan ajratmagan holda — ajoyib va kutilmagan natijalar kutdi.

paras.en: To get as clear a voice as possible for the decisive conversations that were coming, he coughed a little, although he tried to do it very quietly, since perhaps even this sound no longer sounded like a human cough, and he no longer trusted himself to judge. Meanwhile, the next room had become completely silent. Perhaps his parents were sitting at the table with the chief clerk, whispering; perhaps they were all leaning against the door, listening.
paras.uz: Yaqinlashayotgan hal qiluvchi suhbatlar uchun ovozini iloji boricha tiniq qilish maqsadida u biroz yo'talib oldi, lekin buni juda bo'g'iq qilishga harakat qildi, chunki, ehtimol, bu tovush ham endi odam yo'taliga o'xshamas edi, buni esa o'zi aniqlashga endi jur'at etmasdi. Bu orada qo'shni xona butunlay jimib qolgan edi. Balki ota-onasi bosh xizmatchi bilan stol atrofida o'tirib, shivirlashayotgandir, balki hammasi eshikka suyanib quloq solib turgandir.

gloss.ex: ...the smallest slip immediately aroused the greatest suspicion.
...the cash payments recently entrusted to you.

quiz.q: Who comes to the Samsa home from Gregor's firm?
quiz.why_uz: Firma kichik bir kechikish uchun bosh xizmatchining o'zini yuboradi — bu Gregorning ishdagi ahvolini ko'rsatadi.

quiz.q: What does the chief clerk suggest Gregor may have done?
o: Done something wrong with the cash payments
quiz.why_uz: U Gregorni pul yig'imida xiyonatda shubha qilganini ochiq aytadi.

quiz.q: What does the chief clerk say about Gregor's voice?
o: It was the voice of an animal
quiz.why_uz: Gregor o'zini odamday gapiryapman deb o'ylaydi, lekin boshqalar uchun bu allaqachon hayvon ovozi.

chapters.note_uz: Bu bobda Gregorning ichki dunyosi bilan tashqi dunyo o'rtasidagi tafovut kuchayadi. U uzun, odobli nutq so'zlaydi, lekin boshqalar faqat hayvon ovozini eshitadi. Kafka uchun bu muloqotning buzilishi ramzi: inson gapiradi, lekin uni hech kim tushunmaydi.

chapters.title: The Door Opens
chapters.recap_uz: Gregor jag'lari bilan kalitni burab, eshikni ochadi. Uni ko'rgan bosh xizmatchi qochib ketadi, onasi hushidan ketay deydi. Otasi tayoq va gazeta bilan Gregorni xonasiga haydaydi; Gregor eshikda qisilib, yaralanadi.

paras.en: Gregor slowly pushed himself towards the door with the chair, let go of it there, threw himself against the door and held himself upright on it — the pads of his little legs were slightly sticky — and rested there for a moment after the effort. Then he set about turning the key in the lock with his mouth. Unfortunately it seemed that he had no real teeth — what was he supposed to grip the key with? — but on the other hand his jaws were certainly very strong. With their help he really did get the key moving, and he paid no attention to the fact that he was undoubtedly hurting himself, for a brown liquid came out of his mouth, flowed over the key and dripped onto the floor.
paras.uz: Gregor stul bilan birga eshik tomon asta surildi, u yerda stulni qo'yib yubordi, o'zini eshikka tashladi va unga tayanib tik turdi — mitti oyoqlarining tagi biroz yopishqoq edi — va mashaqqatdan keyin u yerda bir lahza dam oldi. Keyin og'zi bilan qulfdagi kalitni burashga kirishdi. Afsuski, uning haqiqiy tishlari yo'qqa o'xshardi — kalitni nima bilan ushlasin? — lekin buning o'rniga jag'lari, shubhasiz, juda kuchli edi. Ular yordamida u chindan ham kalitni qimirlata oldi va o'ziga, shubhasiz, qandaydir zarar yetkazayotganiga e'tibor bermadi: og'zidan jigarrang suyuqlik chiqib, kalit ustidan oqib, polga tomchilardi.

paras.en: “Just listen,” said the chief clerk in the next room, “he's turning the key.” That was a great encouragement for Gregor; but they all should have called out to him, his father and mother too: “Go on, Gregor,” they should have called, “keep going, keep at that lock!” And imagining that they were all following his efforts with suspense, he bit down on the key with all the strength he could gather, almost losing consciousness. As the key turned further, he danced around the lock, now holding himself upright only by his mouth, and as needed he hung on to the key or pressed it down again with the whole weight of his body. The clearer sound of the lock finally snapping back really woke Gregor up. Breathing out, he said to himself: “So I didn't need the locksmith after all,” and laid his head on the handle to open the door completely.
paras.uz: «Eshityapsizmi, — dedi qo'shni xonada bosh xizmatchi, — u kalitni buryapti». Bu Gregor uchun katta dalda bo'ldi; lekin hamma, otasi ham, onasi ham unga baqirishi kerak edi: «Barakalla, Gregor, — deyishlari kerak edi, — davom et, qulfni mahkam ushla!» Hamma uning harakatlarini hayajon bilan kuzatib turibdi, deb tasavvur qilib, u bor kuchini yig'ib, deyarli hushidan ketgancha kalitga tishlarini botirdi. Kalit burilib borgan sari u qulf atrofida aylanib raqsga tushar, endi faqat og'zi bilan tik turar, kerak bo'lsa kalitga osilib olar yoki butun tanasi og'irligi bilan uni pastga bosardi. Nihoyat orqaga qaytgan qulfning jarangdorroq tovushi Gregorni go'yo uyg'otib yubordi. Yengil nafas olib, u o'ziga dedi: «Demak, chilangar kerak bo'lmadi», — va eshikni to'liq ochish uchun boshini dastasiga qo'ydi.

paras.en: Because he had to open the door in this way, it was already quite wide open while he himself still could not be seen. He first had to turn slowly around one half of the door, and very carefully too, if he did not want to fall clumsily onto his back just before entering the room. He was still busy with this difficult movement and had no time to notice anything else when he heard the chief clerk let out a loud “Oh!” — it sounded like the wind rushing — and now he could see him too: being the nearest to the door, he was pressing his hand against his open mouth and slowly backing away, as if driven by an invisible force that kept pushing steadily.
paras.uz: Eshikni shu tarzda ochishga majbur bo'lgani uchun u allaqachon ancha keng ochilgan, o'zi esa hali ko'rinmasdi. Eshik oldida beo'xshov chalqancha yiqilib tushmaslik uchun u avval eshikning bir tavaqasi atrofida sekin, juda ehtiyotkorlik bilan aylanib o'tishi kerak edi. U hali shu qiyin harakat bilan band bo'lib, boshqa narsaga e'tibor berishga ulgurmagan ham ediki, bosh xizmatchining baland ovozda «Oh!» deganini eshitdi — bu shamol g'uvillaganday eshitildi — va endi uni ham ko'rdi: eshikka eng yaqin turgan bosh xizmatchi qo'lini ochiq og'ziga bosib, go'yo uni ko'rinmas, tinimsiz itarayotgan kuch quvayotganday asta orqaga chekinardi.

paras.en: His mother — in spite of the chief clerk's presence she stood there with her hair still undone from the night and sticking up — first looked at his father with her hands clasped, then took two steps towards Gregor and sank to the floor in the middle of her skirts, which spread out all around her, her face sunk so low on her breast that it could not be seen at all. His father clenched his fist with a hostile expression, as if he wanted to push Gregor back into his room, then looked around the living room uncertainly, covered his eyes with his hands and wept so that his powerful chest shook.
paras.uz: Onasi — bosh xizmatchi borligiga qaramay, sochlari tundan beri yoyilgan, tikka-tikka holda turardi — avval qo'llarini qovushtirib otasiga qaradi, keyin Gregor tomon ikki qadam tashladi va atrofiga yoyilgan yubkalari o'rtasida yerga cho'kdi; yuzi ko'kragiga shunday egilgan ediki, umuman ko'rinmasdi. Otasi go'yo Gregorni xonasiga itarib kiritmoqchi bo'lganday dushmanona qiyofada mushtini tugdi, so'ng ishonchsizlik bilan mehmonxonaga ko'z yugurtirdi, keyin qo'llari bilan ko'zlarini to'sib, baquvvat ko'kragi silkinguncha yig'ladi.

paras.en: Gregor did not come into the room at all, but leaned from inside against the half of the door that was bolted, so that only half of his body could be seen, and above it his head, tilted to one side, with which he peered across at the others. Meanwhile it had become much lighter. On the other side of the street a section of the endless grey-black building opposite stood out clearly — it was a hospital — with its regular windows cutting harshly through the front. The rain was still falling, but only in large drops that could each be seen separately and seemed to be thrown down to the earth one by one.
paras.uz: Gregor xonaga umuman kirmadi, balki eshikning qulflangan tavaqasiga ichkaridan suyandi; shu bois tanasining faqat yarmi va uning tepasida yonboshga egilgan boshi ko'rinardi, u shu bosh bilan boshqalarga mo'ralab turardi. Bu orada ancha yorishib qolgan edi. Ko'chaning narigi tomonida ro'parada turgan cheksiz kulrang-qora binoning bir qismi aniq ko'rinib turardi — bu kasalxona edi — uning old tomonini qattiq yorib o'tgan bir xil derazalari bor edi. Yomg'ir hali ham yog'ardi, lekin endi faqat har biri alohida ko'rinadigan va go'yo yerga bittalab otilayotgan yirik tomchilar bilan.

paras.en: There were far too many breakfast dishes on the table, because for his father breakfast was the most important meal of the day, which he dragged out for hours while reading various newspapers. On the wall directly opposite hung a photograph of Gregor from his time in the army, showing him as a lieutenant, his hand on his sword, smiling carefree, demanding respect for his bearing and his uniform. The door to the hall was open, and since the front door was open too, one could see out onto the landing and the top of the stairs going down.
paras.uz: Stolda nonushta idishlari haddan tashqari ko'p edi, chunki otasi uchun nonushta kunning eng muhim taomi bo'lib, u turli gazetalarni o'qiy-o'qiy uni soatlab cho'zardi. Ro'paradagi devorda Gregorning harbiy xizmat davridagi surati osig'liq edi: unda u leytenant sifatida, qo'li qilichida, beg'am jilmayib, o'z qaddi-qomati va formasiga hurmat talab qilib turardi. Dahlizga olib chiqadigan eshik ochiq edi, kvartira eshigi ham ochiq bo'lgani uchun zinapoya maydonchasi va pastga tushadigan zinaning boshi ko'rinib turardi.

paras.en: “Well,” said Gregor, well aware that he was the only one who had kept calm, “I'll get dressed right away, pack up the samples and leave. Will you, will you let me go? Well, sir, you can see I'm not stubborn and I like to work; travelling is hard, but I couldn't live without it. Where are you going, sir? To the office? Yes? Will you report everything truthfully? A man can be unable to work for a moment, but that is exactly the right time to remember his past achievements and to consider that later, once the obstacle is out of the way, he will certainly work all the harder and with more concentration. I owe so much to the boss, you know that very well.
paras.uz: «Xo'sh, — dedi Gregor, xotirjamligini saqlab qolgan yagona odam o'zi ekanini yaxshi anglab, — hozir kiyinaman, namunalarni yig'aman va jo'nayman. Menga ketishga, ketishga ruxsat berasizlarmi? Ko'ryapsizmi, janob, men o'jar emasman va ishlashni yaxshi ko'raman; safar og'ir, lekin men safarsiz yashay olmasdim. Qayoqqa ketyapsiz, janob? Idoragami? Ha? Hammasini to'g'ri aytib berasizmi? Odam bir lahza ishlay olmay qolishi mumkin, lekin aynan shunda uning avvalgi yutuqlarini eslash va keyinchalik, to'siq olib tashlangach, u, albatta, yanada tirishqoqroq va jamlanibroq ishlashini o'ylash kerak. Axir men xo'jayindan qanchalik qarzdorman, buni siz juda yaxshi bilasiz.

paras.en: On the other hand, I have to worry about my parents and my sister. I'm in a tight spot, but I'll work my way out of it again. Just don't make it harder for me than it already is. Take my side at the office! People don't like travelling salesmen, I know. They think he earns a fortune and has a fine life on top of it. They simply have no particular reason to think this prejudice through. But you, sir, you have a better overview of the situation than the rest of the staff, even — between you and me — a better overview than the boss himself, who, as the owner of the business, can easily let his judgement be turned against an employee.
paras.uz: Boshqa tomondan, ota-onam va singlim tashvishi bor. Men qiyin ahvolga tushib qoldim, lekin yana undan chiqib ketaman. Faqat buni hozirgidan ham qiyinlashtirmang. Idorada mening tomonimni oling! Sayyor agentlarni yoqtirishmaydi, bilaman. Uni katta pul topadi va shu bilan birga rohat qilib yashaydi, deb o'ylashadi. Bu xurofot haqida yaxshilab o'ylab ko'rishga hech kimning alohida sababi yo'q. Lekin siz, janob, siz vaziyatni boshqa xodimlardan yaxshiroq ko'rasiz, hatto — oramizda qolsin — xo'jayinning o'zidan ham yaxshiroq: u korxona egasi sifatida o'z hukmini osongina xodim zarariga burib yuborishi mumkin.

paras.en: You also know very well that a travelling salesman, who is away from the office almost all year, can so easily become the victim of gossip, accidents and groundless complaints, against which he cannot possibly defend himself, because he usually knows nothing about them, and only when he comes home exhausted at the end of a trip does he feel the bad consequences in his own body, without being able to trace their causes any more. Sir, don't go away without saying a word to show me that you agree with me at least a little!”
paras.uz: Yana siz yaxshi bilasizki, deyarli yil bo'yi idoradan tashqarida yuradigan agent osongina g'iybatlar, tasodiflar va asossiz shikoyatlar qurboni bo'lishi mumkin; u ulardan o'zini himoya qila olmaydi, chunki ko'pincha ular haqida hech narsa bilmaydi va faqat safardan holdan toyib qaytgandagina, sabablarini endi aniqlab bo'lmaydigan yomon oqibatlarini o'z jonida his qiladi. Janob, menga hech bo'lmasa qisman haq ekanimni ko'rsatadigan biror so'z aytmay ketmang!»

paras.en: But at Gregor's very first words the chief clerk had already turned away, and he only looked back at Gregor over his twitching shoulder, with his lips curled. And during Gregor's speech he did not stand still for a moment but moved away towards the door, without taking his eyes off Gregor, but very gradually, as if there were some secret ban on leaving the room. He was already in the hall, and from the sudden movement with which he pulled his foot out of the living room for the last time, one might have thought he had just burned the sole of his foot. In the hall, however, he stretched his right hand far out towards the stairs, as if some truly heavenly salvation were waiting for him there.
paras.uz: Lekin bosh xizmatchi Gregorning birinchi so'zlaridanoq yuzini burib olgan va faqat uchib turgan yelkasi osha lablarini burishtirib Gregorga qarab qo'yardi. Gregor gapirayotgan paytda u bir lahza ham joyida turmadi, Gregordan ko'zini uzmay eshik tomon chekinib bordi, lekin go'yo xonani tark etishni yashirin ta'qiq bor-day juda sekin. U allaqachon dahlizda edi va mehmonxonadan oyog'ini oxirgi marta to'satdan tortib olishini ko'rgan odam tovonini hozirgina kuydirib olgan, deb o'ylashi mumkin edi. Dahlizda esa u o'ng qo'lini zinapoya tomon uzoqqa cho'zdi, go'yo u yerda uni chinakam ilohiy najot kutayotganday.

paras.en: Gregor realised that he must on no account let the chief clerk leave in this mood, if his position at the firm was not to be put in the greatest danger. His parents did not understand all this so well. Over the long years they had become convinced that Gregor was provided for in this firm for life, and besides, they were now so busy with their immediate worries that they had lost all foresight. But Gregor had that foresight. The chief clerk had to be held back, calmed down, persuaded and finally won over; the future of Gregor and his family depended on it! If only his sister had been there! She was clever; she had already cried while Gregor was still lying calmly on his back.
paras.uz: Gregor tushundiki, agar firmadagi o'rnini o'ta xavf ostiga qo'ymoqchi bo'lmasa, bosh xizmatchini bu kayfiyatda hech qachon ketishiga yo'l qo'ymasligi kerak. Ota-onasi bularning hammasini unchalik yaxshi tushunmasdi. Uzoq yillar davomida ular Gregor bu firmada umrbod ta'minlangan, degan ishonchga kelgan edilar, buning ustiga endi shu lahzadagi tashvishlar bilan shunchalik band ediki, oldindan ko'ra bilish qobiliyatini butunlay yo'qotgandilar. Gregorda esa bu qobiliyat bor edi. Bosh xizmatchini to'xtatish, tinchlantirish, ishontirish va oxiri o'z tomoniga og'dirish kerak edi; axir Gregor va oilasining kelajagi shunga bog'liq edi! Qani endi singlisi shu yerda bo'lsa! U aqlli edi; Gregor hali xotirjam chalqancha yotgan paytdayoq yig'lagan edi.

paras.en: And the chief clerk, who was fond of the ladies, would certainly have let her guide him; she would have shut the front door and talked him out of his fright in the hall. But his sister was not there, and Gregor had to act himself. Without thinking that he did not yet know what he was now able to do in terms of movement, and without thinking that his speech had possibly — no, probably — once again not been understood, he let go of the door, pushed himself through the opening and tried to go to the chief clerk, who was already holding on to the banister on the landing with both hands in a ridiculous way. But as he looked for something to hold on to, he immediately fell with a little cry onto his many little legs.
paras.uz: Ayollarni yaxshi ko'radigan bosh xizmatchi esa, albatta, uning gapiga kirgan bo'lardi; u kvartira eshigini yopib, dahlizda uning qo'rquvini gapirib-gapirib yo'qotgan bo'lardi. Lekin singlisi u yerda yo'q edi, Gregor o'zi harakat qilishi kerak edi. Hozir qanday harakatlana olishini hali umuman bilmasligini ham, nutqini, ehtimol — yo'q, katta ehtimol bilan — yana tushunishmaganini ham o'ylamay, u eshik tavaqasini qo'yib yubordi; tirqishdan o'tib, zinapoya maydonchasidagi panjaradan kulgili tarzda ikki qo'li bilan mahkam ushlab turgan bosh xizmatchi tomon bormoqchi bo'ldi; lekin tayanch izlab, darhol kichkina qichqiriq bilan o'zining ko'p mitti oyoqlari ustiga yiqildi.

paras.en: Hardly had this happened than he felt, for the first time that morning, a sense of physical well-being. His little legs had firm ground beneath them; they obeyed him completely, as he noticed to his joy; they were even eager to carry him wherever he wanted to go; and he already believed that the final end of all his suffering was close at hand. But at that very moment, as he lay on the floor rocking with suppressed movement, not far from his mother and directly opposite her, she, who had seemed so completely lost in herself, suddenly jumped up with her arms stretched wide and her fingers spread and cried: “Help, for God's sake, help!”
paras.uz: Bu sodir bo'lishi bilanoq u o'sha tong birinchi marta jismoniy yengillikni his qildi. Mitti oyoqlari ostida mustahkam zamin bor edi; ular, u xursand bo'lib payqaganidek, unga butunlay bo'ysunardi; hatto uni xohlagan joyiga olib borishga intilardi; va u barcha azoblarining batamom tugashi yaqin qolgan, deb ishona boshladi. Lekin xuddi o'sha lahzada, u onasidan unchalik uzoq bo'lmagan joyda, uning ro'parasida bosib turgan harakatdan tebranib yerda yotganida, o'z xayollariga butunlay g'arq bo'lganday ko'ringan onasi birdaniga qo'llarini keng yozib, barmoqlarini yoyib, sakrab turdi va qichqirdi: «Yordam bering, Xudo haqqi, yordam bering!»

paras.en: She held her head bent as if she wanted to see Gregor better, but at the same time, contradicting this, she ran senselessly backwards. She had forgotten that the laid table was behind her; when she reached it she sat down on it hastily, as if absent-minded, and did not seem to notice at all that beside her coffee was pouring in a full stream from the big overturned pot onto the carpet.
paras.uz: U Gregorni yaxshiroq ko'rmoqchi bo'lganday boshini egib turdi, lekin bunga zid ravishda ma'nosiz orqaga yugurdi; orqasida dasturxon tuzalgan stol turganini unutgan edi; unga yetib kelgach, xayoli parishonday shoshib uning ustiga o'tirib oldi va yonida ag'darilgan katta qahvadondan qahva gilamga sharillab oqayotganini umuman sezmaganday edi.

paras.en: “Mother, Mother,” Gregor said softly, and looked up at her. For a moment the chief clerk had gone completely out of his mind; on the other hand, at the sight of the flowing coffee he could not stop himself from snapping his jaws at the empty air several times. At this his mother screamed again, fled from the table and fell into the arms of his father, who was hurrying towards her. But Gregor had no time for his parents now; the chief clerk was already on the stairs. With his chin on the banister he was looking back for the last time. Gregor took a run in order to be as sure as possible of catching him; the chief clerk must have sensed something, because he leapt down several steps and disappeared. “Huh!” he still shouted, and it rang through the whole staircase.
paras.uz: «Onajon, onajon», — dedi Gregor sekin va unga yuqoriga qaradi. Bir lahzaga bosh xizmatchi uning xayolidan butunlay chiqib ketdi; buning o'rniga oqayotgan qahvani ko'rib, jag'lari bilan bir necha marta havoni qapishdan o'zini tiyolmadi. Bundan onasi yana qichqirib, stoldan qochdi va unga qarab shoshib kelayotgan otasining quchog'iga yiqildi. Lekin Gregorning hozir ota-onasiga vaqti yo'q edi; bosh xizmatchi allaqachon zinapoyada edi. U iyagini panjaraga tirab, oxirgi marta orqasiga qarab turardi. Gregor uni albatta quvib yetish uchun yugurib keldi; bosh xizmatchi nimanidir sezgan bo'lsa kerak, chunki bir necha zinadan sakrab o'tib, g'oyib bo'ldi. Lekin u «Uh!» deb qichqirdi va bu butun zinapoya bo'ylab yangradi.

paras.en: Unfortunately this flight of the chief clerk seemed to throw his father, who until then had been relatively composed, into complete confusion. Instead of running after the chief clerk himself, or at least not hindering Gregor from following him, he grabbed with his right hand the chief clerk's walking stick, which he had left on a chair together with his hat and coat, took a large newspaper from the table with his left, and, stamping his feet, set about driving Gregor back into his room by waving the stick and the newspaper. None of Gregor's pleading helped; none of his pleading was even understood. However humbly he turned his head, his father only stamped harder.
paras.uz: Afsuski, bosh xizmatchining bu qochishi shu paytgacha nisbatan o'zini tutib turgan otasini butunlay sarosimaga solib qo'ydi. U o'zi bosh xizmatchi ortidan yugurish yoki hech bo'lmasa Gregorning quvishiga xalaqit bermaslik o'rniga, o'ng qo'li bilan bosh xizmatchining shlyapasi va paltosi bilan birga kresloda qoldirib ketgan hassasini oldi, chap qo'li bilan stoldan katta gazetani oldi va oyoqlarini dupurlatib, hassa va gazetani silkitgancha Gregorni xonasiga haydashga kirishdi. Gregorning hech qanday yolvorishi yordam bermadi, hech bir yolvorishi tushunilmadi ham; u boshini qanchalik itoatkorona burmasin, otasi faqat qattiqroq dupurlatardi.

paras.en: Over on the other side, in spite of the cool weather, his mother had flung open a window, and leaning out she pressed her face into her hands far outside the window. A strong draught formed between the street and the staircase; the curtains flew up, the newspapers on the table rustled, and single pages blew across the floor. Relentlessly his father pushed on, making hissing noises like a savage. But Gregor had no practice at all in walking backwards, and it really went very slowly. If only Gregor had been allowed to turn round, he would have been in his room at once, but he was afraid of making his father impatient with the time it would take to turn, and at any moment the stick in his father's hand threatened him with a deadly blow on the back or on the head.
paras.uz: Narigi tomonda, salqin havoga qaramay, onasi derazani lang ochib yuborgan va tashqariga engashib, yuzini deraza tashqarisida kaftlari orasiga bosib turardi. Ko'cha bilan zinapoya o'rtasida kuchli yel paydo bo'ldi, deraza pardalari ko'tarilib uchdi, stoldagi gazetalar shitirladi, ayrim varaqlar polda uchib yurdi. Otasi shafqatsiz ravishda itarar va yovvoyidek vishillardi. Gregorning esa orqaga yurishda hech qanday mashqi yo'q edi, bu chindan ham juda sekin borardi. Agar unga burilishga ruxsat berilganda, u darhol xonasida bo'lardi, lekin burilish uchun ketadigan vaqt bilan otasining sabrini tugatishdan qo'rqardi, otasining qo'lidagi hassa esa har lahza uning orqasi yoki boshiga halokatli zarba berishi mumkin edi.

paras.en: In the end, however, Gregor had no other choice, because he noticed with horror that when walking backwards he could not even keep in one direction. And so, with constant anxious glances at his father, he began to turn round as quickly as possible, though in reality very slowly. Perhaps his father noticed his good intentions, because he did not disturb him in this; he even directed the turning from a distance now and then with the tip of his stick. If only it hadn't been for his father's unbearable hissing! It made Gregor lose his head completely. He had almost turned all the way round when, always listening to this hissing, he even made a mistake and turned back a little way again.
paras.uz: Ammo oxiri Gregorga boshqa iloj qolmadi, chunki u orqaga yurganda hatto yo'nalishni ushlab tura olmasligini dahshat bilan payqadi. Shu bois u otasiga tinimsiz xavotir bilan qarab, imkon qadar tez, aslida esa juda sekin burila boshladi. Balki otasi uning yaxshi niyatini sezgandir, chunki bunda unga xalaqit bermadi, hatto vaqti-vaqti bilan hassasining uchi bilan uzoqdan burilishni boshqarib turdi. Qani endi otasining bu chidab bo'lmas vishillashi bo'lmasa! Gregor shundan butunlay esini yo'qotdi. U deyarli butunlay burilib bo'lgan ediki, doim shu vishillashga quloq solib, hatto adashib, yana bir oz orqaga burilib ketdi.

paras.en: But when at last he happily had his head in front of the doorway, it turned out that his body was too wide to get through without help. In his present state, of course, it did not even remotely occur to his father to open the other half of the door so as to make a wide enough passage for Gregor. His fixed idea was simply that Gregor must get back into his room as quickly as possible. He would never have allowed the complicated preparations Gregor needed to stand up and perhaps get through the door that way. Instead, as if there were no obstacle, he now drove Gregor forward with a particular noise; behind Gregor it no longer sounded like the voice of just one single father. Now it really was no joke any more, and Gregor forced himself — whatever might happen — into the doorway.
paras.uz: Lekin nihoyat boshi eshik tirqishi oldiga baxtli ravishda yetib kelganida, tanasi bemalol o'tish uchun juda keng ekani ma'lum bo'ldi. Hozirgi ahvolida otasining xayoliga, albatta, Gregor uchun yetarli yo'l ochish maqsadida eshikning ikkinchi tavaqasini ochish degan fikr kelmasdi ham. Uning miyasiga o'rnashib olgan yagona fikr — Gregor imkon qadar tezroq xonasiga kirishi kerak edi. Gregorga tik turib, balki shu tarzda eshikdan o'tishi uchun kerak bo'lgan murakkab tayyorgarlikka u hech qachon yo'l qo'ymasdi. Aksincha, go'yo hech qanday to'siq yo'qday, u endi Gregorni alohida shovqin bilan oldinga haydardi; Gregorning orqasidan eshitilayotgan ovoz endi bitta otaning ovoziga o'xshamasdi. Endi chindan ham hazilga o'rin qolmagan edi va Gregor — nima bo'lsa bo'lsin — eshikka suqildi.

paras.en: One side of his body lifted up; he lay at an angle in the doorway; one of his flanks was rubbed completely raw, and ugly stains were left on the white door. Soon he was stuck fast and could no longer have moved by himself; the little legs on one side hung trembling up in the air, and those on the other side were painfully pressed against the floor — then his father gave him a hard shove from behind, which was now truly a release, and he flew, bleeding heavily, far into his room. The door was slammed shut with the stick, and then at last there was silence.
paras.uz: Tanasining bir tomoni ko'tarildi, u eshik tirqishida qiyshayib yotib qoldi, bir biqini butunlay shilinib, oq eshikda xunuk dog'lar qoldi; tez orada u qisilib qoldi va o'zi qimirlay olmasdi: bir tomondagi mitti oyoqlari havoda titrab osilib turar, boshqa tomondagilari esa og'riq bilan polga bosilgan edi — shunda otasi orqadan unga endi chinakam najot bo'lgan kuchli turtki berdi va u qattiq qon oqizgancha xonasining ichkarisiga uchib kirdi. Eshik hassa bilan yopib qo'yildi, keyin nihoyat jimjitlik cho'kdi.

That was a great encouragement for Gregor.
