chapters.title: Grete Brings Food
chapters.recap_uz: Gregor kechqurun uyg'onadi. Sevimli sutini endi yoqtirmaydi. Singlisi Grete unga turli ovqatlar olib kelib, nimani yeyishini sinab ko'radi: u faqat aynigan narsalarni yeydi. Gregor divan ostida yashirinadi va oilaning gaplarini tinglab, ularning ahvolini bilib oladi.

paras.en: It was not until dusk that Gregor woke from his heavy, almost unconscious sleep. He would certainly have woken up not much later even without being disturbed, because he felt sufficiently rested and had slept enough, but it seemed to him that he had been woken by a quick footstep and the careful closing of the door to the hall. The light from the electric streetlamps lay pale here and there on the ceiling and on the higher parts of the furniture, but down where Gregor was it was dark.
paras.uz: Gregor og'ir, hushsizlikka o'xshash uyqusidan faqat shom paytida uyg'ondi. U hech kim bezovta qilmaganida ham, albatta, ko'p o'tmay uyg'onardi, chunki o'zini yetarlicha dam olgan va to'yib uxlaganday his qilardi; lekin unga go'yo shoshqin qadam va dahlizga ochiladigan eshikning ehtiyotkorlik bilan yopilgani uyg'otganday tuyuldi. Elektr tramvayining nuri shift va mebellarning yuqori qismlariga u yer-bu yerda xira tushib turardi, lekin pastda, Gregor yotgan joyda qorong'i edi.

paras.en: Slowly, still clumsily feeling his way with his antennae, which he was only now beginning to appreciate, he pushed himself towards the door to see what had happened there. His left side seemed to be one long, unpleasantly tight scar, and he really had to limp on his two rows of legs. One of his little legs, by the way, had been badly injured in the course of the morning's events — it was almost a miracle that only one had been injured — and it dragged along lifelessly behind.
paras.uz: U hozirgina qadrlay boshlagan mo'ylovlari bilan hali beo'xshov paypaslab, u yerda nima bo'lganini bilish uchun eshik tomon asta surildi. Chap yonboshi bitta uzun, yoqimsiz tortishib turgan chandiqqa o'xshardi va u ikki qator oyog'ida rostakamiga oqsoqlanib yurishga majbur edi. Aytgancha, mitti oyoqlaridan biri ertalabki voqealar paytida qattiq jarohatlangan edi — faqat bittasi jarohatlangani deyarli mo'jiza edi — va jonsiz holda orqada sudralib kelardi.

paras.en: Only when he reached the door did he notice what had actually drawn him there: it was the smell of something to eat. For there stood a bowl filled with sweet milk, in which little pieces of white bread were floating. He almost laughed with joy, because he was even hungrier than in the morning, and he immediately dipped his head into the milk almost up to his eyes. But he soon drew it back in disappointment. Not only did eating cause him difficulty because of his sore left side — and he could only eat if his whole body worked along, panting — but on top of that he did not like the milk at all, though it had always been his favourite drink, which was surely why his sister had put it there. In fact he turned away from the bowl almost with disgust and crawled back into the middle of the room.
paras.uz: Faqat eshik oldiga kelgandagina uni u yerga aslida nima tortib kelganini payqadi: bu qandaydir yegulikning hidi edi. U yerda ichida mayda oq non bo'laklari suzib yurgan shirin sut to'la tog'ora turardi. U xursandligidan kulib yuborishiga oz qoldi, chunki ertalabkidan ham qattiqroq och edi va darhol boshini deyarli ko'zlarigacha sutga botirdi. Lekin tez orada hafsalasi pir bo'lib, uni yana tortib oldi. Nafaqat og'riyotgan chap yonboshi tufayli ovqatlanish unga qiyin edi — u faqat butun tanasi pishillab ishlagandagina yeya olardi — balki ilgari sevimli ichimligi bo'lgan va shuning uchun singlisi qo'ygan bo'lsa kerak bo'lgan sut unga umuman yoqmadi. U hatto deyarli jirkanib tog'oradan yuz o'girdi va xona o'rtasiga sudralib qaytdi.

paras.en: In the living room, as Gregor saw through the crack in the door, the gaslight had been lit. But while at this time of day his father usually read the afternoon newspaper aloud to his mother, and sometimes to his sister too, now not a sound could be heard. Well, perhaps this reading aloud, which his sister had always told him and written to him about, had gone out of fashion recently. But all around it was so quiet too, even though the flat was certainly not empty. “What a quiet life the family leads,” Gregor said to himself, and, as he stared rigidly into the darkness, he felt great pride that he had been able to provide his parents and his sister with such a life in such a lovely flat. But what if now all the peace, all the comfort, all the contentment were to come to a terrible end? So as not to lose himself in such thoughts, Gregor preferred to start moving, and he crawled up and down the room.
paras.uz: Gregor eshik tirqishidan ko'rganidek, mehmonxonada gaz chirog'i yoqilgan edi, lekin odatda kunning shu paytida otasi tushdan keyin chiqadigan gazetani onasiga, ba'zan singlisiga ham baland ovozda o'qib berardi, endi esa hech qanday tovush eshitilmasdi. Balki singlisi unga doim aytib, xatlarida yozib turadigan bu o'qib berish odati so'nggi paytlarda butunlay yo'qolgandir. Lekin atrofda ham juda jimjit edi, holbuki kvartira bo'sh emasligi aniq edi. «Oila qanday tinch hayot kechiradi-a», — dedi o'ziga Gregor va qorong'ilikka tikilib qarab turib, ota-onasi va singlisiga shunday chiroyli kvartirada shunday hayotni ta'minlay olganidan katta faxr his qildi. Ammo endi butun osoyishtalik, butun farovonlik, butun mamnunlik dahshatli tarzda tugab qolsa-chi? Bunday fikrlarga berilib ketmaslik uchun Gregor harakat qilishni ma'qul ko'rdi va xonada u yoqdan-bu yoqqa sudralib yurdi.

paras.en: Once during the long evening one side door was opened to a small crack and quickly shut again, and once the other; someone obviously felt the need to come in but also had too many doubts. Gregor now stopped right by the living-room door, determined to get the hesitant visitor to come in somehow, or at least to find out who it was; but now the door was not opened again and Gregor waited in vain. Early that morning, when the doors were locked, everyone had wanted to come in to him; now that he had opened one door and the others had evidently been opened during the day, no one came any more, and the keys were now in the locks on the outside.
paras.uz: Uzoq oqshom davomida bir marta bir yon eshik, bir marta boshqasi kichik tirqish qadar ochilib, tezda yana yopildi; kimdir ichkariga kirishni istagan, lekin ikkilanishlari ham juda ko'p edi. Endi Gregor ikkilanayotgan mehmonni qanday bo'lmasin ichkariga kiritishga yoki hech bo'lmasa kimligini bilishga qaror qilib, mehmonxona eshigi yonida to'xtadi; lekin eshik boshqa ochilmadi va Gregor bekorga kutdi. Ertalab, eshiklar qulflangan paytda, hamma uning oldiga kirmoqchi edi; endi esa u bir eshikni ochgan, boshqalari ham kunduzi ochilgan bo'lsa-da, hech kim kelmasdi, kalitlar esa endi tashqaridan qulfga suqib qo'yilgan edi.

paras.en: Only late at night was the light in the living room put out, and now it was easy to tell that his parents and his sister had stayed awake until then, because, as could clearly be heard, all three were now moving away on tiptoe. Now certainly no one would come in to Gregor until the morning; so he had a long time to think, undisturbed, about how he should rearrange his life now. But the high, empty room, in which he was forced to lie flat on the floor, frightened him, without his being able to find out why, for it was the room he had lived in for five years.
paras.uz: Faqat tun yarmidan oshgandagina mehmonxonadagi chiroq o'chirildi va endi ota-onasi va singlisi shu paytgacha uxlamay o'tirganini bilish oson edi, chunki uchalasi ham oyoq uchida uzoqlashayotgani aniq eshitilardi. Endi tonggacha Gregorning oldiga hech kim kirmasligi aniq edi; demak, unda hayotini endi qanday qilib qaytadan tartibga solish haqida xotirjam o'ylash uchun ko'p vaqt bor edi. Lekin u polda yassi yotishga majbur bo'lgan baland, bo'sh xona uni qo'rqitardi va buning sababini u topa olmasdi, axir bu besh yildan beri yashab kelgan xonasi edi.

paras.en: And with a half-unconscious turn, and not without a slight feeling of shame, he hurried under the sofa, where, although his back was a little squashed and he could no longer lift his head, he immediately felt very comfortable, and only regretted that his body was too wide to fit completely under the sofa. He stayed there the whole night. He spent part of it half asleep, constantly startled awake by hunger, and part of it in worries and vague hopes, which all led to the conclusion that for the time being he must keep calm and, through patience and the greatest consideration, make bearable for the family the unpleasantness that he was, after all, forced to cause them in his present condition.
paras.uz: Va yarim ongsiz holda burilib, biroz uyalib, u divan ostiga shoshildi; u yerda orqasi biroz siqilgan va boshini endi ko'tarolmasa ham, o'zini darhol juda qulay his qildi, faqat tanasi divan ostiga butunlay sig'ish uchun juda keng ekanidan afsuslandi. U tun bo'yi o'sha yerda qoldi. Tunning bir qismini ochlik qayta-qayta cho'chitib uyg'otgan yarim uyquda, bir qismini esa tashvishlar va noaniq umidlar bilan o'tkazdi; ular hammasi bitta xulosaga olib kelardi: hozircha u o'zini tinch tutishi, sabr va oilaga nisbatan eng katta e'tibor bilan hozirgi ahvolida ularga majburan keltirayotgan noqulayliklarni chidasa bo'ladigan holga keltirishi kerak.

paras.en: Early the next morning — it was still almost night — Gregor had a chance to test the strength of the decisions he had just made, for his sister, almost fully dressed, opened the door from the hall and looked in eagerly. She did not find him at once, but when she noticed him under the sofa — God, he had to be somewhere, he couldn't have flown away — she was so frightened that, unable to control herself, she slammed the door shut again from outside. But as if she regretted her behaviour, she opened the door again immediately and came in on tiptoe, as if she were visiting someone seriously ill, or even a stranger.
paras.uz: Ertasi kuni tong saharda — hali deyarli tun edi — Gregorga hozirgina qilgan qarorlarining kuchini sinab ko'rish imkoni tug'ildi, chunki deyarli to'liq kiyingan singlisi dahliz tomondan eshikni ochib, hayajon bilan ichkariga qaradi. U uni darhol topa olmadi, lekin divan ostida ko'rganida — Xudoyim, u qayerdadir bo'lishi kerak-ku, uchib ketolmaydi-ku — shunchalik qo'rqib ketdiki, o'zini tutolmay, eshikni tashqaridan yana qarsillatib yopdi. Lekin go'yo qilgan ishidan pushaymon bo'lganday, darhol eshikni yana ochdi va og'ir kasal yoki hatto begona odam oldiga kirganday oyoq uchida ichkari kirdi.

paras.en: Gregor had pushed his head forward to the very edge of the sofa and was watching her. Would she notice that he had left the milk, and by no means because he was not hungry, and would she bring in some other food that suited him better? If she did not do it of her own accord, he would rather starve than draw her attention to it, although in fact he felt an enormous urge to shoot out from under the sofa, throw himself at his sister's feet and beg her for something good to eat. But his sister immediately noticed with surprise the bowl, which was still full except for a little milk spilt around it. She picked it up at once — not with her bare hands, but with a rag — and carried it out.
paras.uz: Gregor boshini divanning eng chetigacha surib, uni kuzatib turardi. U sutni ichmay qoldirganini — va bu aslo ochlik yo'qligidan emasligini — payqarmikan va unga ko'proq mos keladigan boshqa ovqat olib kelarmikan? Agar o'zi shunday qilmasa, u bunga uning e'tiborini tortgandan ko'ra ochdan o'lishni afzal ko'rardi, garchi aslida divan ostidan otilib chiqib, singlisining oyoqlariga o'zini tashlash va undan biror yaxshi yegulik so'rashga juda-juda intilsa ham. Lekin singlisi atrofiga ozgina sut to'kilgan, hali ham to'la tog'orani darhol hayron bo'lib payqadi va uni darhol — yalang'och qo'li bilan emas, latta bilan — ko'tarib olib chiqib ketdi.

paras.en: Gregor was extremely curious to see what she would bring instead, and he thought of all kinds of possibilities. But he could never have guessed what his sister, in her kindness, actually did. To test his taste, she brought him a whole selection, all spread out on an old newspaper. There were old, half-rotten vegetables; bones from last night's supper, surrounded by white sauce that had gone solid; a few raisins and almonds; a cheese that Gregor had declared inedible two days before; a dry piece of bread, a piece of bread spread with butter, and a piece of bread spread with butter and salted. Besides all this, she put down the bowl, probably meant for Gregor once and for all, into which she had poured water.
paras.uz: Gregor uning o'rniga nima olib kelishini bilishga juda qiziqardi va bu haqda turli-tuman narsalarni o'yladi. Lekin singlisi o'z mehribonligi bilan aslida nima qilganini u hech qachon taxmin qila olmasdi. U uning ta'bini sinash uchun eski gazeta ustiga yoyilgan bir qancha tanlov olib keldi. U yerda eski, yarim chirigan sabzavotlar; kechki ovqatdan qolgan, qotib qolgan oq sous bilan qoplangan suyaklar; bir nechta mayiz va bodom; Gregor ikki kun oldin yeb bo'lmaydi degan pishloq; quruq non, sariyog' surtilgan non va sariyog' surtilib tuz sepilgan non bor edi. Bularning barchasiga qo'shimcha qilib, u, ehtimol, endi bir umrga Gregorniki bo'lib qolgan tog'orani qo'ydi va unga suv quydi.

paras.en: And out of tactfulness, knowing that Gregor would not eat in front of her, she left very quickly and even turned the key, just so that Gregor would know he could make himself as comfortable as he liked. Gregor's little legs whirred as he now went to eat. His wounds, by the way, must already have healed completely; he no longer felt any difficulty. He was amazed at this and thought of how, more than a month ago, he had cut his finger very slightly with a knife, and how that wound had still hurt quite a lot only the day before yesterday. “Am I less sensitive now?” he thought, and he was already sucking greedily at the cheese, which had attracted him immediately and strongly, more than any of the other foods.
paras.uz: Va nozik tabiatliligidan, Gregor uning oldida ovqat yemasligini bilgani uchun, u shoshib chiqib ketdi va hatto Gregor o'zini xohlaganicha erkin his qilishi mumkinligini bilsin deb kalitni ham burab qo'ydi. Gregor ovqatga yo'l olganida, mitti oyoqlari vizillab ketdi. Aytgancha, jarohatlari ham butunlay bitib ketgan bo'lsa kerak, u endi hech qanday qiyinchilik sezmasdi. U bundan hayron bo'ldi va bir oydan ko'proq vaqt oldin pichoq bilan barmog'ini sal kesib olganini va bu jarohat hali o'tgan kuni ham ancha og'riganini esladi. «Endi sezgirligim kamaydimikan?» — deb o'yladi u va boshqa barcha ovqatlardan ko'ra uni darhol va kuchli tortgan pishloqni ochko'zlik bilan so'ra boshladi.

paras.en: Quickly, one after another, with eyes watering with satisfaction, he ate up the cheese, the vegetables and the sauce. The fresh food, on the other hand, he did not like; he could not even stand its smell, and he even dragged the things he wanted to eat a little further away. He had long since finished everything and was just lying lazily in the same spot when his sister slowly turned the key, as a sign that he should withdraw. That startled him at once, although he was already almost dozing, and he hurried back under the sofa.
paras.uz: Tez-tez, birin-ketin, mamnunlikdan ko'zlari yoshlanib, u pishloqni, sabzavotlarni va sousni yeb tugatdi; yangi ovqatlar esa unga yoqmadi, u hatto ularning hidiga ham chiday olmasdi va yemoqchi bo'lgan narsalarini sal nariroqqa sudrab olib ketdi. U allaqachon hammasini tugatib, shunchaki o'sha joyda dangasalarcha yotgan ediki, singlisi uning yashirinishi kerakligiga ishora qilib, kalitni asta burdi. Garchi deyarli mudrab qolgan bo'lsa ham, bu uni darhol cho'chitib yubordi va u yana divan ostiga shoshildi.

paras.en: But it took great self-control for him to stay under the sofa even for the short time his sister was in the room, because the big meal had made his body swell a little, and he could hardly breathe in that narrow space. With small fits of suffocation, his eyes bulging slightly, he watched his sister, who suspected nothing, sweep up with a broom not only the leftovers but even the food Gregor had not touched at all, as if this too could no longer be used. She hastily emptied everything into a bucket, closed it with a wooden lid and carried it all out. She had hardly turned round when Gregor pulled himself out from under the sofa, stretched and puffed himself up.
paras.uz: Lekin singlisi xonada bo'lgan qisqa vaqt davomida ham divan ostida qolish unga o'zini juda qattiq tutishni talab qildi, chunki mo'l ovqatdan tanasi biroz yumaloqlashib qolgan va u o'sha torlikda arang nafas olardi. Kichik-kichik bo'g'ilish xurujlari ostida, ko'zlari sal bo'rtib, u hech narsadan bexabar singlisining supurgi bilan nafaqat qoldiqlarni, balki Gregor umuman tegmagan ovqatlarni ham, go'yo ular ham endi yaroqsizday, supurib yig'ishtirayotganini kuzatdi. U hammasini shoshib chelakka to'kdi, uni yog'och qopqoq bilan yopdi va hammasini olib chiqib ketdi. U endigina burilgan ediki, Gregor divan ostidan sudralib chiqib, kerishib, shishinib oldi.

paras.en: In this way Gregor now received his food every day: once in the morning, while his parents and the maid were still asleep, and the second time after the family's lunch, for then his parents also slept for a little while, and his sister sent the maid away on some errand. They certainly did not want Gregor to starve either, but perhaps they could not have borne to know more about his eating than what they heard from others; perhaps his sister also wanted to spare them what was perhaps only a small sorrow, because in fact they were suffering enough already.
paras.uz: Shu tarzda Gregor endi har kuni ovqatini olardi: bir marta ertalab, ota-onasi va oqsoch hali uxlab yotganida, ikkinchi marta umumiy tushlikdan keyin, chunki o'shanda ham ota-onasi bir oz uxlardi, oqsochni esa singlisi biror yumush bilan tashqariga jo'natardi. Ular ham, albatta, Gregorning ochdan o'lishini istamasdi, lekin, ehtimol, uning ovqatlanishi haqida eshitganlaridan ortiq narsa bilishga chiday olmasdilar; balki singlisi ularni ozgina bo'lsa ham qayg'udan asramoqchi bo'lgandir, chunki aslida ular shusiz ham yetarlicha azob chekishardi.

paras.en: Gregor could never find out what excuses had been used that first morning to get the doctor and the locksmith out of the flat again, because since he could not be understood, nobody, not even his sister, thought that he could understand the others. So when his sister was in his room, he had to be content with hearing her sighs and her calls to the saints now and then. Only later, when she had got a little used to everything — there could, of course, never be any question of getting completely used to it — did Gregor sometimes catch a remark that was meant kindly or could be understood that way. “He liked it today,” she would say when Gregor had cleared away a good amount of the food, while in the opposite case, which gradually happened more and more often, she used to say almost sadly: “Everything's been left again.”
paras.uz: O'sha birinchi tongda shifokor va chilangarni qanday bahonalar bilan kvartiradan chiqarib yuborishganini Gregor hech qachon bila olmadi, chunki uni tushunishmagani uchun hech kim, hatto singlisi ham, u boshqalarni tushunishi mumkin deb o'ylamasdi. Shuning uchun singlisi uning xonasida bo'lganida, u faqat vaqti-vaqti bilan uning xo'rsinishlari va avliyolarga murojaatlarini eshitish bilan qanoatlanishi kerak edi. Faqat keyinroq, u hammasiga biroz ko'nikkanidan so'ng — to'liq ko'nikish haqida, albatta, hech qachon gap bo'lishi mumkin emasdi — Gregor ba'zan mehribonlik bilan aytilgan yoki shunday tushunish mumkin bo'lgan gapni ilib olardi. «Bugun yoqibdi», — derdi u, Gregor ovqatning ko'p qismini tozalab qo'yganida; aksincha bo'lganida esa — bu borgan sari tez-tez takrorlanardi — deyarli qayg'u bilan: «Yana hammasi qolibdi», — derdi.

paras.en: But while Gregor could not learn any news directly, he overheard a good deal from the neighbouring rooms, and whenever he heard voices, he ran straight to the door in question and pressed his whole body against it. Especially in the early days there was no conversation that was not somehow about him, even if only secretly. For two days, at every meal, there were discussions about how they should behave now; but between meals, too, they talked about the same subject, for there were always at least two members of the family at home, since nobody wanted to stay at home alone and the flat could on no account be left completely empty.
paras.uz: Gregor bevosita hech qanday yangilik bila olmasa-da, qo'shni xonalardan ko'p narsani eshitib olardi va qayerdan ovoz eshitsa, darhol o'sha eshikka yugurib borib, butun tanasi bilan unga yopishib olardi. Ayniqsa dastlabki paytlarda biror suhbat yo'q ediki, u qandaydir yo'l bilan, hatto yashirin bo'lsa ham, u haqda bo'lmasin. Ikki kun davomida har bir ovqat paytida endi o'zlarini qanday tutish kerakligi haqida maslahatlar eshitildi; lekin ovqat oralig'ida ham shu mavzuda gaplashishardi, chunki uyda doim kamida oilaning ikki a'zosi bo'lardi: hech kim uyda yolg'iz qolishni istamasdi, kvartirani esa butunlay bo'sh qoldirib bo'lmasdi.

paras.en: On the very first day, too, the maid — it was not quite clear what and how much she knew of what had happened — had begged his mother on her knees to dismiss her at once. And when she said goodbye a quarter of an hour later, she thanked them in tears for her dismissal, as if it were the greatest kindness ever shown to her in that house, and, without anyone asking her to, she swore a terrible oath not to tell anyone even the slightest thing.
paras.uz: Buning ustiga oqsoch birinchi kuniyoq — u sodir bo'lgan voqeadan nimani va qanchalik bilishi unchalik aniq emasdi — onasining oldida tiz cho'kib, uni darhol ishdan bo'shatishni so'radi. Chorak soatdan keyin xayrlashayotganda esa, go'yo bu uyda unga ko'rsatilgan eng katta yaxshilikday, ishdan bo'shatilgani uchun ko'z yoshlari bilan minnatdorchilik bildirdi va hech kim talab qilmasa ham, hech kimga zarracha ham sir ochmaslik haqida dahshatli qasam ichdi.

paras.en: Now his sister had to cook too, together with his mother; admittedly that was not much trouble, because they ate almost nothing. Again and again Gregor heard one of them urging another to eat, in vain, and getting no answer but “Thank you, I've had enough,” or something like it. Perhaps nothing was drunk either. His sister often asked his father whether he would like some beer, and kindly offered to fetch it herself; and when his father said nothing, she said, to remove any hesitation he might have, that she could also send the caretaker's wife for it. But then at last his father said a loud “No,” and nothing more was said about it.
paras.uz: Endi singlisi onasi bilan birga ovqat ham pishirishi kerak edi; to'g'ri, bu unchalik qiyin emasdi, chunki deyarli hech narsa yeyishmasdi. Gregor qayta-qayta birining boshqasini bekorga ovqatlanishga undayotganini va «Rahmat, to'ydim» yoki shunga o'xshash javobdan boshqa javob olmayotganini eshitardi. Balki hech narsa ichishmas ham edi. Singlisi tez-tez otasidan pivo istaysizmi, deb so'rar va uni o'zi olib kelishni samimiy taklif qilardi; otasi jim tursa, uning har qanday ikkilanishini yo'qotish uchun farroshning xotinini ham yuborishi mumkinligini aytardi; lekin keyin otasi oxiri baland ovozda «Yo'q» derdi va bu haqda boshqa gap bo'lmasdi.

His left side seemed to be one long scar.
He turned away from the bowl almost with disgust.

chapters.note_uz: Grete — Gregorga g'amxo'rlik qiladigan yagona odam, lekin uning mehribonligida ham masofa bor: u Gregorni ko'rib qo'rqadi, tog'orani latta bilan ushlaydi. Gregor esa hamon oila haqida o'ylaydi va ularga «noqulaylik tug'dirmaslik» uchun yashirinadi.

chapters.title: The Family's Money
chapters.recap_uz: Gregor otasining yashirin jamg'armasi borligini bilib oladi. U Gretani konservatoriyaga yubormoqchi bo'lganini eslaydi. Endi oila pul topishi kerak. Gregor shift va devorlarda o'rmalashni yaxshi ko'rib qoladi; Grete va onasi xonadagi mebellarni olib chiqmoqchi bo'lishadi, lekin onasi ikkilanadi.

paras.en: In the course of the very first day his father explained the family's whole financial situation and prospects to both his mother and his sister. Now and then he got up from the table and took some receipt or notebook out of the small strongbox he had saved from the collapse of his business five years before. One could hear him unlocking the complicated lock and locking it again after taking out what he was looking for. These explanations of his father's were, in part, the first pleasant thing Gregor had heard since his imprisonment. He had believed that his father had nothing at all left from that business; at least his father had never told him anything different, and Gregor, it is true, had never asked him either.
paras.uz: Birinchi kunning o'zidayoq otasi oilaning butun moliyaviy ahvoli va istiqbollarini onasiga ham, singlisiga ham tushuntirib berdi. Vaqti-vaqti bilan u stoldan turib, besh yil oldin savdo ishi singanida saqlab qolgan kichkina temir sandiqchasidan qandaydir kvitansiya yoki yozuv daftarini olib chiqardi. Uning murakkab qulfni ochib, kerakli narsani olgach yana qulflagani eshitilardi. Otasining bu tushuntirishlari qisman Gregor qamalib qolganidan beri eshitgan birinchi xushxabar edi. U otasiga o'sha savdo ishidan hech narsa qolmagan, deb o'ylardi; hech bo'lmasa otasi unga buning aksini aytmagan edi, to'g'ri, Gregor ham bu haqda so'ramagandi.

paras.en: At that time Gregor's only concern had been to do everything he could to make the family forget as quickly as possible the business disaster that had plunged them all into complete hopelessness. And so he had started working with quite special energy and, almost overnight, had gone from being a junior clerk to a travelling salesman, who of course had very different opportunities for earning money, and whose successes at work were turned at once, in the form of commission, into cash that could be laid on the table at home in front of his astonished and delighted family.
paras.uz: O'shanda Gregorning yagona tashvishi — barchani butunlay umidsizlikka solgan savdo falokatini oila imkon qadar tezroq unutishi uchun bor kuchini sarflash edi. Shuning uchun u o'shanda alohida g'ayrat bilan ishlay boshladi va deyarli bir kechada oddiy kichik xizmatchidan sayyor agentga aylandi; agentning esa pul topish uchun, albatta, butunlay boshqacha imkoniyatlari bor edi va uning ishdagi muvaffaqiyatlari darhol komissiya shaklida naqd pulga aylanardi — bu pulni uyda hayron qolgan va baxtiyor oila oldiga stolga qo'yish mumkin edi.

paras.en: Those had been wonderful times, and they had never been repeated afterwards, at least not with the same splendour, even though Gregor later earned so much money that he was able to cover the expenses of the whole family, and did cover them. They had simply got used to it, both the family and Gregor; they accepted the money gratefully, he handed it over gladly, but there was no longer any special warmth.
paras.uz: Bu ajoyib damlar edi va keyin ular hech qachon, hech bo'lmasa o'sha jilosi bilan, takrorlanmadi, garchi Gregor keyinchalik butun oilaning xarajatlarini ko'tara oladigan darajada pul topgan va ko'targan bo'lsa ham. Shunchaki hamma bunga ko'nikib qolgandi — oila ham, Gregor ham; pulni minnatdorchilik bilan olishar, u ham uni bajonidil berardi, lekin endi alohida iliqlik paydo bo'lmasdi.

paras.en: Only his sister had remained close to Gregor. Unlike Gregor, she loved music very much and could play the violin movingly, and it was his secret plan to send her to the conservatory next year, regardless of the great expense this would involve, which could surely be made up in some other way. During Gregor's short stays in town the conservatory was often mentioned in his conversations with his sister, but always only as a beautiful dream that could not possibly come true, and his parents did not even like to hear these innocent mentions. But Gregor thought about it very seriously and intended to announce it solemnly on Christmas Eve.
paras.uz: Faqat singlisi Gregorga yaqin bo'lib qolgan edi. Gregordan farqli o'laroq, u musiqani juda yaxshi ko'rardi va skripkani ta'sirchan chalardi; Gregorning yashirin rejasi uni kelasi yili, bunga ketadigan katta xarajatlarga qaramay — ularni boshqa yo'l bilan qoplash mumkin edi — konservatoriyaga yuborish edi. Gregor shaharda qisqa muddat bo'lganida singlisi bilan suhbatlarda konservatoriya tez-tez tilga olinardi, lekin har doim faqat amalga oshishi mumkin bo'lmagan go'zal orzu sifatida; ota-onasi esa bu begunoh eslatmalarni eshitishni ham yoqtirmasdi. Lekin Gregor bu haqda juda jiddiy o'ylardi va buni Rojdestvo oqshomida tantanali ravishda e'lon qilmoqchi edi.

paras.en: Thoughts like these, completely useless in his present condition, went through his head while he stuck upright to the door, listening. Sometimes, out of general tiredness, he could not listen any more and let his head bump carelessly against the door, but he immediately held it still again, because even the small noise he had made had been heard next door and had made everyone fall silent. “What's he up to now?” said his father after a while, evidently turning towards the door, and only then was the interrupted conversation gradually taken up again.
paras.uz: Hozirgi ahvolida mutlaqo befoyda bo'lgan bunday fikrlar u eshikka tik yopishib quloq solib turganida xayolidan o'tardi. Ba'zan umumiy charchoqdan u boshqa tinglay olmay qolar va boshini beparvolik bilan eshikka urib olardi, lekin darhol yana uni mahkam tutardi, chunki hatto shu bilan chiqargan kichkina tovushi ham qo'shni xonada eshitilib, hammani jim qilib qo'ygan edi. «U yana nima qilyapti?» — dedi otasi bir ozdan keyin, aftidan eshik tomon o'girilib; shundan keyingina to'xtab qolgan suhbat asta-sekin yana davom etdi.

paras.en: Gregor now learned well enough — for his father tended to repeat himself in his explanations, partly because he himself had not dealt with these things for a long time, and partly because his mother did not understand everything the first time — that in spite of all their misfortune a small sum of money, admittedly a very small one, still remained from the old days, and that the interest, which had not been touched, had made it grow a little in the meantime. Besides that, the money Gregor had brought home every month — he had kept only a few gulden for himself — had not all been used up and had built up into a small amount of capital.
paras.uz: Endi Gregor yetarlicha bilib oldi — chunki otasi tushuntirishlarida ko'pincha gaplarini takrorlardi: qisman o'zi bu ishlar bilan uzoq vaqtdan beri shug'ullanmagani uchun, qisman esa onasi hammasini birinchi marta tushunmagani uchun — barcha baxtsizliklarga qaramay, eski davrdan juda kichik bo'lsa ham bir oz mablag' qolgan ekan va tegilmagan foizlar bu orada uni biroz ko'paytirgan ekan. Bundan tashqari, Gregor har oy uyga olib kelgan pul — o'ziga u bir necha guldengina qoldirardi — to'liq sarflanmagan va kichik bir sarmoyaga aylangan ekan.

paras.en: Behind his door, Gregor nodded eagerly, pleased at this unexpected caution and thrift. Actually, he could have used this extra money to pay off more of his father's debt to the boss, and the day when he could have got rid of this job would have been much closer; but now it was undoubtedly better the way his father had arranged it.
paras.uz: Eshik ortida Gregor bu kutilmagan ehtiyotkorlik va tejamkorlikdan xursand bo'lib, g'ayrat bilan bosh irg'ab qo'ydi. Aslida u bu ortiqcha pul bilan otasining xo'jayinga bo'lgan qarzini ko'proq to'lashi mumkin edi va bu ishdan qutuladigan kuni ancha yaqinroq bo'lardi; lekin endi, shubhasiz, otasi qanday tartib bergan bo'lsa, shunisi yaxshiroq edi.

paras.en: This money, however, was not nearly enough for the family to live on the interest; it was enough to keep the family for one, at most two years, no more. So it was only a sum that really should not be touched and had to be put aside for emergencies; the money to live on had to be earned. But his father, though healthy, was an old man who had not worked for five years and could not expect much of himself. During these five years, which were the first holiday of his hard-working yet unsuccessful life, he had put on a lot of fat and had become rather slow and heavy as a result.
paras.uz: Lekin bu pul oilaning foizlar hisobiga yashashi uchun mutlaqo yetarli emasdi; u oilani bir, ko'pi bilan ikki yil boqishga yetishi mumkin edi, xolos. Demak, bu aslida tegish mumkin bo'lmagan va favqulodda holat uchun saqlab qo'yilishi kerak bo'lgan pul edi; yashash uchun esa pul topish kerak edi. Otasi esa sog'lom bo'lsa ham, keksa odam edi, besh yildan beri hech qayerda ishlamagan va o'ziga unchalik ishona olmasdi; mashaqqatli, lekin muvaffaqiyatsiz hayotining birinchi ta'tili bo'lgan bu besh yilda u ancha semirib, shu sababli og'ir-karvon bo'lib qolgan edi.

paras.en: And was his old mother now supposed to earn money, when she suffered from asthma, when even walking through the flat was a strain for her, and when she spent every other day on the sofa by the open window struggling for breath? And was his sister supposed to earn money, who was still a child at seventeen, and who so deserved the way of life she had had until now, which had consisted of dressing nicely, sleeping late, helping in the house, taking part in a few modest pleasures and, above all, playing the violin? Whenever the conversation turned to this need to earn money, Gregor would always let go of the door and throw himself onto the cool leather sofa next to it, because he felt hot with shame and grief.
paras.uz: Endi astmadan aziyat chekadigan, hatto kvartira bo'ylab yurish ham qiyin bo'lgan va har ikki kunning birini ochiq deraza yonidagi divanda nafas qisib o'tkazadigan keksa onasi pul topishi kerakmidi? Yoki o'n yetti yoshida hali bola bo'lgan, shu paytgacha bo'lgan hayot tarziga — chiroyli kiyinish, uzoq uxlash, uy ishlariga qarashish, bir nechta oddiy ko'ngilxushliklarda qatnashish va eng muhimi skripka chalishga — juda loyiq bo'lgan singlisi pul topishi kerakmidi? Gap pul topish zaruratiga kelganda, Gregor doim avval eshikni qo'yib yuborar va eshik yonidagi salqin charm divanga o'zini tashlardi, chunki uyat va qayg'udan butun vujudi qizib ketardi.

paras.en: Often he lay there through the long nights, not sleeping for a moment, just scratching at the leather for hours. Or he would go to the great trouble of pushing a chair to the window, then crawling up onto the windowsill and, propped against the chair, leaning against the window, evidently only in some memory of the sense of freedom that looking out of the window used to give him. For in fact, from day to day, he saw things that were even a little distance away less and less clearly. The hospital opposite, which he used to curse because he had to see it all too often, he could no longer see at all, and if he had not known for certain that he lived in the quiet but completely urban Charlotte Street, he could have believed that he was looking out of his window at a wasteland where the grey sky and the grey earth merged and could not be told apart.
paras.uz: Ko'pincha u uzun tunlar bo'yi o'sha yerda yotar, bir lahza ham uxlamas, soatlab charmni tirnab chiqardi. Yoki u kreslo'ni deraza tomon surish, so'ng deraza tokchasiga o'rmalab chiqish va kreslo'ga tayangancha derazaga suyanish kabi katta mashaqqatdan qochmasdi — bu, aftidan, faqat ilgari derazadan qarash unga beradigan erkinlik tuyg'usini eslash uchun edi. Chunki aslida u kundan-kunga hatto sal uzoqroqdagi narsalarni ham tobora xira ko'rardi; ilgari juda tez-tez ko'zga tashlangani uchun la'natlagan ro'paradagi kasalxonani endi umuman ko'rmasdi va agar u jimjit, lekin to'la shahar ko'chasi bo'lgan Sharlotta ko'chasida yashashini aniq bilmaganida, derazasidan kulrang osmon va kulrang yer bir-biridan ajratib bo'lmaydigan darajada qo'shilib ketgan sahroga qarab turibman, deb o'ylashi mumkin edi.

paras.en: His attentive sister only had to see twice that the chair was standing by the window; after that, every time she had tidied the room, she pushed the chair back exactly to the window, and from then on she even left the inner window open.
paras.uz: Ziyrak singlisi kreslo deraza yonida turganini atigi ikki marta ko'rdi; shundan keyin har safar xonani yig'ishtirgach, kreslo'ni yana aynan deraza yoniga surib qo'yardi, hatto endi ichki deraza tavaqasini ochiq qoldirardi.

paras.en: If only Gregor had been able to speak to his sister and thank her for everything she had to do for him, he would have found her services easier to bear; as it was, he suffered from them. His sister, of course, tried to cover up the awkwardness of the whole thing as much as possible, and the more time passed, the better she naturally succeeded; but with time Gregor also saw through everything much more clearly. Even her coming in was terrible for him. Hardly had she entered when, without taking the time to close the door — however careful she otherwise was to spare everyone the sight of Gregor's room — she ran straight to the window and tore it open with hasty hands, as if she were almost suffocating, and stayed by the window for a while, however cold it was, breathing deeply.
paras.uz: Agar Gregor singlisi bilan gaplashib, u uchun qilishga majbur bo'lgan hamma narsa uchun unga rahmat ayta olganida, uning xizmatlarini osonroq ko'targan bo'lardi; hozir esa bundan azob chekardi. Singlisi, albatta, bu ishdagi noqulaylikni iloji boricha yashirishga urinardi va vaqt o'tgan sari, tabiiyki, bu unga yaxshiroq uddalanardi; lekin vaqt o'tib Gregor ham hamma narsani ancha aniqroq ko'ra boshladi. Uning xonaga kirishining o'ziyoq unga dahshatli edi. Kirishi bilanoq — aslida Gregor xonasining ko'rinishidan hammani asrashga qanchalik e'tibor bermasin — eshikni yopishga ham vaqt sarflamay, to'g'ri derazaga yugurar, go'yo bo'g'ilib qolayotganday uni shoshqin qo'llari bilan yulqib ochar, havo qanchalik sovuq bo'lmasin, deraza yonida biroz turib, chuqur nafas olardi.

paras.en: With this running and noise she frightened Gregor twice a day. The whole time he trembled under the sofa, and yet he knew very well that she would gladly have spared him this if only she had been able to stay in a room where Gregor was with the window closed.
paras.uz: Bu yugurish va shovqin bilan u Gregorni kuniga ikki marta qo'rqitardi; u butun vaqt divan ostida titrab yotardi, lekin agar singlisi Gregor bor xonada deraza yopiq holda tura olganida, uni bundan albatta asragan bo'lishini juda yaxshi bilardi.

paras.en: Once — about a month must have passed since Gregor's transformation, and there was really no particular reason any more for his sister to be amazed at Gregor's appearance — she came a little earlier than usual and found Gregor still looking out of the window, motionless and positioned in a truly frightening way. It would not have surprised Gregor if she had not come in, since his position stopped her from opening the window immediately; but she not only did not come in, she even jumped back and shut the door. A stranger might almost have thought that Gregor had been lying in wait for her and had wanted to bite her.
paras.uz: Bir kuni — Gregorning o'zgarishiga bir oycha bo'lgan, singlisi uchun uning qiyofasidan hayratlanishga endi alohida sabab qolmagan edi — u odatdagidan sal erta keldi va Gregorni hali ham qimirlamay, chinakam qo'rqinchli holatda derazadan qarab turgan holda ko'rdi. Agar u ichkariga kirmaganida, Gregor uchun bu kutilmagan bo'lmasdi, chunki u o'z holati bilan singlisining darhol derazani ochishiga xalaqit berardi; lekin u nafaqat kirmadi, balki hatto orqaga sakrab, eshikni yopdi; begona odam hatto Gregor uni poylab turib, tishlamoqchi bo'lgan, deb o'ylashi mumkin edi.

paras.en: Gregor of course hid under the sofa at once, but he had to wait until noon before his sister came back, and she seemed much more uneasy than usual. From this he realised that the sight of him was still unbearable to her and must remain unbearable to her, and that she probably had to make a great effort not to run away even from the sight of the small part of his body that stuck out from under the sofa. To spare her even this sight, one day he carried the bedsheet on his back onto the sofa — the job took him four hours — and arranged it in such a way that he was now completely covered, and his sister could not see him even if she bent down.
paras.uz: Gregor, albatta, darhol divan ostiga yashirindi, lekin singlisi qaytib kelguncha tushgacha kutishga majbur bo'ldi va u odatdagidan ancha bezovtaroq ko'rinardi. Bundan u o'zining ko'rinishi singlisi uchun hamon chidab bo'lmasligini va bundan keyin ham shunday bo'lib qolishi kerakligini, divan ostidan chiqib turgan tanasining kichik bir qismini ko'rganda ham qochib ketmaslik uchun singlisi o'zini juda qattiq tutishi kerakligini tushundi. Uni hatto bu manzaradan ham asrash uchun u bir kuni choyshabni orqasiga ortib divan ustiga olib chiqdi — bu ish unga to'rt soat vaqt oldi — va uni shunday joylashtirdiki, endi butunlay yopilib qoldi va singlisi hatto engashganda ham uni ko'ra olmasdi.

paras.en: If she had thought this sheet unnecessary, she could have removed it, for it was clear enough that Gregor could not be shutting himself off so completely for his own pleasure; but she left the sheet as it was, and Gregor even thought he caught a grateful look when he once carefully lifted the sheet a little with his head to see how his sister was taking the new arrangement.
paras.uz: Agar uning fikricha bu choyshab keraksiz bo'lganida, uni olib tashlashi mumkin edi, chunki Gregor o'zini bunchalik to'sib olishdan zavq olmasligi yetarlicha aniq edi; lekin u choyshabni qanday bo'lsa shunday qoldirdi va Gregor bir marta singlisi yangi tartibni qanday qabul qilayotganini ko'rish uchun boshi bilan choyshabni sal ko'targanida, hatto minnatdor nigohni ilg'aganday bo'ldi.

paras.en: During the first two weeks his parents could not bring themselves to come in to him, and he often heard them praising his sister's present work, whereas until then they had often been annoyed with her because she had seemed to them a rather useless girl. But now both of them, his father and his mother, often waited outside Gregor's room while his sister tidied it, and as soon as she came out she had to tell them in great detail what the room looked like, what Gregor had eaten, how he had behaved this time, and whether perhaps a slight improvement could be noticed.
paras.uz: Dastlabki ikki hafta davomida ota-onasi uning oldiga kirishga o'zlarida kuch topa olmadilar va u ko'pincha ular singlisining hozirgi mehnatini to'liq tan olishayotganini eshitardi, holbuki shu paytgacha ular singlisidan tez-tez achchiqlanishardi, chunki u ularga biroz foydasiz qizday tuyulardi. Endi esa ikkalasi — otasi ham, onasi ham — singlisi Gregorning xonasini yig'ishtirayotganda ko'pincha eshik oldida kutib turishardi va u chiqishi bilanoq xona qanday ahvolda ekanini, Gregor nima yeganini, bu safar o'zini qanday tutganini va, ehtimol, biroz yaxshilanish sezilyaptimi-yo'qmi, juda batafsil aytib berishi kerak edi.

paras.en: His mother, by the way, wanted to visit Gregor fairly soon, but his father and sister held her back at first with sensible arguments, which Gregor listened to very attentively and fully approved of. Later, however, she had to be held back by force, and when she cried out: “Let me go to Gregor, he's my unhappy son! Don't you understand that I have to go to him?”, Gregor thought that perhaps it would be good after all if his mother came in — not every day, of course, but perhaps once a week. She understood everything much better than his sister, who, in spite of all her courage, was only a child and had perhaps, in the end, taken on such a difficult task only out of childish thoughtlessness.
paras.uz: Aytgancha, onasi Gregorni ancha erta ko'rmoqchi bo'ldi, lekin otasi va singlisi avval uni oqilona dalillar bilan to'xtatishdi; Gregor bu dalillarni juda diqqat bilan tingladi va to'liq ma'qulladi. Keyinroq esa uni kuch bilan ushlab qolishga to'g'ri keldi va u: «Meni Gregorning oldiga qo'yib yuboringlar, axir u mening baxtsiz o'g'lim! Uning oldiga borishim kerakligini nahotki tushunmasanglar?» — deb qichqirganida, Gregor onasi kirsa, balki yaxshi bo'lar, deb o'yladi — albatta, har kuni emas, lekin, balki haftada bir marta; axir u hamma narsani singlisidan ancha yaxshi tushunardi; singlisi esa butun jasoratiga qaramay, hali bola edi va, ehtimol, oxir-oqibatda bunday og'ir vazifani faqat bolalarcha beparvolik bilan o'z zimmasiga olgandir.

paras.en: Gregor's wish to see his mother was soon fulfilled. During the day, out of consideration for his parents, Gregor did not want to show himself at the window; but he could not crawl very much on the few square metres of floor either; he already found it hard to lie still during the night; eating soon gave him no pleasure at all. So, to amuse himself, he took up the habit of crawling crisscross over the walls and the ceiling. He particularly liked hanging from the ceiling. It was quite different from lying on the floor; one could breathe more freely; a gentle swaying went through his body; and in the almost happy absent-mindedness Gregor fell into up there, it could happen that, to his own surprise, he let go and smacked down onto the floor. But now, of course, he had his body under much better control than before, and he did not hurt himself even in such a big fall.
paras.uz: Gregorning onasini ko'rish istagi tez orada amalga oshdi. Kunduzi Gregor ota-onasini o'ylab derazada ko'rinishni istamasdi; lekin polning bir necha kvadrat metrida ham ko'p o'rmalay olmasdi; tunlari tinch yotishga ham zo'rg'a chidar, ovqat esa tez orada unga hech qanday zavq bermay qo'ydi. Shuning uchun ko'ngil ochish maqsadida u devor va shift bo'ylab u yoqdan-bu yoqqa o'rmalash odatini chiqardi. Ayniqsa shiftga osilib turishni yaxshi ko'rardi; bu polda yotishdan butunlay boshqacha edi: erkinroq nafas olinardi, tanasi bo'ylab yengil tebranish o'tardi va Gregor u yerda tushib qoladigan deyarli baxtiyor parishonlik holatida, o'zi ham hayron qolib, qo'yib yuborib, polga shap etib tushishi mumkin edi. Lekin endi u, albatta, tanasini avvalgidan ancha yaxshi boshqarardi va hatto shunday baland joydan yiqilganda ham shikastlanmasdi.

paras.en: His sister noticed at once the new entertainment Gregor had found for himself — after all, as he crawled he left traces of his sticky substance here and there — and so she got it into her head to let Gregor crawl as widely as possible and to remove the furniture that got in his way, above all the chest of drawers and the writing desk. But she could not do this alone. She did not dare to ask her father for help; the maid would certainly not have helped her, for this girl of about sixteen, though she had bravely stayed on since the former cook had been dismissed, had asked for the privilege of keeping the kitchen locked at all times and only having to open it when specially called. So his sister had no choice but to fetch her mother one day while her father was out.
paras.uz: Singlisi Gregor o'zi uchun topgan yangi ermakni darhol payqadi — axir u o'rmalaganida u yer-bu yerda yopishqoq suyuqligining izlarini qoldirardi — va shunda Gregorga imkon qadar keng o'rmalash imkonini berish va bunga xalaqit beradigan mebellarni, avvalo javon va yozuv stolini olib chiqib ketishni ko'ngliga tugib qo'ydi. Lekin buni u yolg'iz qila olmasdi; otasidan yordam so'rashga jur'at etmasdi; oqsoch esa, shubhasiz, yordam bermasdi, chunki taxminan o'n olti yoshli bu qiz avvalgi oshpaz ishdan bo'shatilgandan beri jasorat bilan ishlab yurgan bo'lsa-da, oshxonani doim qulflab o'tirishga va faqat alohida chaqirilgandagina ochishga ruxsat so'ragan edi. Shunday qilib, singlisiga otasi yo'qligida bir kuni onasini chaqirib kelishdan boshqa iloj qolmadi.

paras.en: His mother came with exclamations of excited joy, but fell silent at the door of Gregor's room. First, of course, his sister checked whether everything in the room was in order; only then did she let her mother come in. In great haste Gregor had pulled the sheet down even lower and into more folds; the whole thing really looked just like a sheet thrown carelessly over the sofa. This time, too, Gregor did not spy from under the sheet; he gave up seeing his mother this time and was simply glad that she had come at last. “Come in, he can't be seen,” said his sister, and she was evidently leading her mother by the hand.
paras.uz: Onasi hayajonli quvonch bilan xitob qilib keldi, lekin Gregorning xonasi eshigi oldida jim bo'lib qoldi. Avval, albatta, singlisi xonada hammasi joyidami-yo'qmi, tekshirdi; shundan keyingina onasini ichkariga kiritdi. Gregor juda shoshib choyshabni yanada pastroq va ko'proq burmalar bilan tortib qo'ygan edi; hammasi chindan ham divan ustiga tasodifan tashlab qo'yilgan choyshabga o'xshardi. Bu safar ham Gregor choyshab ostidan mo'ralamadi; u onasini bu safar ko'rishdan voz kechdi va uning nihoyat kelganidan xursand edi, xolos. «Kiravering, u ko'rinmaydi», — dedi singlisi va aftidan onasini qo'lidan yetaklab kirdi.

paras.en: Gregor now heard the two weak women moving the old chest of drawers, which was heavy after all, from its place, and heard his sister constantly taking the greater part of the work on herself, without listening to the warnings of her mother, who was afraid she would overstrain herself. It took a very long time. After about a quarter of an hour of work his mother said that they had better leave the chest where it was. Firstly, it was too heavy; they would not be finished before his father came home, and with the chest in the middle of the room they would block every path for Gregor. Secondly, it was not at all certain that removing the furniture would be doing Gregor a favour.
paras.uz: Endi Gregor ikki zaif ayolning baribir og'ir bo'lgan eski javonni joyidan siljitayotganini va singlisi onasining o'zini haddan tashqari charchatib qo'yishidan qo'rqqan ogohlantirishlariga quloq solmay, ishning eng katta qismini doim o'z zimmasiga olayotganini eshitdi. Bu juda uzoq davom etdi. Chorak soatcha ishlagandan keyin onasi javonni shu yerda qoldirgan ma'qul, dedi: birinchidan, u juda og'ir, otasi kelguncha ular tugatisholmaydi va javon xona o'rtasida qolib, Gregorning barcha yo'llarini to'sib qo'yadi; ikkinchidan esa mebelni olib chiqish Gregorga yaxshilik bo'lishi umuman aniq emas.

paras.en: It seemed to her that the opposite was true; the sight of the bare wall actually made her heart heavy; and why shouldn't Gregor have the same feeling, since he had long been used to the furniture in his room and would therefore feel abandoned in the empty room? “And isn't it as if,” his mother ended very quietly — in fact she was almost whispering all the time, as if she wanted to prevent Gregor, whose exact whereabouts she did not know, from hearing even the sound of her voice, for she was convinced that he did not understand the words — “and isn't it as if, by removing the furniture, we were showing that we have given up all hope of improvement and are leaving him to himself without any consideration? I think it would be best to try to keep the room exactly as it was before, so that when Gregor comes back to us he will find everything unchanged and can more easily forget the time in between.”
paras.uz: Unga buning aksi to'g'riday tuyulardi; bo'm-bo'sh devorni ko'rish uning yuragini ezardi; va nega Gregor ham shunday his qilmasligi kerak, axir u xonasidagi mebellarga allaqachon ko'nikib qolgan va shuning uchun bo'sh xonada o'zini tashlab qo'yilganday his qiladi. «Bu xuddi shunday emasmi, — deb gapini juda sekin tugatdi onasi; u umuman deyarli pichirlab gapirardi, go'yo qayerdaligini aniq bilmaydigan Gregor hatto uning ovozini ham eshitmasligini istaganday, chunki u so'zlarni tushunmasligiga ishonchi komil edi, — bu xuddi mebellarni olib chiqib, biz yaxshilanishga bo'lgan barcha umidni uzganimizni va uni shafqatsizlarcha o'z holiga tashlab qo'yganimizni ko'rsatayotganday emasmi? Menimcha, eng yaxshisi — xonani avvalgi holatida aynan saqlab qolish, toki Gregor yana oramizga qaytganda hamma narsani o'zgarmagan holda topsin va o'rtadagi vaqtni osonroq unutsin».
