chapters.note_uz: Bu bobda Gregorning oiladagi o'rni ochiladi: u yillar davomida oilaning yagona boquvchisi bo'lgan, lekin bu munosabatda «iliqlik qolmagan». Shift bo'ylab o'rmalashdan zavqlanishi — uning hasharot tanasiga ko'nikib borayotganini ko'rsatadi. Mebel masalasi esa savol tug'diradi: Gregorga xona kerakmi yoki odamlik xotirasi?

chapters.title: The Apple
chapters.recap_uz: Gregor xonasi bo'shatilishini istamasligini anglaydi va devordagi mo'yna kiygan xonim suratiga yopishib oladi. Onasi uni ko'rib hushidan ketadi. Bank xizmatchisi formasini kiygan otasi kelib, Gregorga olma otadi; bitta olma uning orqasiga botib qoladi.

paras.en: When he heard these words of his mother's, Gregor realised that the lack of any direct human conversation, together with the monotonous life in the middle of the family, must have confused his mind over the course of these two months; for he could not explain otherwise how he could seriously have wanted his room to be emptied. Did he really want to have his warm room, comfortably furnished with inherited furniture, turned into a cave in which he could of course crawl about undisturbed in every direction, but at the same time quickly and completely forget his human past? He was already close to forgetting, and only his mother's voice, which he had not heard for so long, had shaken him awake.
paras.uz: Onasining bu so'zlarini eshitib, Gregor bevosita odamlar bilan hech qanday muloqot yo'qligi va oila orasidagi bir xil hayot bu ikki oy ichida aqlini chalkashtirib yuborgan bo'lsa kerak, deb tushundi; aks holda xonasi bo'shatilishini jiddiy istaganini boshqacha izohlay olmasdi. Nahotki u meros mebellar bilan qulay jihozlangan iliq xonasini g'orga aylantirishni chindan ham istagan bo'lsa? U yerda, albatta, har tomonga bemalol o'rmalay olardi, lekin shu bilan birga odamlik o'tmishini tez va butunlay unutib yuborardi. U allaqachon unutishga yaqin edi va faqat uzoq vaqtdan beri eshitmagan onasining ovozi uni silkitib uyg'otdi.

paras.en: Nothing should be removed; everything had to stay; he could not do without the good effect the furniture had on his condition; and if the furniture stopped him from crawling around senselessly, that was no loss but a great advantage.
paras.uz: Hech narsa olib chiqilmasligi kerak, hammasi qolishi shart edi; mebelning uning holatiga yaxshi ta'siridan u voz kecha olmasdi; agar mebel uning ma'nosiz o'rmalab yurishiga xalaqit bersa, bu zarar emas, balki katta foyda edi.

paras.en: But his sister unfortunately thought differently. She had got into the habit — admittedly not entirely without reason — of acting as a special expert in front of their parents whenever Gregor's affairs were discussed, and so now too her mother's advice was reason enough for his sister to insist on removing not only the chest and the desk, which was all she had thought of at first, but all the furniture except the indispensable sofa. Of course it was not only childish defiance and the self-confidence she had recently and so unexpectedly gained with such difficulty that made her demand this; she had also actually observed that Gregor needed a lot of space to crawl about, while, as far as could be seen, he did not use the furniture at all.
paras.uz: Lekin afsuski, singlisi boshqacha fikrda edi; u — to'g'ri, butunlay asossiz emas — Gregorning ishlari muhokama qilinganda ota-onasi oldida alohida mutaxassis sifatida chiqishga odatlanib qolgan edi; shuning uchun hozir ham onasining maslahati singlisi uchun avval o'zi o'ylagan javon va yozuv stolinigina emas, balki ajralmas divandan tashqari barcha mebellarni olib chiqishni talab qilish uchun yetarli sabab bo'ldi. Albatta, uni bu talabga undagan narsa faqat bolalarcha o'jarlik va so'nggi paytlarda kutilmaganda hamda qiyinchilik bilan orttirilgan o'ziga ishonch emasdi; u Gregorga o'rmalash uchun ko'p joy kerakligini, mebellardan esa, ko'rinishicha, u zarracha ham foydalanmasligini rostdan ham kuzatgan edi.

paras.en: But perhaps the romantic enthusiasm of girls of her age also played a part, which seeks satisfaction at every opportunity and which now tempted Grete to want to make Gregor's situation even more terrifying, so that she could then do even more for him than before. For into a room where Gregor ruled the bare walls all alone, probably no one but Grete would ever dare to enter.
paras.uz: Lekin, ehtimol, uning yoshidagi qizlarga xos, har qanday imkoniyatda qoniqish izlaydigan xayolparastlik ham o'z rolini o'ynagandir: shu tuyg'u endi Gretani Gregorning ahvolini yanada qo'rqinchliroq qilishga, so'ngra u uchun avvalgidan ham ko'proq ish qilishga undardi. Chunki Gregor bo'm-bo'sh devorlar ustidan yolg'iz o'zi hukmronlik qiladigan xonaga, ehtimol, Gretadan boshqa hech kim kirishga jur'at etmasdi.

paras.en: And so she did not let her mother talk her out of her decision. Her mother, who also seemed unsure of herself in this room out of sheer anxiety, soon fell silent and helped his sister as well as she could to get the chest out. Well, in an emergency Gregor could do without the chest, but the desk at least had to stay. And hardly had the women left the room with the chest, which they were pushing with groans, when Gregor stuck his head out from under the sofa to see how he could intervene carefully and with as much consideration as possible.
paras.uz: Shunday qilib, u onasining gapi bilan qaroridan qaytmadi; bu xonada xavotirdan o'ziga ishonchsiz ko'ringan onasi tez orada jim bo'lib qoldi va javonni olib chiqishda singlisiga qo'lidan kelganicha yordam berdi. Xo'sh, zarurat bo'lsa, Gregor javonsiz ham yasha olardi, lekin yozuv stoli albatta qolishi kerak edi. Ayollar ingrab itarayotgan javon bilan xonadan chiqishlari bilanoq, Gregor qanday qilib ehtiyotkorlik bilan va imkon qadar e'tiborli tarzda aralashish mumkinligini ko'rish uchun boshini divan ostidan chiqardi.

paras.en: But unfortunately it was his mother who came back first, while Grete in the next room had her arms around the chest and was rocking it back and forth on her own, without of course moving it from the spot. His mother, however, was not used to the sight of Gregor; it could have made her ill. So Gregor, frightened, hurried backwards to the other end of the sofa, but he could not prevent the sheet from moving a little at the front. That was enough to catch his mother's attention. She stopped, stood still for a moment and then went back to Grete.
paras.uz: Lekin baxtga qarshi, birinchi bo'lib aynan onasi qaytdi, Grete esa qo'shni xonada javonni quchoqlab, uni yolg'iz o'zi u yoqdan-bu yoqqa tebratardi, albatta, joyidan qimirlatolmay. Onasi esa Gregorni ko'rishga o'rganmagan edi, bu uni kasal qilib qo'yishi mumkin edi; shuning uchun Gregor qo'rqib ketib, orqaga yurib divanning narigi chetiga shoshildi, lekin choyshabning oldi biroz qimirlashining oldini ololmadi. Bu onasining e'tiborini tortish uchun yetarli edi. U to'xtadi, bir lahza qimirlamay turdi, so'ng Gretaning oldiga qaytib ketdi.

paras.en: Although Gregor kept telling himself that nothing extraordinary was happening, that just a few pieces of furniture were being moved, he soon had to admit that the women going back and forth, their little calls to each other, the scraping of the furniture on the floor, affected him like a great commotion coming at him from all sides; and however tightly he drew in his head and legs and pressed his body to the floor, he had to tell himself that he would not be able to stand it all for long. They were clearing out his room; taking away everything he loved. They had already carried out the chest that held his fretsaw and other tools.
paras.uz: Gregor o'ziga hech qanday favqulodda narsa bo'lmayapti, shunchaki bir nechta mebel joyi o'zgartirilyapti, deb qayta-qayta aytsa ham, tez orada tan olishga majbur bo'ldiki, ayollarning u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yurishi, bir-biriga qisqa-qisqa chaqiriqlari, mebellarning polda g'ichirlashi unga har tomondan bostirib kelayotgan katta g'alayonday ta'sir qilardi va u boshi bilan oyoqlarini qanchalik mahkam yig'ib, tanasini polga bosmasin, bunga uzoq chiday olmasligini o'ziga aytishga majbur edi. Ular xonasini bo'shatishardi; unga aziz bo'lgan hamma narsani olib ketishardi; arracha va boshqa asboblari turgan javonni allaqachon olib chiqib ketishgan edi.

paras.en: Now they were loosening the writing desk, which was firmly dug into the floor, at which he had done his homework as a student at the business academy, at secondary school, and even at primary school. At that point he really had no more time to weigh up the good intentions of the two women, whose existence, by the way, he had almost forgotten, because they were so exhausted that they were already working in silence, and only the heavy tread of their feet could be heard.
paras.uz: Endi ular polga mahkam o'rnashib qolgan yozuv stolini bo'shatishardi — uning ortida u tijorat akademiyasi talabasi sifatida, o'rta maktab o'quvchisi sifatida, hatto boshlang'ich maktab o'quvchisi sifatida ham vazifalarini yozgan edi. Shunda u ikki ayolning yaxshi niyatlarini tahlil qilishga endi chindan ham vaqt topolmadi; aytgancha, u ularning borligini deyarli unutgan ham edi, chunki ular holdan toyganidan allaqachon jim ishlashar va faqat oyoqlarining og'ir tapillashi eshitilardi.

paras.en: And so he broke out — the women were just leaning against the desk in the next room to get their breath back a little — and changed direction four times; he really did not know what to save first. Then he saw, hanging conspicuously on the otherwise empty wall, the picture of the lady dressed all in furs. He quickly crawled up to it and pressed himself against the glass, which held him fast and felt good against his hot belly. This picture at least, which Gregor now covered completely, nobody would take away now. He twisted his head towards the living-room door so as to watch the women when they came back.
paras.uz: Shunday qilib u otilib chiqdi — ayollar qo'shni xonada biroz nafas rostlash uchun endigina yozuv stoliga suyanib turishgan edi — va to'rt marta yo'nalishini o'zgartirdi, u chindan ham avval nimani qutqarishni bilmasdi; shunda u boshqa tomoni allaqachon bo'shab qolgan devorda butunlay mo'ynaga burkangan xonimning surati ko'zga tashlanib osilib turganini ko'rdi; shoshib unga o'rmalab chiqdi va uni mahkam ushlab turgan va qizib ketgan qorniga huzur bergan oynaga yopishdi. Hech bo'lmasa Gregor endi butunlay to'sib turgan bu suratni hech kim olib ketmasa kerak. U ayollar qaytganda ularni kuzatish uchun boshini mehmonxona eshigi tomon burdi.

paras.en: They had not allowed themselves much rest and were already coming back; Grete had put her arm around her mother and was almost carrying her. “So what shall we take now?” said Grete, and looked around. Then her eyes met Gregor's on the wall. Probably only because her mother was there, she kept her composure. She bent her face towards her mother to stop her from looking around and said, trembling and without thinking: “Come, hadn't we better go back into the living room for a moment?” Grete's intention was clear to Gregor: she wanted to get her mother to safety and then chase him down from the wall. Well, let her try! He sat on his picture and would not give it up. He would rather jump in Grete's face.
paras.uz: Ular o'zlariga ko'p dam bermadilar va yana qaytib kelishdi; Grete qo'lini onasining beliga qo'yib, uni deyarli ko'tarib kelardi. «Xo'sh, endi nimani olamiz?» — dedi Grete atrofga qarab. Shunda uning nigohi devordagi Gregorning nigohi bilan to'qnashdi. Faqat onasi yonida bo'lgani uchungina u o'zini tutib qoldi, onasi atrofga qaramasligi uchun yuzini unga egdi va titrab, o'ylamay dedi: «Yuring, biroz mehmonxonaga qaytsak-chi?» Gretaning niyati Gregorga aniq edi: u onasini xavfsiz joyga olib borib, keyin uni devordan quvib tushirmoqchi edi. Mayli, urinib ko'rsin! U suratining ustida o'tirar va uni bermasdi. Bundan ko'ra Gretaning yuziga sakrardi.

paras.en: But Grete's words had only made her mother more anxious. She stepped to one side, caught sight of the huge brown stain on the flowered wallpaper, and before she really became aware that what she saw was Gregor, she cried out in a shrill, rough voice: “Oh God, oh God!” and fell with her arms spread out over the sofa, as if she were giving up everything, and did not move. “You, Gregor!” cried his sister, raising her fist and glaring at him. These were the first words she had spoken directly to him since the transformation.
paras.uz: Lekin Gretaning so'zlari onasini yanada bezovta qilib qo'ydi; u bir chetga o'tdi, gulli gulqog'oz ustidagi ulkan jigarrang dog'ni ko'rdi va ko'rgan narsasi Gregor ekanini anglab yetmasidan oldin, qichqiriq, xirildoq ovozda: «Yo Xudo, yo Xudo!» — dedi va go'yo hamma narsadan voz kechganday, qo'llarini yoyib divan ustiga yiqildi va qimirlamay qoldi. «Sen, Gregor!» — deb qichqirdi singlisi mushtini ko'tarib, unga o'qrayib. Bu o'zgarishdan beri u to'g'ridan-to'g'ri unga aytgan birinchi so'zlar edi.

paras.en: She ran into the next room to fetch some kind of essence with which to bring her mother round from her faint. Gregor wanted to help too — there was still time to save the picture — but he was stuck fast to the glass and had to tear himself loose by force. He then ran into the next room too, as if he could give his sister some advice, as in the old days; but then he had to stand behind her doing nothing. While she was searching among various little bottles, she was frightened again when she turned round; a bottle fell on the floor and broke; a splinter cut Gregor's face, and some burning medicine flowed around him.
paras.uz: U onasini hushiga keltirish uchun qandaydir hidli dori olib kelish uchun qo'shni xonaga yugurdi; Gregor ham yordam bermoqchi edi — suratni qutqarishga hali vaqt bor edi — lekin u oynaga mahkam yopishib qolgan edi va o'zini kuch bilan yulib olishiga to'g'ri keldi; keyin u ham go'yo avvalgi kunlardagidek singlisiga biror maslahat bera oladiganday qo'shni xonaga yugurdi; lekin keyin uning orqasida hech narsa qilmay turishga majbur bo'ldi; u turli shishachalarni titkilayotganda o'girilib, yana qo'rqib ketdi; bir shisha yerga tushib sindi; bir parcha Gregorning yuzini yaraladi, qandaydir achchiq, kuydiruvchi dori uning atrofiga oqib ketdi.

paras.en: Without stopping any longer, Grete now took as many little bottles as she could hold and ran in to her mother with them; she slammed the door shut with her foot. Gregor was now shut off from his mother, who, through his fault, was perhaps close to death. He must not open the door if he did not want to drive away his sister, who had to stay with their mother; there was nothing for him to do now but wait. And tormented by self-reproach and worry, he began to crawl. He crawled over everything — walls, furniture and ceiling — and finally, in his despair, as the whole room was already beginning to spin around him, he fell down onto the middle of the big table.
paras.uz: Grete endi boshqa to'xtamay, qo'li sig'adigan qadar shishachalarni oldi va ular bilan onasining oldiga yugurib kirdi; eshikni oyog'i bilan tepib yopdi. Endi Gregor onasidan ajratib qo'yilgan edi; onasi esa uning aybi bilan, ehtimol, o'limga yaqin edi; agar onasi yonida qolishi kerak bo'lgan singlisini haydab yubormoqchi bo'lmasa, u eshikni ochmasligi kerak edi; hozir kutishdan boshqa qiladigan ishi yo'q edi; va o'zini ayblash hamda xavotir azobida u o'rmalay boshladi, hamma narsa — devorlar, mebellar va shift ustidan o'rmalab chiqdi va nihoyat umidsizlikda, butun xona atrofida aylana boshlaganida, katta stolning o'rtasiga yiqildi.

paras.en: A little while passed. Gregor lay there weakly; all around it was quiet; perhaps that was a good sign. Then the doorbell rang. The maid, of course, was locked in her kitchen, so Grete had to go and open the door. His father had come home. “What's happened?” were his first words; Grete's appearance had probably told him everything. Grete answered in a muffled voice, evidently pressing her face against her father's chest: “Mother fainted, but she's already better. Gregor has broken out.” “Just as I expected,” said his father, “I always told you so, but you women never want to listen.”
paras.uz: Biroz vaqt o'tdi, Gregor holsiz yotardi, atrof jimjit edi, balki bu yaxshi belgidir. Shu payt qo'ng'iroq chalindi. Oqsoch, albatta, oshxonasida qamalib o'tirgan edi, shuning uchun eshikni Grete ochishi kerak edi. Otasi kelgan edi. «Nima bo'ldi?» — bular uning birinchi so'zlari edi; Gretaning qiyofasi unga hammasini aytib bergan bo'lsa kerak. Grete bo'g'iq ovozda, aftidan yuzini otasining ko'kragiga bosib, javob berdi: «Onam hushidan ketdi, lekin hozir yaxshiroq. Gregor qochib chiqdi». «Shuni kutgandim, — dedi otasi, — men sizlarga doim aytardim, lekin sizlar, ayollar, eshitishni istamaysizlar».

paras.en: It was clear to Gregor that his father had misunderstood Grete's all too short report and assumed that Gregor had committed some act of violence. So Gregor now had to try to calm his father down, for he had neither the time nor the means to explain things to him. And so he fled to the door of his room and pressed himself against it, so that his father, coming in from the hall, could see at once that Gregor had the best intention of going back into his room immediately, and that there was no need to drive him back — they only needed to open the door, and he would disappear at once.
paras.uz: Gregorga otasi Gretaning juda qisqa xabarini noto'g'ri tushunganligi va Gregor qandaydir zo'ravonlik qilgan deb o'ylayotgani aniq edi. Shuning uchun Gregor endi otasini tinchlantirishga urinishi kerak edi, chunki unga tushuntirish uchun na vaqti, na imkoni bor edi. Shunday qilib u o'z xonasining eshigi tomon qochib, unga yopishdi, toki otasi dahlizdan kirishi bilanoq Gregorning darhol xonasiga qaytishga eng yaxshi niyati borligini, uni haydashga hojat yo'qligini, faqat eshikni ochish kifoyaligini va u shu zahoti g'oyib bo'lishini ko'rsin.

paras.en: But his father was in no mood to notice such subtleties. “Ah!” he cried as soon as he came in, in a tone as if he were furious and glad at the same time. Gregor drew his head back from the door and raised it towards his father. He had really not imagined his father the way he stood there now. Admittedly, recently, absorbed in his new crawling, he had failed to pay attention to what was going on in the rest of the flat as he used to, and he really should have been prepared to find things changed. But still, still — was this really his father?
paras.uz: Lekin otasi bunday nozikliklarni sezadigan kayfiyatda emasdi. «A!» — deb qichqirdi u kirishi bilanoq, go'yo bir vaqtning o'zida ham g'azablangan, ham xursand bo'lganday ohangda. Gregor boshini eshikdan tortib, otasiga qarab ko'tardi. U otasini hozir qanday turgan bo'lsa, shunday tasavvur qilmagan edi; to'g'ri, so'nggi paytlarda yangi o'rmalash bilan ovora bo'lib, kvartiraning qolgan qismida nimalar bo'layotganiga avvalgidek e'tibor bermay qo'ygan edi va aslida o'zgargan vaziyatga duch kelishga tayyor bo'lishi kerak edi. Shunga qaramay, shunga qaramay, nahotki bu otasi bo'lsa?

paras.en: The same man who used to lie buried wearily in bed when Gregor set off on a business trip; who, on the evenings when he came home, used to receive him sitting in an armchair in his dressing gown, not really able to get up, but only raising his arms as a sign of joy; and who, on the rare walks they took together on a few Sundays a year and on the most important holidays, walked between Gregor and his mother, who walked slowly anyway, even a little more slowly than they did, wrapped in his old coat, always carefully setting down his walking stick, and who, when he wanted to say something, nearly always stopped and gathered his companions around him?
paras.uz: Ilgari Gregor ish safariga jo'nayotganda charchab karavotga ko'milib yotadigan o'sha odam; uyga qaytgan oqshomlarda uni xalat kiyib kresloda o'tirgan holda kutib oladigan, o'rnidan turishga ham qurbi yetmay, faqat xursandchilik belgisi sifatida qo'llarini ko'taradigan; yiliga bir necha yakshanba va eng katta bayramlarda kamdan-kam birga sayr qilganlarida, o'zi ham sekin yuradigan Gregor bilan onasi o'rtasida, ulardan ham sal sekinroq, eski paltosiga o'ranib, hassasini doim ehtiyotkorlik bilan qo'yib, zo'rg'a oldinga yuradigan va biror narsa aytmoqchi bo'lsa, deyarli har doim to'xtab, hamrohlarini atrofiga to'playdigan o'sha odammi?

paras.en: Now, however, he was standing up very straight, dressed in a tight blue uniform with gold buttons, like those worn by doormen at banks. Above the high, stiff collar of his jacket his strong double chin bulged out; under his bushy eyebrows the gaze of his black eyes shot out, fresh and alert; his white hair, usually untidy, was combed flat into a painfully precise, shining parting. He threw his cap, which had a gold monogram on it, probably that of a bank, in an arc across the whole room onto the sofa, and, with the tails of his long uniform jacket pushed back and his hands in his trouser pockets, he walked towards Gregor with a grim face.
paras.uz: Endi esa u bank xizmatchilari kiyadigan oltin tugmali tor ko'k formada qaddini rostlab turardi; kamzulning baland, qattiq yoqasi ustidan baquvvat ikki qavat iyagi bo'rtib chiqqan; qalin qoshlari ostidan qora ko'zlarining tetik va hushyor nigohi otilib chiqardi; odatda to'zg'igan oq sochlari g'oyat aniq, yaltiroq farq qilib taralgan edi. U ustida, ehtimol, bankning oltin monogrammasi bo'lgan furajkasini butun xona osha yoy chizdirib divanga otdi va uzun forma kamzulining etaklarini orqaga qayirib, qo'llarini shim cho'ntaklariga solgancha, tishini tishiga qo'yib, Gregor tomon yurdi.

paras.en: He probably did not know himself what he intended to do; still, he lifted his feet unusually high, and Gregor was amazed at the gigantic size of the soles of his boots. But he did not dwell on this; he had known since the first day of his new life that his father considered only the greatest strictness appropriate towards him. And so he ran ahead of his father, stopped when his father stood still, and hurried forward again as soon as his father made the slightest movement. In this way they went round the room several times without anything decisive happening; in fact, because of its slow pace, the whole thing did not even look like a chase.
paras.uz: U o'zi ham nima qilmoqchi ekanini bilmasa kerak; har holda oyoqlarini g'ayrioddiy baland ko'tarardi va Gregor uning etik tagliklarining ulkanligidan hayratda qoldi. Lekin u bunga e'tibor berib to'xtab qolmadi, axir yangi hayotining birinchi kunidan beri otasi unga nisbatan faqat eng qattiq qo'llikni o'rinli deb bilishini bilardi. Shuning uchun u otasidan oldinda yugurar, otasi to'xtasa to'xtar va otasi sal qimirlashi bilanoq yana oldinga shoshilardi. Shu tarzda ular hech qanday hal qiluvchi narsa yuz bermasdan xona atrofida bir necha marta aylanishdi; hatto sekin sur'ati tufayli bularning bari ta'qibga ham o'xshamasdi.

paras.en: That was why Gregor stayed on the floor for the time being, especially as he was afraid his father might regard an escape onto the walls or the ceiling as particularly wicked. Admittedly, Gregor had to tell himself that he could not keep up even this running for long, for while his father took one step, he had to make countless movements. He was already beginning to be short of breath, just as even in his earlier days he had never had entirely reliable lungs.
paras.uz: Shuning uchun Gregor hozircha polda qoldi, ayniqsa otasi devor yoki shiftga qochishni alohida yovuzlik deb hisoblashidan qo'rqardi. To'g'ri, Gregor o'ziga hatto bunday yugurishga ham uzoq chiday olmasligini aytishga majbur edi, chunki otasi bir qadam tashlaganda u son-sanoqsiz harakat qilishi kerak edi. Nafas qisishi allaqachon sezila boshlagan edi; axir u ilgari ham unchalik ishonchli o'pkaga ega emasdi.

paras.en: As he staggered along like this, gathering all his strength for running, hardly keeping his eyes open; as in his dazed state he did not even think of any other way of escape than running; and as he had almost forgotten that the walls were free to him — though here they were blocked by carefully carved furniture full of points and spikes — something flew down right beside him, lightly thrown, and rolled in front of him. It was an apple; a second one immediately flew after it. Gregor stopped in terror; there was no point in running any further, for his father had decided to bombard him.
paras.uz: U yugurish uchun bor kuchini yig'ib, ko'zlarini arang ochiq tutib, gangigan holda qochishdan boshqa najot yo'lini o'ylamay va devorlar unga ochiq ekanini deyarli unutib — garchi bu yerda ular o'ymakor naqshlar bilan bezatilgan, o'tkir uchli va tishli mebellar bilan to'silgan bo'lsa ham — shu tarzda gandiraklab borarkan, uning yonginasiga nimadir yengil otilib tushdi va oldida dumalab ketdi. Bu olma edi; darhol ortidan ikkinchisi uchib keldi; Gregor qo'rqib to'xtab qoldi; yugurishni davom ettirishning ma'nosi yo'q edi, chunki otasi uni o'qqa tutishga qaror qilgan edi.

paras.en: He had filled his pockets from the fruit bowl on the sideboard and was now throwing apple after apple, without aiming carefully for the moment. These little red apples rolled around on the floor as if electrified and bumped into each other. One weakly thrown apple grazed Gregor's back but slid off harmlessly. One that flew right after it, however, actually forced its way into Gregor's back. Gregor wanted to drag himself on, as if this surprising, incredible pain might pass if he changed his position; but he felt as if he had been nailed to the spot and stretched out in complete confusion of all his senses.
paras.uz: U bufet ustidagi meva idishidan cho'ntaklarini to'ldirib olgan va endi hozircha unchalik nishonga olmay, olma ketidan olma otardi. Bu mayda qizil olmalar go'yo elektr urganday polda dumalab, bir-biriga urilardi. Kuchsiz otilgan bir olma Gregorning orqasiga tegib o'tdi, lekin zararsiz sirg'alib tushdi. Uning ortidan darhol uchib kelgan boshqasi esa Gregorning orqasiga rostakamiga botib kirdi. Gregor go'yo bu kutilmagan, aql bovar qilmaydigan og'riq joyini o'zgartirsa o'tib ketadiganday, sudralib ketmoqchi bo'ldi; lekin o'zini mixlab qo'yilganday his qildi va barcha sezgilari butunlay chalkashib, cho'zilib qoldi.

paras.en: With his last glance he saw the door of his room being torn open, and his mother rushing out ahead of his screaming sister, in her chemise, for his sister had undressed her to help her breathe while she was unconscious. He saw his mother run towards his father, and on the way her loosened skirts slipped to the floor one after the other; and he saw how, stumbling over the skirts, she rushed at his father and, embracing him, in complete union with him — but now Gregor's sight was already failing — with her hands behind his father's head, begged him to spare Gregor's life.
paras.uz: Oxirgi nigohi bilan u o'z xonasining eshigi yulqib ochilganini va qichqirayotgan singlisidan oldinda ich ko'ylakda onasi otilib chiqqanini ko'rdi — chunki singlisi hushidan ketganida bemalol nafas olishi uchun uni yechintirgan edi; so'ng onasi otasi tomon yugurganini va yo'lda bog'ichlari bo'shatilgan yubkalari birin-ketin yerga sirg'alib tushganini, yubkalarga qoqilib, otasiga tashlanganini va uni quchoqlab, u bilan butunlay bir bo'lib — lekin endi Gregorning ko'zlari ko'rmay qolayotgan edi — qo'llarini otasining ensasiga qo'yib, Gregorning hayotini ayashni yolvorib so'raganini ko'rdi.

gloss.ex: ...the monotonous life in the middle of the family.

...like a great commotion coming at him.

quiz.why_uz: Onasining ovozi unga odamlik o'tmishini unutmaslik kerakligini eslatadi.

quiz.why_uz: U suratga yopishib, uni tanasi bilan to'sib oladi — bu uning odam hayotidan qolgan so'nggi narsalardan biri.

quiz.why_uz: Otasi otgan olma Gregorning orqasiga botib qoladi va keyinchalik uning o'limiga sabab bo'ladi.

chapters.note_uz: Ikkinchi qismning cho'qqisi. Ota endi zaif keksa emas, kuchli forma kiygan odam — oila Gregorsiz ham «tiklanmoqda». Olma — Injildagi gunoh mevasini eslatuvchi ramz: aynan ota qo'lidan kelgan mevadan Gregor yaralanadi. Onaning yolvorishi esa oilada hali mehr borligini ko'rsatadi.

chapters.title: The Open Door
chapters.recap_uz: Olma Gregorning orqasida qolib, uni nogiron qiladi. Kechqurunlari eshik ochiq qoldiriladi va u charchagan oilani kuzatadi: ota bankda xizmatchi, ona tikuvchi, Grete sotuvchi. Uyga keksa xizmatkor ayol keladi, uch ijarachi joylashadi. Gregorning xonasi keraksiz buyumlar omboriga aylanadi, u deyarli ovqat yemay qo'yadi.

paras.en: Gregor's serious wound, from which he suffered for over a month — the apple stayed lodged in his flesh as a visible reminder, since nobody dared to remove it — seemed to have reminded even his father that, in spite of his present sad and disgusting shape, Gregor was a member of the family who must not be treated like an enemy. On the contrary, the duty of the family required them to swallow their disgust and to tolerate him, simply to tolerate him.
paras.uz: Gregorning bir oydan ortiq azob chekkan og'ir jarohati — olmani hech kim olib tashlashga jur'at etmagani uchun u ko'zga ko'rinadigan esdalik sifatida go'shtida qolib ketdi — hatto otasiga ham Gregor hozirgi g'amgin va jirkanch qiyofasiga qaramay, oila a'zosi ekanini, unga dushmanday munosabatda bo'lib bo'lmasligini eslatganday bo'ldi; aksincha, oilaviy burch nafratni yutib, uni toqat qilishni, faqat toqat qilishni talab qilardi.

paras.en: And although Gregor had probably lost much of his ability to move for ever because of his wound, and for the time being needed long, long minutes to cross his room like an old invalid — crawling up high was out of the question — he received for this worsening of his condition what he considered completely sufficient compensation. Every evening the living-room door, which he used to watch closely for an hour or two beforehand, was opened, so that, lying in the darkness of his room and invisible from the living room, he could see the whole family at the lit table and listen to their conversation — with general permission, as it were, and therefore quite differently from before.
paras.uz: Garchi Gregor jarohati tufayli harakatchanligining katta qismini, ehtimol, bir umrga yo'qotgan va hozircha xonasini kesib o'tish uchun keksa nogironday uzoq-uzoq daqiqalar kerak bo'lsa ham — balandda o'rmalash haqida gap bo'lishi mumkin emasdi — ahvolining bu yomonlashuvi evaziga u o'zining fikricha mutlaqo yetarli tovon oldi: har kuni kechqurun mehmonxona eshigi ochilar edi — u bunga bir-ikki soat oldindan diqqat bilan qarab turardi — shu tufayli u o'z xonasining qorong'isida yotib, mehmonxonadan ko'rinmagan holda butun oilani yoritilgan stol atrofida ko'rishi va ularning suhbatini, go'yo hammaning ruxsati bilan, ya'ni avvalgidan butunlay boshqacha tinglashi mumkin edi.

paras.en: Of course, these were no longer the lively conversations of earlier times, which Gregor had always thought of with some longing in small hotel rooms when he had to throw himself, exhausted, onto damp bedding. Now things were mostly very quiet. His father fell asleep in his armchair soon after supper; his mother and sister urged each other to be quiet; his mother, bent far forward under the light, sewed fine underwear for a fashion shop; his sister, who had taken a job as a shop assistant, studied shorthand and French in the evenings, so as perhaps to get a better position one day.
paras.uz: Albatta, bular endi Gregor kichik mehmonxona xonalarida holdan toyib nam ko'rpa-to'shakka o'zini tashlaganida doim biroz sog'inch bilan eslaydigan avvalgi qizg'in suhbatlar emasdi. Endi ko'pincha juda jimjit o'tardi. Otasi kechki ovqatdan keyin tezda kreslosida uxlab qolardi; onasi va singlisi bir-birini jim bo'lishga undashardi; onasi chiroqqa engashib, moda do'koni uchun nozik ich kiyimlar tikardi; sotuvchilik ishiga kirgan singlisi esa keyinchalik, balki, yaxshiroq lavozimga erishish uchun kechqurunlari stenografiya va fransuz tilini o'rganardi.

paras.en: Sometimes his father woke up and, as if he did not know at all that he had been asleep, said to his mother: “How long you've been sewing again today!” and immediately fell asleep again, while his mother and sister smiled tiredly at each other.
paras.uz: Ba'zan otasi uyg'onar va go'yo uxlaganini umuman bilmaganday, onasiga: «Bugun yana qancha uzoq tikding-a!» — der va darhol yana uxlab qolardi, onasi bilan singlisi esa bir-biriga charchoq bilan jilmayib qo'yishardi.

paras.en: With a kind of obstinacy, his father refused to take off his messenger's uniform even at home; and while his dressing gown hung uselessly on its hook, his father dozed fully dressed in his place, as if he were always ready for duty and were waiting even here for the voice of his superior. As a result, the uniform, which had not been new to begin with, became less and less clean in spite of all the care his mother and sister took, and Gregor often spent whole evenings looking at this garment, covered in stains all over and shining with its always polished gold buttons, in which the old man slept extremely uncomfortably and yet peacefully.
paras.uz: Qandaydir o'jarlik bilan otasi uyda ham xizmatchi formasini yechishdan bosh tortardi; xalati esa ilgakda befoyda osilib turar, otasi go'yo doim xizmatga tayyorday va bu yerda ham boshlig'ining ovozini kutayotganday, to'liq kiyingan holda o'z joyida mudrardi. Natijada boshidan ham yangi bo'lmagan forma ona va singlisining barcha g'amxo'rligiga qaramay tobora kirlanib bordi va Gregor ko'pincha butun oqshomlar bo'yi butunlay dog'larga to'lgan, doim yaltiratib qo'yilgan oltin tugmalari bilan yaltirab turgan bu kiyimga qarab o'tirardi; keksa odam unda juda noqulay, lekin xotirjam uxlardi.

paras.en: As soon as the clock struck ten, his mother would try to wake his father by talking to him gently and then persuade him to go to bed, for this was no proper sleep, and his father, who had to start work at six, badly needed proper sleep. But with the obstinacy that had taken hold of him since he had become a messenger, he always insisted on staying at the table longer, although he regularly fell asleep, and then it took the greatest effort to get him to exchange the armchair for the bed. However much his mother and sister urged him with little reminders, for a quarter of an hour at a time he would slowly shake his head, keep his eyes shut and not get up.
paras.uz: Soat o'nni urishi bilanoq onasi otasini muloyim gaplar bilan uyg'otishga, so'ngra uxlashga yotishga ko'ndirishga urinardi, chunki bu yerdagi uyqu haqiqiy uyqu emasdi, soat oltida xizmatga chiqishi kerak bo'lgan otasiga esa haqiqiy uyqu juda zarur edi. Lekin xizmatchi bo'lganidan beri uni egallab olgan o'jarlik bilan u doimo muntazam uxlab qolishiga qaramay, stolda yana uzoqroq o'tirishni talab qilardi va keyin kreslo'ni karavotga almashtirishga uni katta qiyinchilik bilan ko'ndirish mumkin edi. Onasi va singlisi qanchalik kichik eslatmalar bilan qistamasin, u chorak soatlab sekin bosh chayqar, ko'zlarini yumib turar va o'rnidan turmasdi.

paras.en: His mother would tug at his sleeve and whisper flattering words in his ear; his sister would leave her studies to help her mother; but none of it worked on his father. He only sank deeper into his armchair. Only when the women took hold of him under the arms did he open his eyes, look at his mother and his sister in turn, and usually say: “This is a life. This is the peace and quiet of my old age.” And, leaning on the two women, he would get up laboriously, as if he were the heaviest burden to himself, let the women lead him to the door, wave them away there and go on by himself, while his mother quickly threw down her sewing and his sister her pen so as to run after him and go on helping him.
paras.uz: Onasi uning yengidan tortar, qulog'iga erkalovchi so'zlar shivirlardi, singlisi onasiga yordam berish uchun mashg'ulotini tashlab qo'yardi, lekin otasiga bu ta'sir qilmasdi. U kreslosiga yanada chuqurroq botib ketardi. Faqat ayollar uni qo'ltig'idan ushlagandagina u ko'zlarini ochib, navbatma-navbat onasi va singlisiga qarar va odatda: «Mana hayot. Mana qarilikdagi osoyishtaligim», — derdi. So'ng ikki ayolga tayanib, go'yo o'zi uchun eng og'ir yukday, qiynalib o'rnidan turar, ayollarga uni eshikkacha olib borishga ruxsat berar, u yerda ularga qo'l siltab, o'zi mustaqil davom etardi; onasi esa tikuvini, singlisi qalamini shoshib tashlab, uning ortidan yugurib, unga yana yordam berishardi.

paras.en: Who in this overworked and exhausted family had time to worry about Gregor more than was absolutely necessary? The household was cut back more and more; the maid was dismissed after all; a huge, bony cleaning woman with white hair fluttering around her head came in the mornings and evenings to do the heaviest work; his mother took care of everything else in addition to all her sewing. It even happened that various pieces of family jewellery, which his mother and sister had once worn with great happiness at parties and celebrations, were sold, as Gregor learned in the evening from the general discussion of the prices they had got.
paras.uz: Ishdan holdan toygan va charchagan bu oilada kimning Gregor bilan juda zarur bo'lganidan ortiq shug'ullanishga vaqti bor edi? Ro'zg'or tobora qisqartirildi; oqsoch baribir ishdan bo'shatildi; boshi atrofida oppoq sochlari hilpirab turadigan ulkan, suyakdor xizmatkor ayol eng og'ir ishlarni bajarish uchun ertalab va kechqurun kelardi; qolgan hamma ishni onasi ko'p tikuvchilik ishidan tashqari bajarardi. Hatto ilgari onasi va singlisi ziyofat va bayramlarda katta xursandchilik bilan taqib yurgan oilaviy taqinchoqlar sotilgan ham bo'ldi — Gregor buni kechqurun olingan narxlarning umumiy muhokamasidan bilib oldi.

paras.en: But the biggest complaint was always that they could not leave this flat, which was far too big for their present circumstances, because it was impossible to imagine how Gregor could be moved. But Gregor understood well that it was not only consideration for him that prevented a move, for he could easily have been transported in a suitable box with a few air holes. What mainly kept the family from moving was rather their complete hopelessness and the thought that they had been struck by a misfortune like no one else in their whole circle of relatives and acquaintances.
paras.uz: Lekin eng katta shikoyat doim hozirgi sharoitlar uchun juda katta bo'lgan bu kvartiradan ko'chib keta olmasliklari edi, chunki Gregorni qanday ko'chirish mumkinligini tasavvur qilib bo'lmasdi. Ammo Gregor ko'chishga to'sqinlik qilayotgan narsa faqat unga bo'lgan e'tibor emasligini yaxshi tushunardi, chunki uni bir nechta havo teshigi bo'lgan mos qutida osongina olib ketish mumkin edi; oilani ko'chishdan asosan to'xtatib turgan narsa — to'liq umidsizlik va butun qarindosh-urug' hamda tanishlar doirasida hech kimning boshiga tushmagan baxtsizlikka uchraganlik haqidagi fikr edi.

paras.en: They did everything the world demands of poor people to the utmost: his father fetched breakfast for the junior bank clerks, his mother sacrificed herself for the underwear of strangers, his sister ran back and forth behind the counter at the customers' orders; but the family's strength reached no further. And the wound in his back began to hurt Gregor as if it were new when his mother and sister, having put his father to bed, came back, left their work lying, moved close together and sat cheek to cheek; when his mother, pointing to Gregor's room, said: “Close that door, Grete,” and Gregor was in the dark again, while next door the women mingled their tears, or even stared at the table without tears.
paras.uz: Dunyo kambag'al odamlardan talab qiladigan hamma narsani ular oxirigacha bajarardilar: otasi kichik bank xizmatchilariga nonushta olib kelardi, onasi begonalarning ich kiyimlari uchun o'zini qurbon qilardi, singlisi xaridorlarning buyrug'i bilan peshtaxta ortida u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yugurardi; lekin oilaning kuchi bundan nariga yetmasdi. Onasi va singlisi otasini yotqizib qaytib kelib, ishlarini tashlab, bir-biriga yaqin surilib, yuzma-yuz o'tirganlarida; onasi Gregorning xonasini ko'rsatib: «Anavi eshikni yop, Grete», — deganida va Gregor yana qorong'ilikda qolganida, qo'shni xonada esa ayollar ko'z yoshlarini qo'shib yig'lashar yoki hatto ko'z yoshsiz stolga tikilib qolishardi — shunda Gregorning orqasidagi jarohat xuddi yangiday og'riy boshlardi.

paras.en: Gregor spent the nights and days almost entirely without sleep. Sometimes he thought that the next time the door was opened he would take charge of the family's affairs again just as he used to. In his thoughts, after a long time, the boss and the chief clerk appeared again, the junior clerks and the apprentices, the slow-witted porter, two or three friends from other firms, a chambermaid from a hotel in the provinces — a dear, fleeting memory — and a cashier from a hat shop whom he had courted seriously but too slowly. They all appeared, mixed up with strangers or people he had already forgotten, but instead of helping him and his family, they were all unreachable, and he was glad when they disappeared.
paras.uz: Gregor tunlarni ham, kunlarni ham deyarli uyqusiz o'tkazardi. Ba'zan u eshik navbatdagi ochilganda oila ishlarini yana avvalgidek o'z qo'liga olishni o'ylardi; uzoq vaqtdan keyin xayolida yana xo'jayin va bosh xizmatchi, kichik xizmatchilar va shogirdlar, juda kalta o'ylaydigan farrosh, boshqa firmalardagi ikki-uchta do'sti, viloyatdagi bir mehmonxonaning xizmatkor qizi — shirin, o'tkinchi xotira — va jiddiy, lekin juda sekin sovchilik qilgan shlyapa do'konining kassir qizi paydo bo'ldi. Ularning hammasi begonalar yoki allaqachon unutilganlar bilan aralash paydo bo'lardi, lekin unga va oilasiga yordam berish o'rniga hammasi yetib bo'lmas edi va ular g'oyib bo'lganda u xursand bo'lardi.

paras.en: But then again he was in no mood at all to worry about his family; he was simply filled with rage at how badly he was being looked after. And although he could not think of anything he had an appetite for, he made plans for how he could get into the pantry to take what was, after all, his due, even if he was not hungry. No longer thinking about how she might do Gregor a special favour, his sister now hastily pushed any food at all into Gregor's room with her foot before she ran off to work in the morning and at noon, and in the evening, without caring whether the food had perhaps only been tasted or — the most frequent case — left completely untouched, she swept it out with one swing of the broom.
paras.uz: Lekin keyin u yana oilasi haqida qayg'urish kayfiyatida bo'lmay qolardi, uni faqat yomon qarovdan g'azab qamrab olardi va garchi ishtahasi tortadigan biror narsani tasavvur qila olmasa ham, och bo'lmasa ham, baribir o'ziga haqli bo'lgan narsani olish uchun omborxonaga qanday kirib olish rejalarini tuzardi. Endi Gregorga qanday qilib alohida yoqadigan narsa qilish haqida o'ylamay, singlisi ertalab va tushda ishga yugurib ketishdan oldin shoshib, oyog'i bilan istalgan ovqatni Gregorning xonasiga surib qo'yar, kechqurun esa ovqat faqat totib ko'rilganmi yoki — eng ko'p uchraydigan holat — butunlay tegilmay qolganmi, bunga befarq qarab, supurgini bir siltab uni chiqarib tashlardi.

paras.en: The tidying of the room, which she now always did in the evenings, could not have been done any faster. Streaks of dirt ran along the walls, and here and there lay balls of dust and filth. In the beginning, when his sister arrived, Gregor would place himself in particularly telling corners like this, so as to reproach her, in a way, by his position. But he could probably have stayed there for weeks without his sister improving; she saw the dirt just as well as he did, but she had simply decided to leave it.
paras.uz: U endi doim kechqurunlari bajaradigan xona yig'ishtirish bundan tezroq bo'lishi mumkin emasdi. Devorlar bo'ylab kir yo'llar cho'zilib ketgan, u yer-bu yerda chang va axlat yumaloqlari yotardi. Dastlabki paytlarda singlisi kelganda Gregor ana shunday ayniqsa ko'zga tashlanadigan burchaklarga borib turardi, go'yo bu holati bilan unga ta'na qilganday. Lekin u, ehtimol, haftalab o'sha yerda tursa ham, singlisi o'zini o'nglamas edi; u ham kirni xuddi Gregordek ko'rardi, lekin shunchaki uni qoldirishga qaror qilgan edi.

paras.en: At the same time, with a touchiness that was quite new in her and had in fact taken hold of the whole family, she made sure that the tidying of Gregor's room remained her job alone. Once his mother had given Gregor's room a thorough cleaning, which she had only managed after using several buckets of water — all the dampness upset Gregor too, and he lay spread out, bitter and motionless, on the sofa — but his mother did not escape punishment.
paras.uz: Shu bilan birga, unda butunlay yangi bo'lgan va umuman butun oilani egallab olgan nozik ta'sirchanlik bilan u Gregorning xonasini yig'ishtirish faqat o'zining ishi bo'lib qolishini qattiq kuzatardi. Bir marta onasi Gregorning xonasini katta tozalashdan o'tkazgan edi — buni u bir necha chelak suv sarflab, arang uddalagandi; to'g'ri, bu ko'p namlik Gregorni ham xafa qildi va u divan ustida yoyilib, alam bilan qimirlamay yotdi — lekin onasini jazo kutib turardi.

paras.en: For hardly had his sister noticed the change in Gregor's room that evening than, deeply offended, she ran into the living room and, despite her mother's hands raised imploringly, burst into a fit of tears. At first his parents — his father, of course, had been startled out of his armchair — watched in astonishment and helplessness, until they too began to react: his father, on the right, reproached his mother for not leaving the cleaning of Gregor's room to his sister; on the left, by contrast, he shouted at his sister that she would never be allowed to clean Gregor's room again.
paras.uz: Chunki o'sha oqshom singlisi Gregorning xonasidagi o'zgarishni payqashi bilanoq, qattiq ranjib mehmonxonaga yugurdi va onasining yolvorib ko'tarilgan qo'llariga qaramay, yig'idan o'zini to'xtata olmay qoldi; ota-onasi — otasi, albatta, kreslosidan cho'chib turib ketgan edi — avvaliga hayrat va ojizlik bilan qarab turishdi; keyin ular ham harakatga kelishdi: otasi o'ng tomondagi onasini Gregorning xonasini tozalashni singlisiga qoldirmagani uchun koyidi; chap tomonda esa singlisiga Gregorning xonasini endi hech qachon tozalashga ruxsat berilmasligini aytib baqirdi.

paras.en: Meanwhile his mother tried to drag his father, who was beside himself with excitement, into the bedroom; his sister, shaken by sobs, pounded the table with her little fists; and Gregor hissed loudly with rage because it did not occur to anyone to close the door and spare him this sight and this noise.
paras.uz: Bu orada onasi hayajondan o'zini yo'qotgan otasini yotoqxonaga sudrab olib ketishga urinardi; singlisi o'kirib yig'lab, kichkina mushtlari bilan stolni urardi; Gregor esa hech kimning xayoliga eshikni yopib, uni bu manzara va shovqindan asrash kelmagani uchun g'azabdan baland ovozda vishillardi.

paras.en: But even if his sister, exhausted by her work, had grown tired of looking after Gregor as she used to, his mother still need not have taken her place, and Gregor need not have been neglected. For now there was the cleaning woman. This old widow, who with the help of her strong bony frame had probably survived the worst in her long life, had no real horror of Gregor. Without being curious in any way, she had once happened to open the door of Gregor's room and, at the sight of Gregor, who, completely taken by surprise, began to run back and forth although no one was chasing him, she had stood still in amazement with her hands folded in her lap.
paras.uz: Lekin singlisi ishdan holdan toyib, Gregorga avvalgidek g'amxo'rlik qilishdan bezgan bo'lsa ham, uning o'rnini onasi egallashi shart emasdi va Gregorni e'tiborsiz qoldirishning hojati yo'q edi. Chunki endi xizmatkor ayol bor edi. Uzoq umri davomida baquvvat suyak-tuzilishi yordamida eng og'ir kunlarni boshdan kechirgan bo'lsa kerak bo'lgan bu keksa beva Gregordan unchalik jirkanmasdi. U hech qanday qiziqishsiz bir kuni tasodifan Gregorning xonasi eshigini ochib qo'ygan va hech kim quvmasa ham butunlay kutilmaganda u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yugura boshlagan Gregorni ko'rib, qo'llarini qorni ustida qovushtirib, hayron bo'lib turib qolgan edi.

paras.en: Since then she never failed to open the door a little, briefly, every morning and evening and look in at Gregor. At first she even called him over to her with words that she probably thought were friendly, like “Come over here, you old dung beetle!” or “Look at the old dung beetle!” Gregor answered such remarks with nothing at all, but stayed motionless where he was, as if the door had not been opened at all. If only they had ordered this cleaning woman to clean his room every day, instead of letting her disturb him pointlessly whenever she felt like it!
paras.uz: O'shandan beri u har kuni ertalab va kechqurun eshikni sal ochib, Gregorga qarab qo'yishni kanda qilmasdi. Avvaliga u uni o'zicha do'stona deb hisoblagan so'zlar bilan chaqirardi ham: «Qani, bu yoqqa kel, qari go'ng qo'ng'izi!» yoki «Qaranglar, qari go'ng qo'ng'izini!» Bunday murojaatlarga Gregor hech narsa bilan javob bermas, go'yo eshik umuman ochilmaganday joyida qimirlamay qolardi. Qani endi bu xizmatkor ayolga o'z injiqligiga ko'ra uni behuda bezovta qilishga yo'l qo'yish o'rniga, uning xonasini har kuni tozalashni buyurishsa!

paras.en: Once, early in the morning — heavy rain, perhaps already a sign of the coming spring, was beating against the windowpanes — when the cleaning woman started her remarks again, Gregor was so bitter that he turned towards her as if to attack, although slowly and feebly. But instead of being afraid, the cleaning woman simply lifted a chair standing near the door high into the air, and as she stood there with her mouth wide open, her intention was clear: she would only close her mouth when the chair in her hand came crashing down on Gregor's back. “So that's as far as it goes?” she asked when Gregor turned round again, and calmly put the chair back in the corner.
paras.uz: Bir kuni tong saharda — kuchli yomg'ir, balki yaqinlashayotgan bahorning belgisi, oynalarga urilardi — xizmatkor ayol yana o'z gaplarini boshlaganida, Gregor shunchalik g'azablandiki, go'yo hujumga o'tganday, garchi sekin va madorsiz bo'lsa ham, unga qarab burildi. Lekin xizmatkor ayol qo'rqish o'rniga eshik yaqinida turgan stulni boshi uzra baland ko'tardi va og'zini katta ochib turgan qiyofasidan og'zini faqat qo'lidagi stul Gregorning orqasiga tushgandagina yopmoqchi ekani aniq edi. «Xo'sh, bundan nariga o'tmaysanmi?» — deb so'radi u Gregor yana ortiga burilganida va stulni xotirjam burchakka qaytarib qo'ydi.

paras.en: Gregor now ate almost nothing at all. Only when he happened to pass the food that had been put out would he take a bite into his mouth as a kind of game, hold it there for hours, and then usually spit it out again. At first he thought it was his sadness at the state of his room that kept him from eating, but in fact he very soon made his peace with the changes in the room. They had got into the habit of putting things that could not be stored anywhere else into this room, and there were now many such things, since one room of the flat had been rented to three lodgers.
paras.uz: Endi Gregor deyarli hech narsa yemay qo'ydi. Faqat tasodifan tayyorlab qo'yilgan ovqat yonidan o'tib qolsa, o'yin uchun bir tishlam og'ziga olar, uni soatlab og'zida ushlab turar, keyin ko'pincha yana tupurib tashlardi. Avvaliga u ovqat yeyishiga xonasining ahvolidan qayg'urish xalaqit beryapti, deb o'yladi, lekin aynan xonadagi o'zgarishlar bilan u juda tez murosaga keldi. Boshqa joyga sig'maydigan narsalarni shu xonaga qo'yish odat tusiga kirgan edi va endi bunday narsalar ko'p edi, chunki kvartiraning bir xonasini uchta ijarachiga ijaraga berishgan edi.

paras.en: These serious gentlemen — all three had full beards, as Gregor once noticed through a crack in the door — were painfully particular about order, not only in their own room but, since they were now lodging here, in the whole household, and especially in the kitchen. They could not stand useless, let alone dirty, things. Besides, they had brought most of their own furniture with them. For this reason many things had become superfluous; they could not be sold, but nobody wanted to throw them away either. All of them found their way into Gregor's room. So did the ash bin and the rubbish bin from the kitchen.
paras.uz: Bu jiddiy janoblar — Gregor bir marta eshik tirqishidan payqaganidek, uchalasining ham qalin soqoli bor edi — nafaqat o'z xonalarida, balki bu yerda ijarada yashayotganlari uchun butun ro'zg'orda, ayniqsa oshxonada tartibga juda qattiq e'tibor berishardi. Keraksiz, ayniqsa kir narsalarga toqat qilishmasdi. Bundan tashqari, ular mebellarining ko'p qismini o'zlari bilan olib kelishgan edi. Shu sababli ko'p narsalar ortiqcha bo'lib qoldi: ularni sotib bo'lmasdi, lekin tashlab yuborishni ham istashmasdi. Ularning hammasi Gregorning xonasiga ko'chdi. Oshxonadagi kul qutisi va axlat qutisi ham.

paras.en: Anything that was of no use for the moment the cleaning woman, who was always in a great hurry, simply flung into Gregor's room; fortunately Gregor usually saw only the object in question and the hand that held it. Perhaps the cleaning woman intended to fetch the things again when she had time, or to throw them all out at once, but in fact they stayed lying wherever they had landed when first thrown — unless Gregor wound his way through the junk and moved it. At first he did this because he had to, as there was no other free space to crawl in, but later with growing pleasure, although after such wanderings he would lie for hours without moving, tired to death and sad.
paras.uz: Doim juda shoshib yuradigan xizmatkor ayol hozircha keraksiz bo'lgan narsani shunchaki Gregorning xonasiga uloqtirardi; baxtiga, Gregor ko'pincha faqat o'sha buyumni va uni ushlab turgan qo'lni ko'rardi. Balki xizmatkor ayol vaqti kelganda narsalarni qaytarib olib ketish yoki hammasini birdaniga tashlab yuborish niyatida bo'lgandir, lekin aslida ular birinchi otilganda qayerga tushgan bo'lsa, o'sha yerda yotib qolardi — agar Gregor axlat-chaqir orasidan o'tib, ularni qimirlatmasa. Avval u buni majburan qilardi, chunki o'rmalash uchun boshqa bo'sh joy yo'q edi, keyin esa tobora ortib borayotgan zavq bilan, garchi bunday sayrlardan keyin o'lguday charchab, g'amgin holda soatlab qimirlamay yotsa ham.

chapters.title: The Violin
chapters.recap_uz: Grete ijarachilar uchun skripka chaladi. Musiqadan ta'sirlangan Gregor mehmonxonaga chiqib keladi. Ijarachilar uni ko'rib, kvartiradan voz kechishadi va pul to'lamasliklarini aytishadi. Grete birinchi marta: «Bundan qutulishimiz kerak», — deydi.

paras.en: Since the lodgers sometimes also had their supper at home in the shared living room, the living-room door stayed closed on some evenings. But Gregor gave up the opening of the door quite easily; after all, there had been many evenings when it was open and he had not made use of it, but had lain, without the family noticing, in the darkest corner of his room. Once, however, the cleaning woman had left the door to the living room slightly open, and it stayed open even when the lodgers came in that evening and the light was switched on.
paras.uz: Ijarachilar ba'zan kechki ovqatni ham uyda, umumiy mehmonxonada yeyishgani uchun, ba'zi oqshomlarda mehmonxona eshigi yopiq qolardi; lekin Gregor eshikning ochilishidan osongina voz kechardi, axir eshik ochiq bo'lgan ko'p oqshomlarda ham u bundan foydalanmagan, balki oila sezmagan holda xonasining eng qorong'i burchagida yotgan edi. Bir kuni esa xizmatkor ayol mehmonxona eshigini sal ochiq qoldirgan edi va kechqurun ijarachilar kirib, chiroq yoqilganda ham u ochiq qoldi.

paras.en: They sat down at the top of the table, where in earlier times his father, his mother and Gregor had sat, unfolded their napkins and took up their knives and forks. At once his mother appeared in the doorway with a dish of meat, and close behind her his sister with a dish piled high with potatoes. The food was steaming heavily. The lodgers bent over the dishes set before them as if they wanted to inspect them before eating. And indeed the one who sat in the middle, and who seemed to be regarded as an authority by the other two, cut up a piece of meat while it was still on the dish, evidently to find out whether it was tender enough or whether it should perhaps be sent back to the kitchen. He was satisfied, and his mother and sister, who had been watching anxiously, breathed a sigh of relief and began to smile.
paras.uz: Ular ilgari otasi, onasi va Gregor o'tiradigan stolning to'riga o'tirishdi, salfetkalarini yoyishdi va qo'llariga pichoq va sanchqi olishdi. Darhol eshikda go'sht solingan lagan bilan onasi, uning ortidan esa baland qilib uyilgan kartoshkali lagan bilan singlisi paydo bo'ldi. Ovqatdan quyuq bug' ko'tarilardi. Ijarachilar oldilariga qo'yilgan laganlar ustiga, go'yo ovqatdan oldin ularni tekshirmoqchi bo'lganday engashishdi; haqiqatan ham o'rtada o'tirgan va qolgan ikkisi uchun obro'li odam hisoblanadigan kishi go'shtni hali laganda turganida kesib ko'rdi — aftidan, u yetarlicha yumshoqmi yoki uni oshxonaga qaytarib yuborish kerakmi, aniqlash uchun. U mamnun bo'ldi va hayajon bilan qarab turgan ona va singil yengil nafas olib, jilmaya boshlashdi.

paras.en: The family themselves ate in the kitchen. Nevertheless, before going into the kitchen, his father came into this room and, with a single bow, cap in hand, walked once round the table. The lodgers all rose and murmured something into their beards. When they were alone again, they ate in almost complete silence. It seemed strange to Gregor that out of all the various noises of eating he could always pick out the sound of their chewing teeth, as if this were meant to show Gregor that one needed teeth in order to eat, and that one could achieve nothing even with the finest toothless jaws. “I do have an appetite,” Gregor said to himself anxiously, “but not for these things. How these lodgers are feeding themselves, and I'm dying!”
paras.uz: Oilaning o'zi oshxonada ovqatlanardi. Shunga qaramay, otasi oshxonaga o'tishdan oldin bu xonaga kirib, furajkasini qo'lida ushlagancha, bir marta ta'zim qilib stol atrofini aylanib chiqdi. Ijarachilarning hammasi o'rnidan turib, soqollari ichida nimadir deb g'o'ldirashdi. So'ng yolg'iz qolgach, ular deyarli to'liq jimlikda ovqatlanishdi. Gregorga g'alati tuyuldiki, ovqatlanishning har xil tovushlari orasidan doim ularning chaynayotgan tishlari eshitilardi, go'yo bu bilan Gregorga ovqat yeyish uchun tish kerakligi va eng chiroyli tishsiz jag'lar bilan ham hech narsaga erishib bo'lmasligi ko'rsatilmoqchi bo'lganday. «Ishtaham bor-ku, — dedi o'ziga Gregor tashvish bilan, — lekin bu narsalarga emas. Bu ijarachilar qanday to'yib yeyishyapti, men esa o'lib ketyapman!»

paras.en: On that very evening — Gregor could not remember having heard the violin during all this time — it sounded from the kitchen. The lodgers had already finished their supper; the one in the middle had taken out a newspaper and given each of the other two a page, and now they were leaning back, reading and smoking. When the violin began to play, they became attentive, got up and went on tiptoe to the door of the hall, where they stood pressed close together. They must have been heard from the kitchen, for his father called out: “Perhaps the gentlemen find the playing unpleasant? It can be stopped at once.” “On the contrary,” said the middle gentleman, “wouldn't the young lady like to come in to us and play here in the room, where it is much more comfortable and cosy?” “Oh, certainly,” cried his father, as if he were the violinist.
paras.uz: Aynan o'sha oqshom — Gregor shuncha vaqt ichida skripka ovozini eshitganini eslay olmasdi — oshxona tomondan skripka sadosi keldi. Ijarachilar allaqachon kechki ovqatni tugatishgan edi, o'rtadagisi gazeta chiqarib, qolgan ikkisiga bittadan varaq bergan edi va endi ular suyanib o'tirib o'qishar va chekishardi. Skripka chalina boshlaganda ular e'tibor berishdi, o'rnidan turib, oyoq uchida dahliz eshigiga borishdi va u yerda bir-biriga qisilib to'xtab qolishdi. Ularni oshxonadan eshitishgan bo'lsa kerak, chunki otasi: «Janoblarga musiqa yoqmayaptimi? Uni hozir to'xtatish mumkin», — dedi. «Aksincha, — dedi o'rtadagi janob, — oyimtilla bizning oldimizga kirib, ancha qulay va shinam bo'lgan shu xonada chalishni xohlamaydimi?» «O, albatta», — deb qichqirdi otasi, go'yo skripkachi o'zi bo'lganday.

paras.en: The gentlemen went back into the room and waited. Soon his father came with the music stand, his mother with the music and his sister with the violin. His sister calmly got everything ready to play. His parents, who had never let rooms before and therefore overdid their politeness towards the lodgers, did not even dare to sit in their own armchairs. His father leaned against the door, his right hand pushed between two buttons of his buttoned-up livery coat; his mother, however, was offered an armchair by one of the gentlemen, and, since she left the chair where the gentleman had happened to put it, she sat off to one side in a corner.
paras.uz: Janoblar xonaga qaytib kirib, kutishdi. Tez orada otasi nota tokchasi, onasi notalar va singlisi skripka bilan kelishdi. Singlisi xotirjamlik bilan chalishga hamma narsani tayyorladi; ilgari hech qachon xona ijaraga bermagan va shu sababli ijarachilarga nisbatan xushmuomalalikni oshirib yuborgan ota-onasi o'z kreslolariga o'tirishga ham jur'at etmadi; otasi eshikka suyanib, o'ng qo'lini tugmalangan xizmat kamzulining ikki tugmasi orasiga tiqib turardi; onasiga esa janoblardan biri kreslo taklif qildi va u kreslo'ni janob tasodifan qo'ygan joyda qoldirgani uchun bir chetda, burchakda o'tirdi.

paras.en: His sister began to play. His father and mother, each from their own side, attentively followed the movements of her hands. Gregor, drawn by the playing, had ventured a little further forward and already had his head in the living room. He was hardly surprised that recently he had shown so little consideration for the others; once this consideration had been his pride. And yet just now he would have had more reason to hide, for because of the dust that lay everywhere in his room and flew about at the slightest movement, he too was completely covered in dust. He dragged threads, hairs and leftovers of food around with him on his back and sides; his indifference to everything was far too great for him to lie on his back and rub himself against the carpet, as he used to do several times a day. And in spite of this state he felt no shyness about moving forward a little onto the spotless floor of the living room.
paras.uz: Singlisi chala boshladi; otasi va onasi har biri o'z tomonidan uning qo'llari harakatini diqqat bilan kuzatishardi. Musiqaga tortilgan Gregor biroz oldinga jur'at qilib siljigan va boshi allaqachon mehmonxonada edi. So'nggi paytlarda boshqalarga bunchalik kam e'tibor berayotganidan u deyarli ajablanmadi; ilgari bu e'tiborlilik uning faxri edi. Holbuki, aynan hozir uning yashirinishga ko'proq asosi bor edi, chunki xonasida hamma yoqda yotgan va eng kichik harakatdan ko'tariladigan chang tufayli u ham butunlay changga belangan edi; orqasi va yonlarida iplar, sochlar, ovqat qoldiqlarini sudrab yurardi; hamma narsaga befarqligi shunchalik katta ediki, endi avvalgidek kuniga bir necha marta chalqancha yotib, gilamga ishqalanmasdi. Va shu ahvoliga qaramay, mehmonxonaning beg'ubor poli ustiga biroz oldinga siljishdan tortinmadi.

paras.en: Admittedly, nobody paid any attention to him either. The family was completely absorbed in the violin playing. The lodgers, on the other hand, who had at first placed themselves, hands in their trouser pockets, much too close behind his sister's music stand, so that they could all have read the music, which must certainly have disturbed his sister, soon withdrew to the window, talking in low voices with their heads bowed, and stayed there, anxiously watched by his father. It now really looked all too obvious that they had been disappointed in their expectation of hearing beautiful or entertaining violin playing, that they were tired of the whole performance and were only allowing their peace to be disturbed out of politeness. Especially the way they all blew the smoke of their cigars high into the air from their noses and mouths suggested great nervousness.
paras.uz: To'g'ri, unga hech kim e'tibor bermasdi ham. Oila butunlay skripka sadosiga berilib ketgan edi; ijarachilar esa, avval qo'llarini shim cho'ntaklariga solib, singlisining nota tokchasi orqasida juda yaqin turib olishgandi — shunchalik yaqinki, hammasi notalarni ko'ra olardi, bu esa singlisiga xalaqit bergan bo'lishi aniq — tez orada boshlarini egib, pastroq ovozda gaplashgancha deraza yoniga chekinishdi va otasi tashvish bilan kuzatib turgan holda o'sha yerda qolishdi. Endi ular go'zal yoki ko'ngilochar skripka chalinishini eshitish umidida aldanganlari, butun tomoshadan zerikkanlari va faqat xushmuomalalikdan osoyishtaliklari buzilishiga chidab turganlari haddan tashqari aniq ko'rinib qoldi. Ayniqsa ularning hammasi sigara tutunini burun va og'zidan yuqoriga puflashlari katta asabiylikdan dalolat berardi.

paras.en: And yet his sister was playing so beautifully. Her face was tilted to one side, and her eyes followed the lines of music searchingly and sadly. Gregor crawled a little further forward and held his head close to the floor, so that he might perhaps meet her eyes. Was he an animal, if music moved him so? He felt as if the way to the unknown nourishment he longed for were opening before him. He was determined to push on as far as his sister, to tug at her skirt and so let her know that she should come into his room with her violin, for no one here appreciated her playing as he would appreciate it.
paras.uz: Holbuki singlisi juda chiroyli chalardi. Uning yuzi bir tomonga egilgan, ko'zlari nota satrlarini sinchkovlik va qayg'u bilan kuzatardi. Gregor yana biroz oldinga o'rmaladi va, ehtimol, uning nigohi bilan uchrashish uchun boshini yerga yaqin tutdi. Musiqa unga shunchalik ta'sir qilsa, nahotki u hayvon bo'lsa? Unga go'yo intizor bo'lgan noma'lum ozuqaga yo'l ochilayotganday tuyuldi. U singlisigacha yetib borishga, uning etagidan tortib, skripkasi bilan uning xonasiga kirishi kerakligiga ishora qilishga qaror qildi, chunki bu yerda hech kim uning chalishini u qadrlamoqchi bo'lganchalik qadrlamasdi.

paras.en: He did not want to let her out of his room any more, at least not as long as he lived; his terrifying shape would be useful to him for the first time; he wanted to be at all the doors of his room at once and hiss at the attackers. His sister, however, should not be forced to stay with him but should stay of her own free will; she should sit beside him on the sofa and bend her ear down to him, and he would then confide in her that he had firmly intended to send her to the conservatory, and that, if the misfortune had not come in between, he would have told everyone so last Christmas — surely Christmas was over by now? — without caring about any objections.
paras.uz: U uni endi xonasidan chiqarmoqchi emasdi, hech bo'lmasa o'zi tirik ekan; uning qo'rqinchli qiyofasi birinchi marta unga foyda keltirishi kerak edi; u bir vaqtning o'zida xonasining barcha eshiklari oldida bo'lib, hujumchilarga vishillamoqchi edi; singlisi esa majburan emas, o'z ixtiyori bilan uning yonida qolishi kerak edi; u uning yonida divanda o'tirib, qulog'ini unga egishi kerak edi, shunda u unga uni konservatoriyaga yuborishga qat'iy niyat qilganini va agar bu baxtsizlik o'rtaga tushmaganida, o'tgan Rojdestvoda — Rojdestvo allaqachon o'tib ketgandir-a? — hech qanday e'tirozlarga qaramay, buni hammaga aytgan bo'lishini sirlashib aytmoqchi edi.

paras.en: After this declaration his sister would burst into tears of emotion, and Gregor would raise himself up to her shoulder and kiss her neck, which, since she had started going to work, she had worn bare, without a ribbon or collar.
paras.uz: Bu so'zlardan keyin singlisi hayajondan yig'lab yuborardi, Gregor esa uning yelkasigacha ko'tarilib, ishga qatnay boshlaganidan beri tasma yoki yoqasiz ochiq yuradigan bo'ynidan o'pardi.

paras.en: “Mr Samsa!” the middle gentleman called out to his father and, without wasting another word, pointed with his forefinger at Gregor, who was slowly moving forward. The violin fell silent. The middle lodger first smiled at his friends, shaking his head, and then looked at Gregor again. His father seemed to think it more necessary to calm the lodgers first instead of driving Gregor away, although they were not at all upset and Gregor seemed to entertain them more than the violin playing had. He hurried over to them and, with his arms spread out, tried to push them into their room and at the same time to block their view of Gregor with his body.
paras.uz: «Janob Samsa!» — deb qichqirdi o'rtadagi janob otasiga va boshqa so'z sarflamay, ko'rsatkich barmog'i bilan asta oldinga siljiyotgan Gregorni ko'rsatdi. Skripka jim bo'ldi; o'rtadagi ijarachi avval do'stlariga qarab boshini chayqab jilmaydi, keyin yana Gregorga qaradi. Otasi Gregorni haydash o'rniga avval ijarachilarni tinchlantirish zarurroq, deb hisoblaganday bo'ldi, garchi ular umuman hayajonlanmagan va Gregor ularni skripkadan ko'ra ko'proq qiziqtirayotganday ko'rinsa ham. U ularning oldiga shoshilib bordi va qo'llarini yoyib, ularni xonalariga itarib kiritishga va shu bilan birga tanasi bilan ularning Gregorga bo'lgan nigohini to'sishga urindi.

paras.en: Now they really did become a little angry, though it was no longer clear whether at his father's behaviour or at the realisation now dawning on them that, without knowing it, they had had a neighbour like Gregor. They demanded explanations from his father, raised their own arms, tugged restlessly at their beards and only slowly retreated towards their room.
paras.uz: Endi ular chindan ham biroz achchiqlanishdi — otasining xatti-harakatidanmi yoki bilmagan holda Gregorday qo'shni bilan yashaganliklari endi ayon bo'layotganidanmi, buni endi bilib bo'lmasdi. Ular otasidan tushuntirish talab qilishdi, o'zlari ham qo'llarini ko'tarishdi, bezovtalanib soqollarini tortqilashdi va faqat sekin-asta o'z xonalari tomon chekinishdi.

paras.en: Meanwhile his sister had overcome the state of loss into which she had fallen after her playing was so suddenly broken off. For a while she had held the violin and bow in her loosely hanging hands and gone on looking at the music as if she were still playing; then all at once she pulled herself together, laid the instrument in the lap of her mother, who was still sitting in her armchair struggling for breath, her lungs heaving, and ran into the next room, which the lodgers, pushed on by his father, were now approaching more quickly. One could see the blankets and pillows on the beds fly up and arrange themselves under his sister's practised hands. Even before the gentlemen had reached the room, she had finished making the beds and slipped out.
paras.uz: Bu orada singlisi chalish to'satdan to'xtatilgandan keyin tushib qolgan sarosimani yengib o'tdi; u bir muddat bo'shashgan qo'llarida skripka va kamonni ushlab, go'yo hali chalayotganday notalarga qarab turdi, keyin birdan o'zini qo'lga olib, cholg'uni hali ham kreslosida o'pkasi qattiq ishlab nafas olishga qiynalib o'tirgan onasining tizzasiga qo'ydi va otasi itarishi bilan ijarachilar endi tezroq yaqinlashayotgan qo'shni xonaga yugurdi. Singlisining malakali qo'llari ostida karavotlardagi ko'rpa va yostiqlar havoga ko'tarilib, tartibga tushayotgani ko'rinardi. Janoblar xonaga yetib kelmasdanoq u to'shaklarni yozib bo'lib, sirg'alib chiqib ketdi.

paras.en: His father again seemed so gripped by his obstinacy that he forgot all the respect he did, after all, owe his tenants. He just kept pushing and pushing, until in the very doorway of the room the middle gentleman stamped his foot thunderously and so brought his father to a halt. “I hereby declare,” he said, raising his hand and looking round for the mother and sister too, “that in view of the disgusting conditions prevailing in this flat and this family” — here he spat decisively on the floor — “I give notice on my room with immediate effect. Of course I shall not pay the slightest amount for the days I have lived here either; on the contrary, I shall consider whether I shall not bring some claims against you, which — believe me — would be very easy to justify.”
paras.uz: Otasi yana shunday o'jarlikka berilib ketdiki, ijarachilariga baribir qarzdor bo'lgan barcha hurmatni unutdi. U faqat itarar va itarardi, toki xona eshigining o'zida o'rtadagi janob oyog'ini qattiq yerga urib, otasini to'xtatmaguncha. «Shu bilan e'lon qilaman, — dedi u qo'lini ko'tarib va nigohi bilan onani va singlini ham izlab, — bu kvartira va oilada hukm surayotgan jirkanch sharoitlarni hisobga olib, — shu yerda u qat'iyat bilan yerga tupurdi, — xonamdan darhol voz kechaman. Albatta, bu yerda yashagan kunlarim uchun ham zarracha haq to'lamayman, aksincha, sizga qarshi qandaydir — ishoning, juda oson asoslanadigan — talablar bilan chiqmasam-mi, deb hali o'ylab ko'raman».

paras.en: He fell silent and looked straight ahead, as if he were expecting something. And indeed his two friends at once joined in with the words: “We too give notice with immediate effect.” Then he seized the door handle and shut the door with a crash.
paras.uz: U jim bo'lib, go'yo nimanidir kutayotganday to'g'riga qarab turdi. Haqiqatan ham uning ikki do'sti darhol: «Biz ham darhol voz kechamiz», — deb gapga qo'shildi. Shundan so'ng u eshik dastasini ushlab, eshikni gursillatib yopdi.

paras.en: His father staggered to his armchair, feeling his way with his hands, and let himself fall into it. It looked as if he were stretching out for his usual evening nap, but the heavy nodding of his head, which seemed to have lost all support, showed that he was not asleep at all. Gregor had been lying quietly the whole time on the spot where the lodgers had caught him. The disappointment at the failure of his plan, but perhaps also the weakness caused by so much hunger, made it impossible for him to move. He feared with a certain certainty that at the very next moment everything would collapse on top of him, and he waited. He was not even startled by the violin, which slipped from under his mother's trembling fingers, fell from her lap and gave out a ringing sound.
paras.uz: Otasi qo'llari bilan paypaslab kreslosi tomon gandiraklab bordi va o'zini unga tashladi; go'yo odatdagi kechki mudrog'iga cho'zilayotganday ko'rinardi, lekin go'yo tayanchini yo'qotgan boshining qattiq tebranishi uning umuman uxlamayotganini ko'rsatardi. Gregor butun vaqt davomida ijarachilar uni ushlab olgan joyda jimgina yotardi. Rejasining barbod bo'lganidan hafsalasi pir bo'lgani, balki uzoq ochlik keltirib chiqargan holsizlik ham uning qimirlashini imkonsiz qildi. U qandaydir ishonch bilan keyingi lahzadayoq hamma narsa uning ustiga qulab tushishidan qo'rqar va kutardi. Hatto onasining titrayotgan barmoqlari ostidan sirg'alib, tizzasidan yerga tushib, jarangdor ovoz chiqargan skripka ham uni cho'chitmadi.

paras.en: “Dear parents,” said his sister, striking the table with her hand by way of introduction, “things can't go on like this. Perhaps you don't realise it, but I do. I won't say my brother's name in front of this monster, and so I'll only say: we must try to get rid of it. We have done everything humanly possible to look after it and to put up with it; I don't think anyone can blame us in the slightest.”
paras.uz: «Aziz ota-onam, — dedi singlisi va so'z boshlash uchun qo'li bilan stolga urdi, — bunday davom etib bo'lmaydi. Agar sizlar buni tushunmasangiz, men tushunaman. Men bu maxluq oldida akamning ismini aytmayman va shuning uchun faqat aytaman: biz undan qutulishga harakat qilishimiz kerak. Biz unga qarash va unga toqat qilish uchun inson qo'lidan kelgan hamma narsani qildik; menimcha, hech kim bizni zarracha ham ayblay olmaydi».

paras.en: “She's absolutely right,” said his father to himself. His mother, who still could not get enough breath, began to cough hollowly into her hand, with a wild look in her eyes. His sister hurried to her mother and held her forehead. His father seemed to have been led by his sister's words to more definite thoughts; he had sat up straight and was playing with his messenger's cap among the plates still on the table from the lodgers' supper, looking now and then at the silent Gregor.
paras.uz: «U ming marta haq», — dedi otasi o'zicha. Hamon yetarlicha nafas ololmayotgan onasi ko'zlarida telbanamo ifoda bilan og'ziga tutgan qo'liga bo'g'iq yo'tala boshladi. Singlisi onasining oldiga shoshilib, uning peshonasini ushlab turdi. Otasi singlisining so'zlaridan aniqroq fikrlarga kelganday bo'ldi: u qaddini rostlab o'tirib oldi, stolda ijarachilarning kechki ovqatidan qolgan likopchalar orasida xizmatchi furajkasini o'ynab, vaqti-vaqti bilan jim yotgan Gregorga qarab qo'yardi.
