Ijarachilar esa musiqani tushunmaydi, lekin «odam» hisoblanadi. Gretaning so'zlari burilish nuqtasi: oila Gregorni endi aka emas, «narsa» deb ko'radi.

chapters.title: The End of March
chapters.recap_uz: Grete Gregordan qutulish kerakligini aytadi, ota rozi bo'ladi. Gregor xonasiga qaytadi va oilasini mehr bilan eslagan holda tongda vafot etadi. Xizmatkor ayol uning jasadini topadi. Oila ijarachilarni haydaydi, dam olish kuni e'lon qilib, shahar tashqarisiga sayrga chiqadi va yangi hayot rejalarini tuzadi.

paras.en: “We must try to get rid of it,” his sister now said to his father alone, for his mother could hear nothing through her coughing. “It will kill you both, I can see it coming. When we all have to work as hard as we do, we can't put up with this endless torment at home as well. I can't stand it any more either.” And she burst into such violent tears that they flowed down onto her mother's face, from which she wiped them away with mechanical movements of her hand. “My child,” said his father with pity and with remarkable understanding, “but what are we to do?” His sister only shrugged her shoulders as a sign of the helplessness that had now seized her while she was crying, in contrast to her earlier confidence.
paras.uz: «Biz undan qutulishga harakat qilishimiz kerak, — dedi endi singlisi faqat otasiga, chunki onasi yo'talidan hech narsa eshitmasdi, — u ikkalangizni ham o'ldiradi, men buni ko'rib turibman. Hammamiz shunchalik og'ir ishlashga majbur ekanmiz, uyda ham bu tugamas azobga chidab bo'lmaydi. Men ham endi chiday olmayman». Va u shunday qattiq yig'lab yubordiki, ko'z yoshlari onasining yuziga oqib tushdi, u esa ularni qo'lining mexanik harakatlari bilan artib turdi. «Bolam, — dedi otasi rahm bilan va ajablanarli darajada tushunib, — lekin nima qilishimiz kerak?» Singlisi faqat yelkasini qisdi — bu avvalgi ishonchidan farqli o'laroq, yig'layotganda uni qamrab olgan ojizlik belgisi edi.

paras.en: “If he understood us,” said his father, half questioningly; his sister, still crying, waved her hand vigorously as a sign that that was out of the question. “If he understood us,” his father repeated, and by closing his eyes he took in his sister's conviction that this was impossible, “then perhaps we could come to some agreement with him. But as it is—”
paras.uz: «Agar u bizni tushunganida edi», — dedi otasi yarim savol ohangida; singlisi yig'lab turib, bu haqda o'ylashning ham hojati yo'q, degan ma'noda qo'lini qattiq siltadi. «Agar u bizni tushunganida edi, — deb takrorladi otasi va ko'zlarini yumib, singlisining buning iloji yo'qligiga bo'lgan ishonchini qabul qildi, — unda, balki, u bilan biror kelishuvga kelish mumkin bo'lardi. Lekin hozir esa...»

paras.en: “It has to go,” cried his sister, “that's the only way, Father. You just have to try to get rid of the idea that it's Gregor. The fact that we believed it for so long is our real misfortune. But how can it be Gregor? If it were Gregor, he would have realised long ago that it isn't possible for people to live with such an animal, and he would have gone away of his own accord. Then we wouldn't have a brother, but we could go on living and honour his memory. But as it is, this animal persecutes us, drives away the lodgers, obviously wants to take over the whole flat and make us spend the night in the street.
paras.uz: «U yo'q bo'lishi kerak, — deb qichqirdi singlisi, — bu yagona yo'l, ota. Siz shunchaki bu Gregor degan fikrdan qutulishga harakat qilishingiz kerak. Bunga shuncha vaqt ishonib kelganimiz — haqiqiy baxtsizligimiz shu. Lekin u qanday qilib Gregor bo'lishi mumkin? Agar u Gregor bo'lganida, odamlar bunday hayvon bilan birga yashay olmasligini allaqachon tushunib, o'z ixtiyori bilan ketib qolgan bo'lardi. Shunda bizning akamiz bo'lmasdi, lekin yashashda davom etib, uning xotirasini hurmat qilishimiz mumkin bo'lardi. Hozir esa bu hayvon bizni ta'qib qilyapti, ijarachilarni haydayapti, aftidan butun kvartirani egallab olib, bizni ko'chada tunashga majbur qilmoqchi.

paras.en: Just look, Father,” she suddenly screamed, “he's starting again!” And in a terror that was completely incomprehensible to Gregor, his sister even left her mother, actually pushed herself away from her chair, as if she would rather sacrifice her mother than stay near Gregor, and rushed behind her father, who, excited merely by her behaviour, also stood up and half raised his arms in front of her as if to protect her.
paras.uz: Qarang, ota, — deb qichqirib yubordi u to'satdan, — u yana boshlayapti!» Va Gregor uchun mutlaqo tushunarsiz qo'rquv bilan singlisi hatto onasini ham tashlab, go'yo Gregorning yaqinida qolgandan ko'ra onasini qurbon qilishni afzal ko'rganday, o'zini kresolodan itarib yubordi va otasining orqasiga yugurdi; otasi esa faqat uning xatti-harakatidan hayajonlanib, o'rnidan turdi va go'yo singlisini himoya qilmoqchi bo'lganday qo'llarini uning oldida yarim ko'tardi.

paras.en: But it did not even occur to Gregor to want to frighten anyone, least of all his sister. He had only begun to turn round in order to go back to his room, and admittedly this looked strange, because in his suffering state he had to help with the difficult turns by using his head, which he raised many times and knocked against the floor. He paused and looked round. His good intention seemed to have been recognised; it had only been a moment's fright. Now they all looked at him in silence and sadness. His mother lay in her armchair with her legs stretched out and pressed together, her eyes almost closing with exhaustion; his father and sister sat side by side, his sister with her arm around her father's neck.
paras.uz: Lekin Gregorning xayoliga hech kimni, ayniqsa singlisini qo'rqitish kelmagan ham edi. U shunchaki o'z xonasiga qaytish uchun burila boshlagan edi va bu, to'g'ri, g'alati ko'rinardi, chunki azobli ahvoli tufayli qiyin burilishlarda boshi bilan yordam berishiga to'g'ri kelardi: u boshini ko'p marta ko'tarib, yerga urardi. U to'xtab, atrofga qaradi. Uning yaxshi niyati tushunilganday bo'ldi; bu faqat bir lahzalik qo'rquv ekan. Endi hamma unga jim va qayg'u bilan qarab turardi. Onasi oyoqlarini cho'zib, bir-biriga jipslab kreslosida yotar, ko'zlari holsizlikdan deyarli yumilib qolayotgandi; otasi va singlisi yonma-yon o'tirishar, singlisi qo'lini otasining bo'yniga qo'ygan edi.

paras.en: “Now perhaps I'm allowed to turn round,” thought Gregor, and began his work again. He could not suppress his panting from the effort and had to rest now and then. Besides, nobody was hurrying him; everything was left to him. When he had completed the turn, he immediately began to go straight back. He was amazed at the great distance that separated him from his room and could not understand how, in his weakness, he had covered the same way a short time ago almost without noticing it. Thinking only of crawling quickly, he hardly noticed that no word, no exclamation from his family disturbed him.
paras.uz: «Endi, balki, burilsam bo'lar», — deb o'yladi Gregor va yana ishiga kirishdi. U zo'riqishdan pishillashini to'xtata olmas va vaqti-vaqti bilan dam olishga majbur edi. Qolaversa, uni hech kim shoshiltirmasdi, hammasi o'z ixtiyoriga qoldirilgan edi. Burilishni tugatgach, u darhol to'g'riga qaytib yura boshladi. U o'zini xonasidan ajratib turgan katta masofadan hayratga tushdi va o'zining holsizligi bilan bundan sal oldin xuddi shu yo'lni deyarli sezmay qanday bosib o'tganini umuman tushunmadi. Faqat tez o'rmalashni o'ylab, u oilasining birorta so'zi, birorta xitobi unga xalaqit bermayotganiga deyarli e'tibor bermadi.

paras.en: Only when he was already in the doorway did he turn his head — not completely, because he felt his neck growing stiff — but he still saw that nothing behind him had changed; only his sister had stood up. His last glance brushed over his mother, who had now fallen fast asleep. Hardly was he inside his room when the door was hastily pushed shut, bolted and locked. Gregor was so startled by the sudden noise behind him that his little legs gave way. It was his sister who had been in such a hurry. She had been standing there ready and waiting; then she had sprung forward lightly — Gregor had not heard her coming at all — and as she turned the key in the lock she cried out to her parents: “At last!”
paras.uz: Faqat eshik oldiga yetganidagina u boshini burdi — butunlay emas, chunki bo'yni qotib qolayotganini sezardi — lekin baribir orqasida hech narsa o'zgarmaganini, faqat singlisi o'rnidan turganini ko'rdi. Uning so'nggi nigohi endi butunlay uxlab qolgan onasiga tushdi. U endigina xonasiga kirgan ediki, eshik shosha-pisha yopildi, zanjirlab qulflandi. Orqasidagi to'satdan chiqqan shovqindan Gregor shunchalik qo'rqib ketdiki, mitti oyoqlari bukilib qoldi. Bunchalik shoshilgan singlisi edi. U tik turib, kutib turgan, keyin yengil sakrab oldinga otilgan edi — Gregor uning kelganini umuman eshitmadi — va qulfdagi kalitni burayotib, ota-onasiga: «Nihoyat!» — deb qichqirdi.

paras.en: “And now?” Gregor asked himself, and looked around in the dark. He soon discovered that he could no longer move at all. He was not surprised at this; rather, it seemed unnatural to him that until now he had really been able to move about on these thin little legs. Otherwise he felt relatively comfortable. True, he had pains all over his body, but it seemed to him that they were gradually growing weaker and weaker and would finally disappear altogether. He could hardly feel the rotten apple in his back any more, nor the inflamed area around it, which was completely covered in soft dust.
paras.uz: «Endi-chi?» — deb so'radi o'zidan Gregor va qorong'ilikda atrofga qaradi. Tez orada u endi umuman qimirlay olmasligini kashf qildi. Bundan u hayron bo'lmadi, aksincha, shu paytgacha bu ingichka mitti oyoqlar bilan rostdan ham harakatlana olgani unga g'ayritabiiy tuyuldi. Qolaversa, u o'zini nisbatan yaxshi his qilardi. To'g'ri, butun tanasi og'rirdi, lekin unga go'yo og'riqlar asta-sekin tobora susayib, oxiri butunlay yo'qolib ketadiganday tuyulardi. Orqasidagi chirigan olmani va butunlay mayin chang bilan qoplangan yallig'langan atrofini u deyarli sezmay qo'ygan edi.

paras.en: He thought back on his family with tenderness and love. His opinion that he must disappear was, if possible, even more decided than his sister's. He remained in this state of empty and peaceful reflection until the church clock struck three in the morning. He still lived to see the beginning of the general brightening outside the window. Then, without his willing it, his head sank down completely, and from his nostrils his last breath flowed weakly out.
paras.uz: U oilasini mehr va muhabbat bilan esladi. U yo'q bo'lishi kerakligi haqidagi fikri, imkoni bo'lsa, singlisinikidan ham qat'iyroq edi. Minoradagi soat tonggi uchni urguncha u ana shu bo'sh va osoyishta o'y-xayol holatida qoldi. Deraza tashqarisida hamma yoq yorisha boshlaganini u hali ko'rib ulgurdi. Keyin uning boshi o'z ixtiyorisiz butunlay pastga tushdi va burun teshiklaridan so'nggi nafasi zaif chiqib ketdi.

paras.en: When the cleaning woman came early in the morning — out of sheer strength and haste she slammed all the doors, however often she had been asked not to, so hard that once she arrived no peaceful sleep was possible anywhere in the flat — at first she found nothing special on her usual short visit to Gregor. She thought he was lying so still on purpose, playing at being offended; she believed him capable of all kinds of intelligence. Because she happened to have the long broom in her hand, she tried to tickle Gregor with it from the doorway. When even that had no effect, she became annoyed and poked Gregor a little, and only when she had pushed him from his place without any resistance did she pay attention.
paras.uz: Ertalab erta xizmatkor ayol kelganida — kuchi va shoshqaloqligidan, necha marta iltimos qilishgan bo'lmasin, u barcha eshiklarni shunday qarsillatib yopardiki, u kelgan zahoti kvartirada hech qanday tinch uyqu bo'lishi mumkin emasdi — Gregorning oldiga odatdagi qisqa kirishida u avvaliga hech qanday alohida narsa topmadi. U Gregor ataylab shunday qimirlamay yotib, xafa bo'lganini ko'rsatyapti, deb o'yladi; u uni har qanday aqlga qodir deb hisoblardi. Qo'lida tasodifan uzun supurgi bo'lgani uchun u eshik oldidan turib, Gregorni u bilan qitiqlab ko'rmoqchi bo'ldi. Bundan ham natija chiqmagach, u achchiqlanib, Gregorni biroz turtib qo'ydi va uni hech qanday qarshiliksiz joyidan surib yuborgandagina e'tibor berdi.

paras.en: When she soon realised the true state of affairs, she opened her eyes wide and whistled to herself, but she did not hang about for long. She tore open the bedroom door and called loudly into the darkness: “Come and have a look, it's croaked; there it lies, dead as a doornail!”
paras.uz: Tez orada haqiqiy ahvolni tushungach, u ko'zlarini katta ochib, o'zicha hushtak chalib qo'ydi, lekin uzoq turmadi: yotoqxona eshigini yulqib ochdi va qorong'ilikka qarab baland ovozda qichqirdi: «Qaranglar-chi, u o'libdi; ana yotibdi, butunlay o'lib qolibdi!»

paras.en: Mr and Mrs Samsa sat up straight in their double bed and had to get over the shock the cleaning woman had given them before they managed to take in her news. But then Mr and Mrs Samsa quickly climbed out of bed, each on their own side; Mr Samsa threw the blanket over his shoulders, Mrs Samsa came out in just her nightdress; and like this they went into Gregor's room. Meanwhile the door of the living room had also opened, where Grete had slept since the lodgers moved in. She was fully dressed, as if she had not slept at all, and her pale face seemed to prove it too.
paras.uz: Samsa er-xotin karavotda tik o'tirishar va xizmatkor ayolning xabarini anglashdan oldin u keltirgan qo'rquvdan o'zlariga kelishlari kerak edi. Keyin esa janob va xonim Samsa har biri o'z tomonidan shoshib karavotdan tushishdi; janob Samsa ko'rpani yelkasiga tashladi, xonim Samsa faqat tungi ko'ylakda chiqdi; shu holda ular Gregorning xonasiga kirishdi. Bu orada ijarachilar ko'chib kelganidan beri Grete uxlaydigan mehmonxonaning eshigi ham ochildi; u go'yo umuman uxlamaganday to'liq kiyingan edi, rangpar yuzi ham buni tasdiqlayotganday edi.

paras.en: “Dead?” said Mrs Samsa, looking up questioningly at the cleaning woman, although she could have checked everything herself and could even have seen it without checking. “I should say so,” said the cleaning woman, and as proof she pushed Gregor's body a good way further to one side with the broom. Mrs Samsa made a movement as if she wanted to stop the broom, but did not do it. “Well,” said Mr Samsa, “now we can thank God.” He crossed himself, and the three women followed his example.
paras.uz: «O'ldimi?» — dedi xonim Samsa va xizmatkor ayolga savol nazari bilan qaradi, garchi hammasini o'zi tekshirib ko'rishi, hatto tekshirmasdan ham bilishi mumkin bo'lsa ham. «Shunday deb o'ylayman», — dedi xizmatkor ayol va isbot sifatida Gregorning jasadini supurgi bilan yana ancha chetga surdi. Xonim Samsa go'yo supurgini to'xtatmoqchi bo'lganday harakat qildi, lekin to'xtatmadi. «Xo'sh, — dedi janob Samsa, — endi Xudoga shukr qilsak bo'ladi». U cho'qindi va uch ayol ham uning ortidan shunday qildi.

paras.en: Grete, who did not take her eyes off the body, said: “Just look how thin he was. Well, he hadn't eaten anything for such a long time. The food came out just as it went in.” And indeed Gregor's body was completely flat and dry; one could only really see this now that it was no longer raised up by the little legs and nothing else distracted the eye.
paras.uz: Jasaddan ko'zini uzmayotgan Grete dedi: «Qaranglar, qanchalik ozib ketgan ekan. Axir u ancha vaqtdan beri hech narsa yemagan edi. Ovqat qanday kirsa, shunday chiqardi». Haqiqatan ham Gregorning tanasi butunlay yassi va quruq edi; buni aslida faqat endi — u mitti oyoqlari bilan ko'tarilib turmagan va nigohni boshqa hech narsa chalg'itmagan paytdagina ko'rish mumkin edi.

paras.en: “Come in to us for a little while, Grete,” said Mrs Samsa with a sad smile, and Grete, not without looking back at the body, followed her parents into the bedroom. The cleaning woman shut the door and opened the window wide. Although it was early in the morning, there was already some mildness mixed in with the fresh air. After all, it was already the end of March.
paras.uz: «Yur, Grete, bir oz oldimizga kir», — dedi xonim Samsa g'amgin jilmayib va Grete jasadga orqaga qarab-qarab, ota-onasining ortidan yotoqxonaga kirdi. Xizmatkor ayol eshikni yopdi va derazani lang ochdi. Erta tong bo'lishiga qaramay, toza havoga allaqachon bir oz iliqlik aralashgan edi. Axir mart oyining oxiri edi.

paras.en: The three lodgers came out of their room and looked around in surprise for their breakfast; they had been forgotten. “Where is the breakfast?” the middle gentleman asked the cleaning woman grumpily. But she put her finger to her lips and then hastily and silently waved to the gentlemen to come into Gregor's room. They came, and then stood around Gregor's body in the now quite bright room, their hands in the pockets of their somewhat worn jackets.
paras.uz: Uch ijarachi xonalaridan chiqib, hayron bo'lib nonushtalarini izlab atrofga qarashdi; ularni unutib qo'yishgan edi. «Nonushta qani?» — deb so'radi o'rtadagi janob xizmatkor ayoldan norozi ohangda. Lekin u barmog'ini labiga qo'ydi, so'ng shoshib va indamay janoblarga Gregorning xonasiga kirishlarini imo qildi. Ular kirishdi va qo'llarini biroz eskirgan kamzullarining cho'ntaklariga solgancha, endi butunlay yorishib ketgan xonada Gregorning jasadi atrofida turishdi.

paras.en: Then the bedroom door opened, and Mr Samsa appeared in his livery, with his wife on one arm and his daughter on the other. They had all been crying a little; Grete pressed her face against her father's arm now and then. “Leave my flat at once!” said Mr Samsa, pointing to the door without letting go of the women. “What do you mean?” said the middle gentleman, somewhat taken aback, with a sugary smile. The other two held their hands behind their backs and kept rubbing them together, as if in joyful expectation of a big quarrel which was bound to turn out in their favour.
paras.uz: Shu payt yotoqxona eshigi ochildi va janob Samsa bir qo'lida xotini, ikkinchisida qizi bilan, xizmat kiyimida ko'rindi. Hammasining ko'zi biroz yig'idan qizargan edi; Grete vaqti-vaqti bilan yuzini otasining qo'liga bosib olardi. «Darhol kvartiramdan chiqib keting!» — dedi janob Samsa ayollarni qo'yib yubormay, eshikni ko'rsatib. «Bu bilan nima demoqchisiz?» — dedi o'rtadagi janob biroz dovdirab va shirin jilmaydi. Qolgan ikkisi qo'llarini orqalariga qilib, tinimsiz bir-biriga ishqalashar, go'yo o'zlari uchun albatta foydali tugaydigan katta janjalni quvonch bilan kutishayotganday edi.

paras.en: “I mean exactly what I say,” answered Mr Samsa, and walked towards the lodger in a line with his two companions. At first the lodger stood still and looked at the floor, as if things were arranging themselves in his head into a new order. “Then we'll go,” he said, and looked up at Mr Samsa as if, in a sudden fit of humility, he needed fresh permission even for this decision. Mr Samsa merely nodded to him several times briefly, with wide eyes. At this the gentleman did indeed go straight into the hall with long strides; his two friends, who had been listening for a while with their hands quite still, now practically hopped after him, as if afraid that Mr Samsa might get into the hall before them and cut them off from their leader.
paras.uz: «Men aynan aytganimni nazarda tutyapman», — dedi janob Samsa va ikki hamrohi bilan bir qatorda ijarachi tomon yurdi. Ijarachi avvaliga jim turib, yerga qaradi, go'yo boshidagi narsalar yangi tartibga tushayotganday. «Unday bo'lsa, ketamiz», — dedi u so'ng va janob Samsaga qaradi, go'yo to'satdan kelgan kamtarlik bilan hatto bu qarori uchun ham yangi ruxsat so'rayotganday. Janob Samsa ko'zlarini katta ochib, unga bir necha marta qisqa bosh irg'ab qo'ydi, xolos. Shundan keyin janob haqiqatan ham darhol katta-katta qadamlar bilan dahlizga chiqdi; bir muncha vaqtdan beri qo'llari butunlay jim bo'lib quloq solib turgan ikki do'sti endi uning ortidan deyarli sakrab ketdi, go'yo janob Samsa ulardan oldin dahlizga kirib, ularni yo'lboshchisidan ajratib qo'yishidan qo'rqqanday.

paras.en: In the hall all three took their hats from the coat rack, pulled their walking sticks out of the stand, bowed silently and left the flat. With a mistrust which proved to be completely unfounded, Mr Samsa went out onto the landing with the two women. Leaning on the banister, they watched the three gentlemen go slowly but steadily down the long stairs, disappearing on each floor at a certain bend of the staircase and coming into view again a few moments later. The lower they got, the more the Samsa family lost interest in them; and when a butcher's boy, carrying a tray on his head, came up towards them with a proud bearing and then climbed high above them, Mr Samsa soon left the banister with the women, and they all went back into their flat as if relieved.
paras.uz: Dahlizda uchalasi ilgichdan shlyapalarini olishdi, tayoq qo'yiladigan joydan hassalarini chiqarishdi, indamay ta'zim qilishdi va kvartirani tark etishdi. Keyin ma'lum bo'lishicha, mutlaqo asossiz bo'lgan ishonchsizlik bilan janob Samsa ikki ayol bilan zinapoya maydonchasiga chiqdi; panjaraga suyanib, ular uch janobning uzun zinadan sekin, lekin tinimsiz tushib borayotganini, har qavatda zinaning ma'lum bir burilishida g'oyib bo'lib, bir necha lahzadan keyin yana paydo bo'layotganini kuzatishdi. Ular qanchalik pastga tushgan sari, Samsalar oilasining ularga qiziqishi shunchalik so'nib bordi va qarshilaridan boshiga patnis qo'ygan qassob shogirdi mag'rur qiyofada ko'tarilib, ularning yonidan yuqoriga o'tib ketganida, janob Samsa ayollar bilan tez orada panjaradan uzoqlashdi va hammasi go'yo yengil tortganday kvartiralariga qaytishdi.

paras.en: They decided to spend that day resting and going for a walk; they had not only earned this break from work, they absolutely needed it. And so they sat down at the table and wrote three letters of excuse: Mr Samsa to his management, Mrs Samsa to her employer, and Grete to the owner of her shop. While they were writing, the cleaning woman came in to say that she was leaving, because her morning work was finished. At first the three writers only nodded without looking up; only when the cleaning woman still would not go away did they look up in annoyance. “Well?” asked Mr Samsa.
paras.uz: Ular bugungi kunni dam olish va sayr qilishga bag'ishlashga qaror qilishdi; ular ishdagi bu tanaffusga nafaqat loyiq edilar, balki unga juda muhtoj ham edilar. Shunday qilib ular stolga o'tirib, uchta uzr xati yozishdi: janob Samsa rahbariyatiga, xonim Samsa buyurtmachisiga, Grete esa do'kon egasiga. Ular yozayotganda xizmatkor ayol ertalabki ishi tugagani uchun ketayotganini aytish uchun kirdi. Yozayotgan uchovlon avvaliga boshlarini ko'tarmay bosh irg'ab qo'yishdi, xolos; faqat xizmatkor ayol hali ham ketmayotganini ko'rgachgina achchiqlanib qarashdi. «Xo'sh?» — deb so'radi janob Samsa.

paras.en: The cleaning woman stood smiling in the doorway, as if she had great good news to tell the family but would only do so if she were questioned thoroughly. The small, almost upright ostrich feather on her hat, which had annoyed Mr Samsa the whole time she had worked for them, swayed lightly in all directions. “So what is it you actually want?” asked Mrs Samsa, whom the cleaning woman respected most. “Well,” answered the cleaning woman, and for friendly laughter could not go on at once, “well, you needn't worry about how to get rid of the thing next door. It's all been taken care of.”
paras.uz: Xizmatkor ayol eshik oldida jilmayib turardi, go'yo oilaga katta xushxabar aytadiganday, lekin buni faqat uni batafsil so'rab-surishtirishsagina aytadiganday. Uning shlyapasidagi deyarli tik turgan kichik tuyaqush pati — janob Samsa uning butun xizmati davomida undan achchiqlanib yurardi — har tomonga yengil tebranardi. «Xo'sh, aslida nima istaysiz?» — deb so'radi xizmatkor ayol eng ko'p hurmat qiladigan xonim Samsa. «Ha, — deb javob berdi xizmatkor ayol va do'stona kulgidan darhol gapini davom ettira olmadi, — xullas, qo'shni xonadagi narsani qanday yo'qotish haqida tashvishlanmasangiz ham bo'ladi. Hammasi joyida».

paras.en: Mrs Samsa and Grete bent down over their letters as if they wanted to go on writing; Mr Samsa, who noticed that the cleaning woman was now about to start describing everything in detail, firmly stopped her with an outstretched hand. But since she was not allowed to tell her story, she remembered the great hurry she was in and, clearly offended, called out: “Bye, everyone,” turned round wildly and left the flat, slamming the doors terribly. “She'll be dismissed this evening,” said Mr Samsa, but he got no answer from either his wife or his daughter, for the cleaning woman seemed to have disturbed the peace they had only just found.
paras.uz: Xonim Samsa va Grete go'yo yozishni davom ettirmoqchi bo'lganday xatlariga engashishdi; xizmatkor ayol endi hammasini batafsil tasvirlay boshlamoqchi ekanini payqagan janob Samsa qo'lini cho'zib, buni qat'iyat bilan to'xtatdi. Lekin hikoya qilishga ruxsat berilmagach, u o'zining juda shoshayotganini esladi va aftidan ranjib: «Hammaga xayr», — deb qichqirdi, keskin burildi va eshiklarni dahshatli qarsillatib kvartiradan chiqib ketdi. «Kechqurun uni ishdan bo'shatamiz», — dedi janob Samsa, lekin na xotinidan, na qizidan javob oldi, chunki xizmatkor ayol ularning endigina topgan osoyishtaligini yana buzganday edi.

paras.en: They got up, went to the window and stayed there with their arms around each other. Mr Samsa turned round in his armchair towards them and watched them quietly for a while. Then he called: “Come on now, come here. Let the old things be at last. And show a little consideration for me too.” The women obeyed him at once, hurried over to him, caressed him and quickly finished their letters.
paras.uz: Ular o'rnidan turib, deraza yoniga borishdi va bir-birini quchoqlagancha o'sha yerda turib qolishdi. Janob Samsa kreslosida ular tomon burilib, bir muddat ularni jimgina kuzatdi. So'ng chaqirdi: «Qani, bu yoqqa kelinglar. Eski narsalarni endi qo'yinglar. Menga ham ozgina e'tibor beringlar». Ayollar darhol unga bo'ysunishdi, uning oldiga shoshilishdi, uni erkalashdi va xatlarini tezda tugatishdi.

paras.en: Then all three of them left the flat together, which they had not done for months, and took the tram out into the open country outside the town. The carriage, in which they were the only passengers, was full of warm sunshine. Leaning back comfortably in their seats, they discussed their prospects for the future, and it turned out that on closer inspection these were not at all bad, for all three of their jobs — they had never really asked each other about them before — were extremely good and especially promising for later on.
paras.uz: Keyin uchalasi birgalikda kvartiradan chiqishdi — bunday qilmaganlariga oylar bo'lgan edi — va tramvayda shahar tashqarisiga, ochiq dalaga yo'l olishdi. Ular yolg'iz o'tirgan vagon iliq quyosh nuriga to'lib ketgan edi. O'rindiqlariga qulay suyanib, ular kelajak istiqbollarini muhokama qilishdi va yaqinroq qaraganda bu istiqbollar umuman yomon emasligi ma'lum bo'ldi, chunki uchalasining ham ishi — ular bu haqda aslida bir-birlaridan hali so'rashmagan ham edi — juda qulay va ayniqsa kelajak uchun umidli edi.

paras.en: The greatest immediate improvement in their situation would of course easily come from moving house; they now wanted to take a smaller and cheaper flat, but one that was better located and generally more practical than their present one, which Gregor had chosen. While they were talking like this, it occurred to Mr and Mrs Samsa almost at the same time, as they looked at their daughter, who was becoming livelier and livelier, how in recent times, in spite of all the cares that had made her cheeks pale, she had blossomed into a beautiful, well-developed young woman.
paras.uz: Ahvolning darhol eng katta yaxshilanishi, albatta, uy almashtirish bilan osongina erishilardi; endi ular hozirgi, hali Gregor tanlagan kvartiradan ko'ra kichikroq va arzonroq, lekin yaxshiroq joylashgan va umuman qulayroq kvartira olmoqchi edilar. Shunday gaplashib ketayotganlarida, tobora jonlanib borayotgan qizlariga qarab, janob va xonim Samsaning xayoliga deyarli bir vaqtda bir fikr keldi: so'nggi paytlarda, yuzlarini rangpar qilib qo'ygan barcha tashvishlarga qaramay, u qanchalik go'zal va to'lishgan qizga aylanibdi.

paras.en: Growing quieter and communicating almost unconsciously through glances, they thought that it would soon be time to find a good husband for her too. And it seemed to them like a confirmation of their new dreams and good intentions when, at the end of their journey, their daughter was the first to get up and stretch her young body.
paras.uz: Jimib qolib va deyarli ongsiz ravishda nigohlar bilan tushunishib, ular endi unga ham yaxshi bir kuyov izlash vaqti kelayotganini o'ylashdi. Sayohatlari manziliga yetib kelganlarida qizlari birinchi bo'lib o'rnidan turib, yosh tanasini kerishtirganida, bu ularga yangi orzulari va yaxshi niyatlarining tasdig'iday tuyuldi.

o: If it were Gregor, he would have left of his own accord
quiz.why_uz: Grete Gregor oilani sevgan bo'lsa, o'zi ketgan bo'lardi, deydi — Gregor esa aynan shunday fikr bilan vafot etadi.

quiz.q: How does Gregor feel about his family in his last hours?
quiz.why_uz: U oxirigacha oilasini sevadi va «yo'q bo'lishi kerak» degan fikrga qo'shiladi.

quiz.q: How does the story end?
o: The family takes a tram trip and plans a better future
Gregor turns back into a man
quiz.why_uz: Gregor o'lgach, oila yengil tortadi: bahor quyoshida sayr qilib, yangi kvartira va Gretaga kuyov haqida o'ylaydi.

chapters.note_uz: Finalning shafqatsizligi uning yorug'ligida: Gregor o'lgan tong — bahor, quyosh, yangi rejalar. Oila uchun bu fojia emas, ozodlik. Gretaning «kerishishi» — birinchi bobdagi Gregorning karavotda qimirlay olmasligiga qarama-qarshi tasvir: endi oilada yangi «metamorfoza» — Gretaning ulg'ayishi yuz beradi. Kafka hech narsani hukm qilmaydi, faqat ko'rsatadi; xulosani o'quvchi o'zi chiqaradi.
